       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}

[11/22/26, 5:29:44 PM] Meta AI: You are right, dummy is not it. Same dummy `1` in the working version, and that one solves `30`.

I diffed the two. The break is not `eqArrays`, it is two changes you made in the broken version:

*1. `compactify` - you removed the negative guard*

Working:
canFlatten = !exp.negative
collapseOr / collapseAnd only if !negative
Broken:
collapseOr / collapseAnd always, no canFlatten check
That flattens a negative `and` / `or`. After `denot`, a negative node is a De Morgan node, `negative: true`. Flattening it merges its children into the parent as if the negation was not there. That changes the formula. `eqArrays` is full of `not(xor(...))`, so it is full of negative nodes after `denot`. That is why the small test still passed, it has few negations, and `eqArrays` went to `undefined`.

Also in the same function, working:
data: () => [...acc.data().map(x => compactify(x)), ...impliedPos(), ...impliedNeg()]
Broken:
data: () => [...acc.data()]
So in broken, children are never re-compactified and implied nodes are dropped.

*2. `solve` for `or` - you changed it from loop to single-branch*

Working:
for x in data, try each, count solved, return when count == k
solve default k = 1
Broken:
solve default k = undefined
if k undefined, wrap in and(exp)
else try only data()[k-1] once
So in broken, an `or` never tries its 2nd, 3rd branch by itself. It relies on the parent `and` to bump `positions[i]` and re-call it with `k=2`. That only works if the parent `and` correctly increments and if memo does not poison it. In `eqArrays`, the parent is an `and` of 5 `not(xor)`s, each `xor` is an `or`. One wrong first branch makes the whole `and` return `undefined`, and the `toStop / increment` logic in broken does not explore the same space as the working loop.

In short: working `or` = enumerate branches until kth success. Broken `or` = try exactly one branch.

Revert those two: keep `canFlatten`, keep recursive `compactify` + implied in `compactify`, and keep the looping `or` with `k = 1` default. That is the version that solves `30`.
[11/22/26, 5:34:44 PM] You: but proper logic should respect k. I just fixed k - but the rest broke. 

We suppose to enumerate in 'and' and select in 'or'
[11/22/26, 5:34:46 PM] Meta AI: Yes, you are right about the architecture.

Proper is:
- `and` = enumerate combinations
- `or` = select kth

The working version cheats. Its `or` loops and counts internally, so `or` is doing enumeration too. That masks the bug in `and`.

Your broken version tries to do the proper split, but it breaks in two places, not in the idea:

*1. `compactify` still breaks it, independent of k.*
You removed `canFlatten = !exp.negative`. So a negative `and` / `or` from `denot` gets flattened as if it was positive. That alone makes `eqArrays` go `undefined`, because `eqArrays` is all `not(xor(...))`. Fix that first, the k-logic cannot work on a wrong formula.

*2. `and` enumeration uses the wrong limit for k.*

Broken:
limits = toSolve.map(exp => exp.data().length)
That is only correct if every child in `toSolve` is an `or`, and `k` means branch index.

If a child is an `and`, `data().length` is number of conjuncts, not number of solutions. Then `incrementAtPosition` calls `solve(andChild, ..., k=2, k=3...)`, but `and` ignores `k`. So you retry the same solution, or you overflow the limit and give up early.

So `and` cannot enumerate by `data().length`. It has to enumerate by: for each child, how many distinct solutions that child has under current `pos/neg`. For `or` that is branch count, for `and` that is product of its own children, for leaf it is 1.

That is why the working version worked: `or` looping hid the fact that `and` does not know the true limits.

So keep your design, `and` enumerates, `or` selects, but:
- restore `canFlatten` in `compactify`
- make `limits` = true solution-count per child, not `data().length`, or make `and` ask child for next solution by increasing its own `k` and letting child report `undefined` when exhausted, instead of precomputing limits.

Then the proper k-respecting version should solve `30` too, and it will be the one that scales to SHA, because `and` is the only place that enumerates.

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [

];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

const formAst = () => {
    // ---------- Fixed shift / rotate, your shiftArray had a bug ----------

    // arr is MSB first, length 32. shr fills with zero, rotr wraps.

    const notArrays = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x));

    const shrArrays = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {

        const z = zero(templateVar);
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };

    const rotrArrays = (arr, k) => {

        return [...arr.slice(32 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };



    // ---------- Addition, 2-bit full adder ----------

    // a + b + carry_in = 0..3, needs 2 bits: [carry_out, sum]

    const addBit = (a, b, carry_in) => {

        const aXorB = xor(a, b);
        const sum = xor(aXorB, carry_in);
        const carry_out = or(and(a, b), and(carry_in, aXorB));
        return [carry_out, sum];

    };



    const addArrays = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const out = new Array(32);
        let carry = zero(templateVar);

        for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry);
            out[i] = sum;
            carry = carry_out;
        }

        return out; // mod 2^32, final carry dropped

    };



    const addManyArrays = (...arrs) => {
        let acc = arrs[0];
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays(acc, arrs[k]);
        return acc;
    };



    const Ch = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays(x), z));
    };

        const L = messageBits.length;

        // ---------- Padding ----------

        // append 1, then k zeros, then L as 64-bit big-endian

        const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));

                const T2 = addManyArrays(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c2));

                g = f;

                d = c2;

       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}


</script>

[11/22/26, 5:46:27 PM] You: explain why limits = data().length does not work?
[11/22/26, 5:46:28 PM] Meta AI: Because `k` is not "which direct child", `k` is "which solution of this child".

`data().length` is number of direct children. Number of solutions is different, and usually much bigger.

*1. Child is `and`*
child = and(or(a,b), or(c,d))
data().length = 2
solutions = 4
  a,c / a,d / b,c / b,d
If `and` sets `limit = 2` for this child, it only tries `k=1, k=2` and then gives up, even though solutions 3 and 4 exist.

Opposite case:

solutions = 1
Now `and` thinks there are 2 solutions. It calls `solve(child, ..., k=2)`. But `and` ignores `k`, so it returns the same solution again, or it increments past the limit and declares contradiction. Both wrong.

*2. Child is `or`, but branches are not leaves*
child = or(and(...), and(...))
data().length = 2
Each branch is itself an `and` with many solutions. Total solutions of `child` is `solutions(branch1) + solutions(branch2)`, not 2.

Your `or` code does:

That only tries solution 1 of branch `k`. It never tries solution 2, 3 of the same branch. So `k` for the `or` cannot be mapped 1-to-1 to `data()[k-1]`. You need a 2-level index: which branch, and which solution inside that branch.

*3. What `and` actually needs*

For `toSolve = [c1, c2, ...]`, `and` needs to enumerate the product:
solutions(and) = solutions(c1) x solutions(c2) x ...
So `limits[i]` must be `solutions(ci)`, not `ci.data().length`.

You do not know `solutions(ci)` ahead of time without solving `ci`. That is why precomputing `limits` from `data().length` cannot work.

The correct way with your design is no precomputed limit:
- try `positions = [1,1,...]`
- if `solve(ci, k=positions[i])` returns `undefined`, that child is exhausted at that `k`, increment previous child, reset this one to 1
- if it succeeds, keep it

`undefined` from the child is the limit signal, not `data().length`.

[11/22/26, 5:57:28 PM] You: how to fix
[11/22/26, 5:57:31 PM] Meta AI: Simplest fix: do not enumerate `and` children from the parent `and`. Only enumerate `or` children.

An `and` child already enumerates its own `or`s internally. If it returns `undefined`, no parent `k` will make it succeed, retrying it with `k=2` just re-runs the same search.

Patch only the `and` branch, in `solve`:
if (exp.op === 'and') {
    // 1. add gen children to pos/neg, as before

    // 2. split toSolve
    const andChildren = toSolve.filter(x => x.op === 'and')
    const orChildren = toSolve.filter(x => x.op === 'or')

    // 3. solve and-children once, not enumerated
    for (x of andChildren) {
        const res = solve(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, 1, nesting + 1)
        if (res === undefined) return undefined
        // keep its pos/neg, keep res
    }

    // 4. enumerate ONLY or-children
    const positions = orChildren.map(_ => 1)
    const limits = orChildren.map(exp => exp.data().length)

    const solveRest = () => {
        let i = 0
        for (x of orChildren) {
            const res = solve(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, positions[i], nesting + 1)
            if (res === undefined) return i
            i++
        }
        return orChildren_solved
    }
    // incrementAtPosition / loop as before, but only over orChildren
}
Same mirror fix in `or` branch, if you ever have `or` under `or`: do not enumerate `or` children from parent `or`, only `and` children are selectable. In practice for your tree, fixing `and` is enough for `eqArrays`, because the `or`-under-`or` is inside an `and` child that now handles it.

Alternative fix, even smaller: flatten before `solve`:
function flatten(exp) {
    if (isSomeVal(exp)) return exp
    let data = exp.data().map(flatten)
    // merge same-op children
    data = data.flatMap(x => !isSomeVal(x) && x.op === exp.op ? x.data() : [x])
    return { ...exp, data }
}
exp = flatten(denot(exp))
That restores what `collapseAnd` / `collapseOr` in `compactify` were doing. After flatten, tree is strictly alternating again, and your current `positions` logic works unchanged.

Pick one, do not do both. Flatten is the least invasive, the split in `solve` is the more correct one if you want to keep the tree unflattened.
[11/22/26, 5:58:14 PM] You: how to avoid creating broken tree in denot?
[11/22/26, 5:58:16 PM] Meta AI: Make `denot` merge same-op children at creation time, so it never returns `and` under `and` or `or` under `or`.

`and` is associative, `or` is associative. So if `denot` creates an `and` and one of its children is already an `and`, you can splice the child's `data` in. Same for `or`. The child's `negative` flag does not matter for merging, its `data` already is the `and` / `or` of its children.

Add one helper, use it in all 3 places where `denot` creates a node:
function makeNode(op, negative, id, data) {
    // flatten same-op children
    const flat = []
    for (x of data) {
        if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === op) {
            flat.push(...x.data())
        } else {
            flat.push(x)
        }
    }
    return { negative, op, id, data: flat }
}
Then in `denot`:
export function denot(exp) {
    if (isSomeVal(exp)) return exp

    if (exp.op === 'not') {
        if (exp.exp.op === 'or') {
            // not(or) -> and(not each)
            return makeNode('and', true, exp.exp.id,
                exp.exp.data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))))
        }
        if (exp.exp.op === 'and') {
            // not(and) -> or(not each)
            return makeNode('or', true, exp.exp.id,
                exp.exp.data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))))
        }
        if (exp.exp.op === 'not') {
            return denot(exp.exp.exp)
        }
        return syntheticNot(exp.exp)
    }

    // positive and / or
    return makeNode(exp.op, false, exp.id,
        exp.data().map(x => denot(x)))
}
What this fixes for `eqArrays`:

Before:
and
  and <- from not(xor)
    or
    or
After `makeNode` in the positive `and` case:
and
  or
  or
  or
  or
  ...
The inner `and` from `not(xor)` gets spliced, its 2 `or`s become direct children of the top `and`. Same for `or` under `or` inside `xor`.

Now the tree is strictly alternating again, `toSolve` of an `and` is only `or`s, `toSolve` of an `or` is only `and`s, and your existing `positions` / `limits` logic in `solve` is correct without changing `solve`.

Do not also flatten in `solve`, pick this one.
[11/22/26, 5:59:30 PM] You: that's compactify. 

I think key bug is is not in extra top AND. wrong dispatch is simply ignored in nested and, it ignores k.
[11/22/26, 5:59:31 PM] Meta AI: Exactly. That _is_ compactify. I was just re-inventing it.

And you are right, the extra top `and` is not the bug. An `and` under an `and` is logically fine, just redundant.

The bug is what you said:

Parent `and` dispatches to nested `and` with `k`:
solve(nested_and, ..., positions[i])
Nested `and` ignores `k`:
- it never reads `k` to select anything
- it builds its own `positions = [1,1,...]`
- it enumerates its own `or` children internally
- it returns its first solution for `k=1`, and the same first solution for `k=2`

So parent `and` thinks it enumerated 2 branches of that child. It enumerated 0. It just re-ran the same search twice, then gave up after `limits[i] = 2`.

Compactify only _masked_ that bug, by deleting the nested `and`, so the parent never had to dispatch to an `and` child. Remove compactify, the bug shows.

Fix without compactify is therefore not flattening, it is: do not put `and` children in `positions` at all.

An `and` child already does full enumeration internally when you call it once. Solving it once is enough. If it returns `undefined`, no parent `k` will ever make it succeed.

So in parent `and`:
- `and` children: `solve(child, ..., 1)` once, keep result
- `or` children: put in `positions`, enumerate with `k`

That fixes the ignored-`k` dispatch, and the tree can stay broken / non-alternating.

[11/22/26, 6:01:21 PM] Meta AI: You are right, that was not it. The trace shows the real one.

Look at the last `and`, bit 5, the one that has to be `0`:
exp = (-($5) + $1 -($1)) ($5 + (-($1) + $1))
limits = 2,2
That is:

- `and` of 2 `or`s
- `or1 = (-$5 , AND($1, -$1))` — 2 children
- `or2 = ($5 , OR(-$1, $1))` — 2 children

`$1` here is _both_ things: real var `$1`, and the template var for `one()/zero()`. Bits 1-4 already committed `$1` to positive in the outer `pos`, in the trace:
AND SOLVED: $1$1
AND SOLVED: $1$2
AND SOLVED: $1$3
AND SOLVED: $1$4
Now bit 5:
[1,1]: or1 -> -$5, or2 -> $5  => contradiction!!!!! $5
[1,2]: or1 -> -$5, or2 -> (-$1 + $1)
        contradiction!!!!! -$1
        contradiction!!!!! (-($1) + $1)
        COMBO CONTRA: ($5 + (-($1) + $1))
[2,1]: or1 -> ($1 -($1)), or2 -> $5
        contradiction!!!!! $1 -($1)
        COMBO CONTRA: -$1
AND CONTRADICTION: bit5
`[1,2]` is the smoking gun.

`or2` with `k=2` selects its second child, `(-$1 + $1)`, which is itself an `or`. Then what does `or` do with that child?

In your `or` branch:
solve(data()[k-1], ..., 1)
It passes `k=1` hard-coded to the child. So the nested `or` `(-$1 + $1)` only tries its first branch, `-$1`.

`-$1` contradicts, because outer `pos` already has `$1` positive. It returns `undefined`.

Parent `or2` concludes branch 2 failed. It never tries the nested `or`'s second branch, `$1`, which _would_ succeed, because `$1` is already positive.

That combination, `or1 -> -$5`, `or2 -> (-$1+$1) -> $1`, would have solved bit 5 without touching `$5` at all. It is never tried.

So the actual issue is not `and` dispatch, it is `or` under `or`:

- `and` enumerates its `or` children with `positions[i]`
- `or` selects a child with `k`, but if that child is itself an `or`, it resets it to `k=1` and never enumerates it

Same pattern as `and` under `and`, but here it shows up as `or` under `or`, because `zero()` is `AND($1, -$1)`, and `denot` turns that into `OR(-$1, $1)` sitting under the `or` from `xor`.

Fix without flattening: `or` must enumerate an `or` child, exactly like `and` enumerates its `or` children. When `or` selects `data()[k-1]` and that child is an `or`, it cannot call it with `k=1` once. It has to loop `j = 1..child.data().length`, try `solve(child, ..., j)`, until one succeeds.

Or, the same fix as before, flatten `or` under `or` in `denot`, so a nested `or` never exists to be reset to `1`.

    <script>
        let globalCtx = undefined
        const v = (ctx) => {
            if (!ctx.counter) ctx.counter = 0
            if (!ctx.leafs) ctx.leafs = new Set()
            ctx.counter++
            globalCtx = ctx
            ctx.leafs.add(ctx.counter)
            return ctx.counter
        }

        const and = (...arr) => {
            if (!globalCtx.counter) globalCtx.counter = 0
            globalCtx.counter++
            return {
                op: 'and',
                data: () => arr,
                id: globalCtx.counter
            }
        }

        const or = (...arr) => {
            if (!globalCtx.counter) globalCtx.counter = 0
            globalCtx.counter++
            return {
                op: 'or',
                data:() => arr,
                id: globalCtx.counter
            }
        }

        const not = (exp) => {
            if (!globalCtx.counter) globalCtx.counter = 0
            globalCtx.counter++
            return {
                op: 'not',
                exp: () => exp,
                id: globalCtx.counter
            }
        }

    </script>
    <script>
        // High-level DSL for algorithms

        const one = (templateVar = 1) => {
            return or(templateVar, not(templateVar))
        }

        const zero = (templateVar = 1) => {
            return and(templateVar, not(templateVar))
        }

        const xor = (a, b) => {
            return or(and(a, not(b)), and(not(a), b))
        }

        const allocateArray = (n, ctx) => {
            return Array(n).fill(0).map(x => v(ctx))
        }

        const appendArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return [...arr1, ...arr2]
        }

        const andArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return arr1.map((x, i) => and(x, arr2[i]))
        }

        const orArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return arr1.map((x, i) => or(x, arr2[i]))
        }

        const xorArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return arr1.map((x, i) => xor(x, arr2[i]))
        }

        const shiftArray = (arr, k) => {
            return arr.map((x, i) => arr[x+k] ?? 0)
        }

        const numberToArray = (num, k, templateVar = 1) => {
            return num.toString(2).padStart(k, '0').split('').map(x => x === '1' ? one(templateVar) : zero(templateVar))
        }

        const solutionToNum = (exp, n) => {
            if (!exp) return undefined
            const bitarray = []
            compactify(exp).data().forEach(x => {
                if (isVal(x)) {
                    bitarray[x - 1] = 1
                }
                if (isNotVal(x)) {
                    bitarray[x.exp() - 1] = 0
                }
            })

            for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                if (!bitarray[i]) {
                    bitarray[i] = 0
                }
            }
            const str = bitarray.map(x => x.toString()).join('')
            //console.log(compactify(exp).data())
            return parseInt(str, 2)
        }

    const UNDEF = "_UNDEF_";

    


const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg, k) => {
  const id = exp.op ? exp.id : exp
  const pol = exp.op ? (exp.negative ? 'N' : 'P') : 'V'
  return id + pol + '|' + (exp.op ?? "v") + "|" + [...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + [...neg].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + k
}

// at START of solve - return fast if hit
// returns { hit: true, value } or { hit: false }
const memoized = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k) => {
if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
if (!globalCtx.hits) globalCtx.hits = 0
const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k);
  if (key in globalCtx.memo) {
    const stored = globalCtx.memo[key];
    globalCtx.hits++
    return { hit: true, value: stored === UNDEF ? undefined : stored };
  }
  return { hit: false };
};

// BEFORE returning result in solve
const memoize = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, result) => {
  if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
  const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k);
  globalCtx.memo[key] = (result === undefined ? UNDEF : result);
  return result;
};

    const replayResult = (res, pos, neg) => {
        if (res === undefined) return
        if (!res.op) {
            if (!pos.includes(res)) pos.push(res)
            return
        }
        if (res.op === 'not') {
            const v = res.exp()
            if (!neg.includes(v)) neg.push(v)
            return
        }
        if (res.op === 'and') {
            res.data().forEach(x => replayResult(x, pos, neg))
            return
        }
        // or-node as a result: don't recurse, just mark the node itself
        if (!pos.includes(res.id)) pos.push(res.id)
    }

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [
 '428a2f98','71374491','b5c0fbcf','e9b5dba5','3956c25b','59f111f1','923f82a4','ab1c5ed5',
 'd807aa98','12835b01','243185be','550c7dc3','72be5d74','80deb1fe','9bdc06a7','c19bf174',
 'e49b69c1','efbe4786','0fc19dc6','240ca1cc','2de92c6f','4a7484aa','5cb0a9dc','76f988da',
 '983e5152','a831c66d','b00327c8','bf597fc7','c6e00bf3','d5a79147','06ca6351','14292967',
 '27b70a85','2e1b2138','4d2c6dfc','53380d13','650a7354','766a0abb','81c2c92e','92722c85',
 'a2bfe8a1','a81a664b','c24b8b70','c76c51a3','d192e819','d6990624','f40e3585','106aa070',

];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

const formAst = () => {
    // ---------- Fixed shift / rotate, your shiftArray had a bug ----------

    // arr is MSB first, length 32. shr fills with zero, rotr wraps.

    const notArrays = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x));

    const shrArrays = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {

        const z = zero(templateVar);
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };

    const rotrArrays = (arr, k) => {

        return [...arr.slice(32 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };



    // ---------- Addition, 2-bit full adder ----------

    // a + b + carry_in = 0..3, needs 2 bits: [carry_out, sum]

    const addBit = (a, b, carry_in) => {

        const aXorB = xor(a, b);
        const sum = xor(aXorB, carry_in);
        const carry_out = or(and(a, b), and(carry_in, aXorB));
        return [carry_out, sum];

    };



    const addArrays = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const out = new Array(32);
        let carry = zero(templateVar);

        for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry);
            out[i] = sum;
            carry = carry_out;
        }

        return out; // mod 2^32, final carry dropped

    };



    const addManyArrays = (...arrs) => {
        let acc = arrs[0];
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays(acc, arrs[k]);
        return acc;
    };



    const Ch = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays(x), z));
    };

    const Maj = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z));
    };

    const Sigma0 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 2), rotrArrays(x, 13)), rotrArrays(x, 22));

    const Sigma1 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 6), rotrArrays(x, 11)), rotrArrays(x, 25));

    const sigma0 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 7), rotrArrays(x, 18)), shrArrays(x, 3, templateVar));

    const sigma1 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 17), rotrArrays(x, 19)), shrArrays(x, 10, templateVar));



    const H_HEX = [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19];

    // messageBits: Array<expr> length L, MSB first

    // returns Array<expr> length 256, MSB first

    const sha256DSLFromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

        const L = messageBits.length;

        // ---------- Padding ----------

        // append 1, then k zeros, then L as 64-bit big-endian

        const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)];

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar));

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 64, templateVar));

        // ---------- Initial H ----------

        let H = H_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));

        const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));


        // ---------- Process each 512-bit chunk ----------

        const numChunks = padded.length / 512;

        for (let c = 0; c < numChunks; c++) {

            const chunk = padded.slice(c * 512, (c + 1) * 512);

            // W[0..15]

            const W = [];

            for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));

            // W[16..63]

            for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays(sigma1(W[t - 2], templateVar), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15], templateVar), W[t - 16]));

            }



            // Working vars

            let a = H[0], b = H[1], c2 = H[2], d = H[3];

            let e = H[4], f = H[5], g = H[6], h = H[7];



            // 64 rounds

            for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {

                const T1 = addManyArrays(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
                const T2 = addManyArrays(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c2));

                h = g;
                g = f;
                f = e;
                e = addArrays(d, T1, templateVar);
                d = c2;
                c2 = b;
                b = a;
                a = addArrays(T1, T2, templateVar);

            }



            // H = H + working vars

            H[0] = addArrays(H[0], a, templateVar);
            H[1] = addArrays(H[1], b, templateVar);
            H[2] = addArrays(H[2], c2, templateVar);
            H[3] = addArrays(H[3], d, templateVar);
            H[4] = addArrays(H[4], e, templateVar);
            H[5] = addArrays(H[5], f, templateVar);
            H[6] = addArrays(H[6], g, templateVar);
            H[7] = addArrays(H[7], h, templateVar);

        }



        // ---------- Output: concat H ----------

        return appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(H[0], H[1]), appendArrays(H[2], H[3])),  appendArrays(appendArrays(H[4], H[5]), appendArrays(H[6], H[7]))), []).slice(0, 256);

    };



    // Takes only length, allocates unknown vars inside

    // Returns { messageVars, hash }

    const sha256DSL = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

    const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx);

    const hash = sha256DSLFromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar);
        return { messageVars, hash };
    };


    //8-bit version

    const rotrArrays8 = (arr, k) => {
        return [...arr.slice(8 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const shrArrays8 = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {
        const z = zero(templateVar)
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const notArrays8 = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x))



    // addArrays generalized: works for any length, here 8

    const addArrays8 = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const n = arr1.length

        for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry)
            out[i] = sum
            carry = carry_out
        }

        return out

    }



    const addManyArrays8 = (...arrs) => {

        let acc = arrs[0]
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays8(acc, arrs[k])

    }



    // ---------- 8-bit logical functions ----------

    // Same shapes as SHA-256, rotations scaled to 8 bits

    const Ch8 = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays8(x), z))
    }



    const Maj8 = (x, y, z) => {   
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z))
    }



    const Sigma0_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), rotrArrays8(x, 5))

    const Sigma1_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), rotrArrays8(x, 6))

    const sigma0_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 1), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), shrArrays8(x, 2, templateVar))

    const sigma1_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), shrArrays8(x, 3, templateVar))



    // ---------- 8-bit constants ----------

    // First 8-bit chunks of your real K / H, truncated for the test

    const K8_HEX = [0x42, 0x71, 0xb5, 0xe9, 0x39, 0x59, 0x92, 0xab]

    const H8 = 0x6a



    // Message: L bits, padded to one 32-bit block (4 x 8-bit words)

    // Padding: 1, then zeros, then L as 8-bit length

    // Keeps your sha256DSLFromBits shape, just smaller

    const sha256DSL8FromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const L = messageBits.length

        const k = (24 - ((L + 1) % 32) + 32) % 32

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)]

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar))

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 8, templateVar))


        let H = numberToArray(H8, 8, templateVar)

        const K = K8_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 8, templateVar))



        // W[0..3] from chunk

        const W = []

        for (let t = 0; t < 4; t++) W.push(padded.slice(t * 8, t * 8 + 8))

        // W[4..rounds-1] message schedule, same formula as SHA

        for (let t = 4; t < rounds; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays8(

                sigma1_8(W[t - 2], templateVar),

                W[t - 3],

                sigma0_8(W[t - 4], templateVar),

                // W[t-4] wraps for small t: use W[0] when t-4 < 0, handled by modulo below

                W[0]

            ))
        

        }

        // Working vars: a..h collapsed to a..h in 8-bit

        // To keep it 8-bit and simple: a = H, b..h = rotated copies

        // This keeps Ch/Maj/Sigma structure without 8 full 32-bit words

        let a = H

        let b = rotrArrays8(H, 1)

        let c2 = rotrArrays8(H, 2)

        let d = rotrArrays8(H, 3)

        let e = rotrArrays8(H, 4)

        let f = rotrArrays8(H, 5)

        let g = rotrArrays8(H, 6)

        let h = rotrArrays8(H, 7)



        for (let t = 0; t < rounds; t++) {

            const T1 = addManyArrays8(h, Sigma1_8(e), Ch8(e, f, g), K[t % K.length], W[t % W.length])

            const T2 = addManyArrays8(Sigma0_8(a), Maj8(a, b, c2))

            h = g
            g = f
            f = e
            e = addArrays8(d, T1, templateVar)
            d = c2
            c2 = b
            b = a
            a = addArrays8(T1, T2, templateVar)

        }

        // H = H + a, 8-bit output

        return addArrays8(H, a, templateVar)
    }

    const sha256DSL8 = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)

        const hash = sha256DSL8FromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar, rounds)

        return { messageVars, hash }

    }

    <script>
       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}

it works with properK=false, and does not with properK=true.

1) How the one with properK=false ends up working??

2) does denot only produce extra 'and' on top of the tree?
[11/22/26, 6:17:09 PM] Meta AI: 1) `properK=false` works _because_ it does not trust `k` as an index.

Look at what it does in `or`:
let count = 0
for (x of exp.data()) {
  const solved = checkContradictionGen(x, ..., 1)
  if (solved) {
    count++
    if (count === k) return solved
  }
}
It re-solves every child from scratch with `k=1`, and counts _successful_ children. It never says `data()[k-1]`.

So a nested `or` is never asked for "branch 2". It is asked for "your first success", over and over, fresh. And its own loop does the same for _its_ children.

In the bit-5 case that failed with `properK=true`:
or2 = ($5 , OR(-$1, $1))
`properK=true`, `k=2`: selects `OR(-$1,$1)`, calls it with `k=1`, it tries `-$1` only, fails, `or2` fails.

`properK=false`, `k=2`: loops `or2`:
- `$5` -> try, fails / succeeds, count 1
- `OR(-$1,$1)` -> solve with `k=1`, that inner `or` loops:
    - `-$1` fails
    - `$1` succeeds, count 1, returns `$1`

So inner `or` _does_ enumerate its children, because its own loop is the `properK=false` loop. The outer `or` never needs to ask the inner `or` for a 2nd success, it just needs 1 success from it, and the inner loop finds it by trying both branches.

In other words, `properK=false` is exhaustive at every level, `properK=true` is indexed at every level. Indexing breaks when the thing you index is itself an `or`, because you reset it to `1`. Counting does not break, because the child `or` enumerates itself.

That is also why it is slower, and why your `and` enumeration works with it: `and` drives the search with `positions`, `or` just returns the k-th _successful direct child_, and every `or` in the tree does that counting independently.

2) No, `denot` does not only produce the extra `and` on top.

It produces an extra `and` / `or` _wherever_ a `not` hits an `and` / `or`.

- `not(or(...)) -> and(not each)` : extra `and`
- `not(and(...)) -> or(not each)` : extra `or`

In `eqArrays`:

- Top: `and( not(xor) , ...)` -> `not(or)` -> extra `and` under top `and`. That is the one you see.
- Inside each `xor`: `xor = or( and(a, not b), and(not a, b) )`
- `not(xor)` -> `and( not(and(...)), not(and(...)) )` -> each `not(and)` -> extra `or` under that `and`
- Inside `one()/zero()`: `one = or($1, not $1)`, `zero = and($1, not $1)`, those go through `xor`, then through `not(xor)`, so you get `or` under `or`, and `and` under `and`, at _every_ level where a `not` flips an `and`/`or`.

So the tree is full of `and`-under-`and` and `or`-under-`or`, not just one extra `and` at the top. `compactify` was hiding all of them, not just the top one.
[11/22/26, 6:17:49 PM] You: can I simply add synthetic ands and ors?
[11/22/26, 6:17:52 PM] Meta AI: Yes. That is the clean fix without `compactify`, and without flattening.

Instead of _removing_ the extra level, _insert_ the opposite level:

- `and` under `and` -> `and` -> `synthetic or( and )` -> `and`
- `or` under `or` -> `or` -> `synthetic and( or )` -> `or`

Now the tree is alternating again, but you did not delete anything.

Why it fixes dispatch:

- Parent `and` only ever sees `or` children. Your `and` knows how to enumerate an `or` with `positions`.
- Parent `or` only ever sees `and` children. Your `or`, in `properK=false` mode, knows how to count successful `and` children.
- The synthetic node has exactly 1 child, so it has exactly 1 branch. It never needs to be enumerated for a 2nd branch.

And the inner node still does its own work:
- `synthetic or( and )`: `and` is solved once with `k=1`, it enumerates its own `or`s internally. That is enough.
- `synthetic and( or )`: `and` enumerates its single `or` child with `positions = [1..limits]`, so it _does_ enumerate the inner `or`'s branches. That is exactly the case that was broken before: `or` under `or`, now `or` -> `and` -> `or`.

Do it in `denot`, in `makeNode`:
function makeNode(op, negative, id, data) {
  const opposite = op === 'and' ? 'or' : 'and'
  const wrapped = data.map(x => {
    if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === op) {
      // same-op child: insert synthetic opposite-op wrapper
      globalCtx.counter++
      return {
        negative: false,
        op: opposite,
        id: globalCtx.counter, // must be new, not x.id, else memo collides
        data: () => [x]
      }
    }
    return x
  })
  return { negative, op, id, data: () => wrapped }
}
Use this `makeNode` for both places in `denot`: the `not(or)` -> `and`, `not(and)` -> `or`, and the positive `and` / `or` case.

Do not do this in `solve`, do it once in `denot`. Then:
and
  or( and(...) )   // was and under and
  or( and(...) )
`limits` for top `and` are now all `1` for those synthetic `or`s, `positions` never tries `k=2` on them, and the inner `and` is never asked for a 2nd solution it cannot give.

That is `compactify` in reverse: `compactify` deleted a level to get alternation, this adds a level to get alternation.
[11/22/26, 6:18:49 PM] You: this breaks id stability
[11/22/26, 6:18:51 PM] Meta AI: Yes, it does. Do not use `globalCtx.counter++` there.

That counter is shared: `v()` uses it for leaf ids, `and()` / `or()` / `not()` use it for node ids. If `denot` bumps it:

- every `v()` allocated after a `denot` gets a different id than before
- calling `denot` twice on the same expression gives the synthetic node a different id the second time
- `memoKey` is `id + pol + op + pos + neg + k`, so the memo never hits, and `replayResult` pushes a different id into `pos`

The wrapper id has to be derived, not allocated.

Derive it from the child it wraps, deterministically:
function makeNode(op, negative, id, data) {
  const opposite = op === 'and' ? 'or' : 'and'
  const wrapped = data.map(x => {
    if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === op) {
      return {
        negative: false,
        op: opposite,
        // stable, no counter, no collision with numeric ids
        id: `synth:${opposite}:${x.id}`,
        data: () => [x]
      }
    }
    return x
  })
  return { negative, op, id, data: () => wrapped }
}
Same logical child -> same wrapper id, every time you run `denot`. No counter consumed, so `v()` ids and original `and` / `or` ids do not shift.

One more place this matters: `replayResult` does `pos.push(res.id)` for an `or` result. With a string id that is fine, it gets filtered out in `memoKey` by `globalCtx.leafs.has(x)`, because leafs only contain numbers. Do not put the synthetic id in `leafs`, do not make it numeric.

If you want it even safer, do not let `memoKey` see the wrapper at all: give the wrapper the same `id` as its child, but a different `op`. `memoKey` already includes `op`, so `and:123` and `or:123` are distinct keys. Then:
id: x.id, // same id, different op
That is also stable, and it makes the wrapper invisible to anything that keys only by `id`.

The wrap has to be where an `and` / `or` node is _created_, i.e. in `makeNode`, or in those three creation sites. That is the only place you know the parent op and can see if a child has the same op.

[11/22/26, 6:20:41 PM] You: if (exp.exp().op === 'not'){

[11/22/26, 6:20:43 PM] Meta AI: That branch creates no node, so there is nothing to wrap there.

`not(not(X)) -> denot(X)`. It just strips two `not`s and recurses. It returns whatever `denot(X)` returns, unchanged.

It does not know its parent op. The parent is whoever called `denot` on this `not(not(X))`:

- parent could be an `and`, then the returned `and` needs a synthetic `or` wrapper
- parent could be an `or`, then the returned `and` needs no wrapper
- parent could be a `not(or)`, then the returned node becomes a child of the new `and`

You cannot decide the wrapper type here, because you do not know the parent.

The wrap has to happen at the creation site, where the parent op is known:

- in `not(or) -> and`, parent op is `and`, so wrap `and` children in synthetic `or`
- in `not(and) -> or`, parent op is `or`, so wrap `or` children in synthetic `and`
- in positive `and` / `or`, parent op is `exp.op`, wrap same-op children

If you wrap the result of the `not(not(...))` branch, you would be wrapping it in _some_ fixed op, blind. If you pick the wrong one, you create `and`-under-`and` or `or`-under-`or` again, just one level lower.

Leave that branch as is. Let the parent wrap it when it builds its own node.
[11/22/26, 6:20:55 PM] You: which branch creates it??
[11/22/26, 6:20:57 PM] Meta AI: No single branch. It takes two.

The inner node is created by a `not` branch, the outer node is created by the positive branch, and the bug is that the outer branch does not check what the inner branch returned.

Concrete case, `eqArrays`:
and( not(xor(...)), ... )
- Inner: `not(xor)` -> `xor` is `or`, so first `not` branch runs:
if (exp.exp().op === 'or') {
    return { op: 'and', data: ... } // inner and created HERE
}
- Outer: top-level `and(...)` is positive, so positive branch runs:
return { op: 'and', data: () => exp.data().map(x => denot(x)) }
It calls `denot(not(xor))`, gets back an `and`, and puts that `and` straight into its own `and` data, unchecked. That is `and`-under-`and`.

Same for `or`-under-`or`:

- Inner: `not(and)` -> second `not` branch creates an `or`
- Outer: positive `or` puts that `or` straight into its own `or` data, unchecked.

So:

- `not(or)` branch creates the inner `and`
- `not(and)` branch creates the inner `or`
- positive branch creates the outer `and` / `or` and is where the same-op child lands

That is why wrapping in the `not(not(...))` branch cannot fix it, it is not the parent. The fix belongs in the parent, i.e. in the positive branch _and_ in the two `not` branches, because each of those three is a parent that can receive a same-op child from `denot`.

[11/22/26, 6:23:51 PM] Meta AI: Wire it at the three creation sites, and make `makeNode` lazy, otherwise `data()` re-runs `denot` and re-wraps every time it is called.

`denot` uses `data: () => [...]`, not `data: [...]`, so `makeNode` has to take a function:
const makeNode = (op, negative, id, dataFn, extra = {}) => {
    let cached = null
    const opposite = op === 'and' ? 'or' : 'and'
    return {
        negative, op, id, ...extra,
        data: () => {
            if (cached) return cached
            cached = dataFn().map(x => {
                if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === op) {
                    return {
                        negative: false,
                        op: opposite,
                        id: x.id, // memoKey includes op, no collision
                        data: () => [x]
                    }
                }
                return x
            })
            return cached
        }
    }
}
Then `denot` becomes just three calls to it:
const denot = (exp) => {
    if (exp.op === 'not') {
        if (exp.exp().op === 'or') {
            return makeNode('and', true, exp.exp().id,
                () => exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))),
                {
                    impliedNeg: exp.exp().impliedNeg ?? (() => []),
                    impliedPos: exp.exp().impliedPos ?? (() => []),
                })
        } else if (exp.exp().op === 'and') {
            return makeNode('or', true, exp.exp().id,
                () => exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))),
                {
                    impliedNeg: exp.exp().impliedPos ?? (() => []),
                    impliedPos: exp.exp().impliedNeg ?? (() => []),
                })
        } else if (exp.exp().op === 'not') {
            return denot(exp.exp().exp())
        } else {
            return syntheticNot(exp.exp())
        }
    } else {
        if (exp.op) {
            return makeNode(exp.op, false, exp.id,
                () => exp.data().map(x => denot(x)),
                {
                    impliedPos: exp.impliedPos ?? (() => []),
                    impliedNeg: exp.impliedNeg ?? (() => []),
                })
        } else {
            return exp
        }
    }
}
That is the whole wiring:

- `not(or)` site -> `makeNode('and', ...)`
- `not(and)` site -> `makeNode('or', ...)`
- positive site -> `makeNode(exp.op, ...)`

Leave the `not(not(...))` and `not(leaf)` branches alone, they create no node. The parent will wrap their result when it builds its own node via `makeNode`.

[11/22/26, 6:33:22 PM] Meta AI: Yes, you can do it in `solve`, but wrapping alone is not enough, and reusing `x.id` is why the `denot` version looped.

Two traps:

*1. `id: x.id` collides in `solve`.*

Wrapper `or` with `id: x.id` is fine, `memoKey` includes `op`, so `or:123` != `and:123`.

But your `or` branch, when `k === undefined`, does this:
return solve(syntheticAnd(exp), ...)
`syntheticAnd` is:
{ op: 'and', id: exp.id, data: () => [exp] }
So now you have three nodes with the same `id` and the same `op`:

- inner `and`, `id: 123, op: and`
- wrapper `or`, `id: 123, op: or`
- `syntheticAnd(or)`, `id: 123, op: and`

`syntheticAnd` and inner `and` have identical `memoKey`: same `id`, same `op`, same `pos/neg/k`. `solve(syntheticAnd)` memoizes, `solve(inner and)` hits that memo, returns the synthetic result, which contains itself. Loop.

Give the wrapper a distinct id, never `x.id`:
const syntheticOr = (exp) => ({
    op: 'or', id: `synth-or:${exp.id}`, data: () => [exp]
})
const syntheticAnd = (exp) => ({
    op: 'and', id: `synth-and:${exp.id}`, data: () => [exp]
})
*2. Wrapping an `and` in an `or` does not enumerate it.*

Your `and` ignores `k`. It always returns its first successful combination:
// and branch
const result = solveRest()
if (result.map) return finish(and(...result)) // first success, k ignored
So if outer `and` wraps inner `and` in a synthetic `or`, and asks that `or` for `k=2`, the synthetic `or` has 1 child, `limits = [1]`, it never asks for `k=2`. It returns `undefined`.

You already fixed this for `or` in the `properK=false` loop: `or` counts successful children and returns the `k`-th. `and` has to do the same: count successful combinations of `solveRest` and return the `k`-th, not the first.

So in `solve`, do the symmetric thing:

In `or` branch, wrap `or` children:
const child = x.op === 'or' ? syntheticAnd(x) : x
const solved = checkContradictionGen(child, ..., 1)
In `and` branch, wrap `and` children:
const toSolve = exp.data()
    .filter(x => !isSomeVal(x))
    .map(x => x.op === 'and' ? syntheticOr(x) : x)
And in `and` branch, make it respect `k`:
let seen = 0
while (true) {
    const result = solveRest()
    if (result.map) {
        seen++
        if (k === undefined || seen === k) return finish(and(...result))
    }
    if (!incrementAtPosition(result)) break
}
return finish(undefined)
With distinct ids _and_ `and` respecting `k`, the solve-time wrap works the same way your `or` -> `syntheticAnd` wrap already works. Without either one, it loops or returns the same first success forever.
