            }
            return exp
        }

        const isVal = exp => !exp.op
        
        const isNotVal = exp => {
            if (exp.op === 'not') {
                if (exp.exp().op) throw "needs denot"
                return true
            }
            return false
        }
        const isSomeVal = exp => isVal(exp) || isNotVal(exp)

        const getid = exp => isSomeVal(exp) ? (isVal(exp) ? exp : exp.exp()) : exp.id
        
        const isGenVal = exp => isVal(exp) || (!isSomeVal(exp) && !exp.negative)
        
        const isGenNotVal = exp => isNotVal(exp) || (!isSomeVal(exp) && exp.negative)

        const addPos = (arr, exp) => {
            const id = getid(exp)
            if (arr.includes(id)) return false
             arr.push(id)
            return true
        }

        const addNeg = (arr, exp) => {
            const id = getid(exp)
            if (arr.includes(id)) return false
            arr.push(id)
            return true
        }

        const contradicts = (exp, pos, neg) => (isGenNotVal(exp) && pos.includes(getid(exp))) || (isGenVal(exp) && neg.includes(getid(exp)))

        const checkContradictionGen = (exp, pos, neg, nesting) => {
          if (contradicts(exp, pos, neg)) return undefined
          return solve(exp, pos, neg, 1, nesting + 1)
        }

        const checkContradiction = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, nesting) => {
            if (!(isSomeVal(exp))) {
                return solve(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, 1, nesting + 1)
            } else {
   
                if (isNotVal(exp) && outerAndPositive.find(x => getid(exp) === x)) {
                    return undefined
                }

                if (isVal(exp) && outerAndNegative.find(x => getid(exp) === x)) {
                    return undefined
                }

                return solve(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, undefined, nesting + 1)
            }
        }


        const limit = 500000

        const solve = (exp, outerAndPositive = [], outerAndNegative = [], k = undefined, nesting = 0) => {
            if (!globalCtx.ticks) globalCtx.ticks = 0
            globalCtx.ticks++

            if (globalCtx.ticks > limit) {
                console.log("\n\n\nk = " + k)
                console.log("outer negatives = " + outerAndNegative)
                console.log("outer positives = " + outerAndPositive)

                console.log(globalCtx.memo)
                
                throw "too many contradictions, over " + limit + ", nesting = " + nesting + ", memo length = " + Object.keys(globalCtx.memo).length + " hits = " + globalCtx.hits
            }
            
            const snapPos = [...outerAndPositive]
            const snapNeg = [...outerAndNegative]
            const mm = memoized(exp, snapPos, snapNeg, k)

            if (mm.hit) {
                if (mm.value !== undefined) {
                    if (exp.op && !outerAndPositive.includes(exp.id)) outerAndPositive.push(exp.id)
                    replayResult(mm.value, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)
                }
                return mm.value
            }
            
            const finish = (r) => {
                memoize(exp, snapPos, snapNeg, k, r)
                return r
            }
    
            if (!exp.op) { 
                if (outerAndNegative.some(x => x === exp)) return finish(undefined)
                outerAndPositive.push(exp)
                return finish(exp)
            }

            if (exp.op === 'not') {
                if (exp.exp().op) throw "needs denot!"
                if (outerAndPositive.some(x => x === exp.exp())) return finish(undefined)
                outerAndNegative.push(exp.exp())
                return finish(exp)
            }

 
            if (contradicts(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)

            if (exp.op === 'and') {

                const extra = exp.data().filter(x => isSomeVal(x))
                //console.log(exp)
                const toSolve = exp.data().filter(x => !isSomeVal(x)).map(x => x.op === 'and' ? syntheticOr(x) : x)

                for (x of exp.data()){
                  if (contradicts(x, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)
                  if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(outerAndPositive, x)
                  else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(outerAndNegative, x)
                }

                const positions = toSolve.map(_ => 1)

                const limits = toSolve.map(exp => exp.data().length)

                //console.log("limits = " + limits + " exp = " + show(exp))

                const solveRest = () => {

                    //console.log(positions)
                    const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
                    const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

                    let result = []
                    let i = 0
                    for (x of toSolve) {
                        
                        const res = solve(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, positions[i], nesting + 1)

                        if (res) {  

                            const negativeSet = new Set(tryOuterAndNegative)
                            const positiveSet = new Set(tryOuterAndPositive)
                            
                            if (res.filter) {

                                for (x of res) {
                                    if (contradicts(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative)) return i
                                    if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(tryOuterAndPositive, x) 
                                    else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(tryOuterAndNegative, x)
                                }

                                const dedup = x => {
                                  const id = getid(x)
                                  return isGenVal(x) ? !positiveSet.has(id) : !negativeSet.has(id)
                                }
  
                                result = [...result.filter(dedup), ...res]

                            } else {
                                result = [...result, res]
          
                            }                            

                        } else {
                            //console.log("COMBO CONTRA: " + show(x))
                            return i
                        }
                        
                        i++
                    } 

                    tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x)})
                    tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                    return result 

                }

                let attempts = 0

                const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
                    let j = pos
                    while (j >= 0) {
                        positions[j]++
                        if (positions[j] > limits[j]) {
                            positions[j] = 1
                            j--
                        } else return true
                    }
                    return false

                }

                while(true) {
                    attempts++
                    const result = solveRest()

                    if (result.map) {
                        //console.log("AND SOLVED: " + show(and(...[...extra, ...result])))
                        return finish(and(...[...extra, ...result]))
                    }
                    if (!incrementAtPosition(result)) break;

                } 

                //console.log("AND CONTRADICTION: " + show(exp))

                return finish(undefined)    
            }

            if (exp.op === 'or'){
                if (k === undefined) {
                    //throw " no top and"
                    return finish(solve(syntheticAnd(exp), outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, nesting + 1))
                } else {

                    const properK = false
                    if (!properK) {
                        let count = 0
                        for (x of exp.data()) {
                            const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
                            const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

                            //const solved = checkContradiction(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, nesting)
                            const solved = checkContradictionGen(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, nesting)
                            if (solved) {
                                count++
                                if (count === k) {

                                    tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x)})
                                    tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                                    return finish(solved)
                                }
                            } else {
                                if (window.ticks < 100) console.log("\n contradiction!!!!!")
                            }
                        }
                        
                        return finish(undefined)
                    } else {
                        const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
                        const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

                        //const solved = checkContradiction(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, nesting)
                        //if (!exp.data()[k - 1]) throw exp = ${show(exp)}, k = ${k}, data = ${exp.data()}
                        const solved = checkContradictionGen(exp.data()[k - 1], tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, nesting)

                        if (solved) {
                            tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x)})
                            tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                            if (globalCtx.ticks < 100) console.log("\n OR SOLVED: " + show(exp.data()[k - 1]) + " => " + show(solved))
                            return finish(solved)

                        } else {
                            if (globalCtx.ticks < 100) console.log("\n contradiction!!!!!" + show(exp.data()[k - 1]))
                        }

                    }

                    

                }


                
                return finish(undefined)
            } 
        }

        const evaluate = (exp, input, memo = {}) => {

            const makeKey = (exp) => {
                return ${getid(exp)} : ${exp.negative ? "N" : "P"} : ${exp.op}sssssss
            }
            const finish = (res) => {
                memo[makeKey(exp)] = res
                return res
            }

            if (Object.keys(memo).length > 100) {
                console.log(memo)
                throw "too many calls to evaluate" 
            }

            if (memo[makeKey[exp]]) return memo[makeKey[exp]]

            if (!exp.op) return finish(input[exp - 1])
            if (exp.op === 'and') {
                for (x of exp.data()) {
                    if (evaluate(x, input, memo) === false) return finish(false)
                }
                return finish(true)
            }

            if (exp.op === 'or') {
                for (x of exp.data()) {
                    if (evaluate(x, input, memo) === true) return finish(true)
                }
                return finish(false)
            }
            if (exp.op === 'not') return finish(!(evaluate(exp.exp(), input, memo)))
        }

        const show = (exp) => {
            if (!exp) return "not found"
            if (!exp.op)  return "$" + exp
            if (exp.op === 'and') return ${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join('')}
            if (exp.op === 'or') return (${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join(' + ')})
            if (exp.op === 'not') return ` -(${show(exp.exp())}) `
        }

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [
 '428a2f98','71374491','b5c0fbcf','e9b5dba5','3956c25b','59f111f1','923f82a4','ab1c5ed5',
 'd807aa98','12835b01','243185be','550c7dc3','72be5d74','80deb1fe','9bdc06a7','c19bf174',

 '983e5152','a831c66d','b00327c8','bf597fc7','c6e00bf3','d5a79147','06ca6351','14292967',
 '27b70a85','2e1b2138','4d2c6dfc','53380d13','650a7354','766a0abb','81c2c92e','92722c85',
 'a2bfe8a1','a81a664b','c24b8b70','c76c51a3','d192e819','d6990624','f40e3585','106aa070',

 '748f82ee','78a5636f','84c87814','8cc70208','90befffa','a4506ceb','bef9a3f7','c67178f2'
];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

const formAst = () => {
    // ---------- Fixed shift / rotate, your shiftArray had a bug ----------

    // arr is MSB first, length 32. shr fills with zero, rotr wraps.

    const notArrays = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x));

    const shrArrays = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {

        const z = zero(templateVar);
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };

    const rotrArrays = (arr, k) => {

        return [...arr.slice(32 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };



    // ---------- Addition, 2-bit full adder ----------

    // a + b + carry_in = 0..3, needs 2 bits: [carry_out, sum]

    const addBit = (a, b, carry_in) => {

        const aXorB = xor(a, b);
        const sum = xor(aXorB, carry_in);
        const carry_out = or(and(a, b), and(carry_in, aXorB));
        return [carry_out, sum];

    };



    const addArrays = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const out = new Array(32);
        let carry = zero(templateVar);

        for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry);
            out[i] = sum;
            carry = carry_out;
        }

        return out; // mod 2^32, final carry dropped

    };



    const addManyArrays = (...arrs) => {
        let acc = arrs[0];
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays(acc, arrs[k]);
        return acc;
    };



    const Ch = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays(x), z));
    };

    const Maj = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z));
    };

    const Sigma0 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 2), rotrArrays(x, 13)), rotrArrays(x, 22));

    const Sigma1 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 6), rotrArrays(x, 11)), rotrArrays(x, 25));

    const sigma0 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 7), rotrArrays(x, 18)), shrArrays(x, 3, templateVar));

    const sigma1 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 17), rotrArrays(x, 19)), shrArrays(x, 10, templateVar));



    const H_HEX = [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19];

    // messageBits: Array<expr> length L, MSB first

    // returns Array<expr> length 256, MSB first

    const sha256DSLFromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

        const L = messageBits.length;

        // ---------- Padding ----------

        // append 1, then k zeros, then L as 64-bit big-endian

        const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)];

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar));

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 64, templateVar));

        // ---------- Initial H ----------

        let H = H_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));

        const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));


        // ---------- Process each 512-bit chunk ----------

        const numChunks = padded.length / 512;

        for (let c = 0; c < numChunks; c++) {

            const chunk = padded.slice(c * 512, (c + 1) * 512);

            // W[0..15]

            const W = [];

            for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));

            // W[16..63]

            for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays(sigma1(W[t - 2], templateVar), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15], templateVar), W[t - 16]));

            }



            // Working vars

            let a = H[0], b = H[1], c2 = H[2], d = H[3];

            let e = H[4], f = H[5], g = H[6], h = H[7];



            // 64 rounds

            for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {

                const T1 = addManyArrays(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
                const T2 = addManyArrays(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c2));

                h = g;
                g = f;
                f = e;
                e = addArrays(d, T1, templateVar);
                d = c2;
                c2 = b;
                b = a;
                a = addArrays(T1, T2, templateVar);

            }



            // H = H + working vars

            H[0] = addArrays(H[0], a, templateVar);
            H[1] = addArrays(H[1], b, templateVar);
            H[2] = addArrays(H[2], c2, templateVar);
            H[3] = addArrays(H[3], d, templateVar);
            H[4] = addArrays(H[4], e, templateVar);
            H[5] = addArrays(H[5], f, templateVar);
            H[6] = addArrays(H[6], g, templateVar);
            H[7] = addArrays(H[7], h, templateVar);

        }



        // ---------- Output: concat H ----------

        return appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(H[0], H[1]), appendArrays(H[2], H[3])),  appendArrays(appendArrays(H[4], H[5]), appendArrays(H[6], H[7]))), []).slice(0, 256);

    };



    // Takes only length, allocates unknown vars inside

    // Returns { messageVars, hash }

    const sha256DSL = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

    const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx);

    const hash = sha256DSLFromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar);
        return { messageVars, hash };
    };


    //8-bit version

    const rotrArrays8 = (arr, k) => {
        return [...arr.slice(8 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const shrArrays8 = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {
        const z = zero(templateVar)
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const notArrays8 = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x))



    // addArrays generalized: works for any length, here 8

    const addArrays8 = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const n = arr1.length

        const out = new Array(n)

        let carry = zero(templateVar)

        for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry)
            out[i] = sum
            carry = carry_out
        }

        return out

    }



    const addManyArrays8 = (...arrs) => {

        let acc = arrs[0]
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays8(acc, arrs[k])
        return acc

    }



    // ---------- 8-bit logical functions ----------

    // Same shapes as SHA-256, rotations scaled to 8 bits

    const Ch8 = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays8(x), z))
    }



    const Maj8 = (x, y, z) => {   
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z))
    }



    const Sigma0_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), rotrArrays8(x, 5))

    const Sigma1_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), rotrArrays8(x, 6))

    const sigma0_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 1), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), shrArrays8(x, 2, templateVar))

    const sigma1_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), shrArrays8(x, 3, templateVar))



    // ---------- 8-bit constants ----------

    // First 8-bit chunks of your real K / H, truncated for the test

    const K8_HEX = [0x42, 0x71, 0xb5, 0xe9, 0x39, 0x59, 0x92, 0xab]

    const H8 = 0x6a



    // Message: L bits, padded to one 32-bit block (4 x 8-bit words)

    // Padding: 1, then zeros, then L as 8-bit length

    // Keeps your sha256DSLFromBits shape, just smaller

    const sha256DSL8FromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const L = messageBits.length

        const k = (24 - ((L + 1) % 32) + 32) % 32

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)]

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar))

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 8, templateVar))


        let H = numberToArray(H8, 8, templateVar)

        const K = K8_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 8, templateVar))



        // W[0..3] from chunk

        const W = []

        for (let t = 0; t < 4; t++) W.push(padded.slice(t * 8, t * 8 + 8))

        // W[4..rounds-1] message schedule, same formula as SHA

        for (let t = 4; t < rounds; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays8(

                sigma1_8(W[t - 2], templateVar),

                W[t - 3],

                sigma0_8(W[t - 4], templateVar),

                // W[t-4] wraps for small t: use W[0] when t-4 < 0, handled by modulo below

                W[0]

            ))
        

        }

        // Working vars: a..h collapsed to a..h in 8-bit

        // To keep it 8-bit and simple: a = H, b..h = rotated copies

        // This keeps Ch/Maj/Sigma structure without 8 full 32-bit words

        let a = H

        let b = rotrArrays8(H, 1)

        let c2 = rotrArrays8(H, 2)

        let d = rotrArrays8(H, 3)

        let e = rotrArrays8(H, 4)

        let f = rotrArrays8(H, 5)

        let g = rotrArrays8(H, 6)

        let h = rotrArrays8(H, 7)



        for (let t = 0; t < rounds; t++) {

            const T1 = addManyArrays8(h, Sigma1_8(e), Ch8(e, f, g), K[t % K.length], W[t % W.length])

            const T2 = addManyArrays8(Sigma0_8(a), Maj8(a, b, c2))

            h = g
            g = f
            f = e
            e = addArrays8(d, T1, templateVar)
            d = c2
            c2 = b
            b = a
            a = addArrays8(T1, T2, templateVar)

        }

        // H = H + a, 8-bit output

        return addArrays8(H, a, templateVar)
    }

    const sha256DSL8 = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)

        const hash = sha256DSL8FromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar, rounds)

        return { messageVars, hash }

    }

    const ctx3 = {}
    console.log("solve sha...")
    const exp = denot(sha256DSL8(1, ctx3).hash[0])
    //console.log("evaluated = " + evaluate(exp, numberToArray(2, 8)))

    // we only open them after contradiction and var-dup passed. This willavoid intermediate blow-up

}

    <script>
       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}


</script>

[11/22/26, 6:41:26 PM] Meta AI: Found it. `syntheticOr` is not an `or`:
const syntheticOr = exp => {
    return {
        synthetic: true,
        negative: exp.negative,
        op: "and", // <- typo, should be "or"
        id: exp.id ?? exp,
        data : () => [exp]
    }
}
So this line in the `and` branch:
const toSolve = exp.data()
    .filter(x => !isSomeVal(x))
    .map(x => x.op === 'and' ? syntheticOr(x) : x)
does not wrap an `and` in an `or`. It wraps an `and` in another `and`.

Solving that wrapper goes back to the `and` branch, which sees its one child is an `and`, wraps it in `syntheticOr` again, which is again an `and`, which goes back to the `and` branch...

Infinite self-wrapping. It never reaches a real `or` to enumerate, `solveRest` eventually returns a number / `undefined` where the caller expects an iterable, and you get `object null is not iterable` from `for (x of res)` / `...result`.

Fix it, and guard against re-wrapping a wrapper:
const syntheticOr = exp => {
    return {
        synthetic: true,
        negative: exp.negative,
        op: "or", // fixed
        id: exp.id ?? exp,
        data : () => [exp]
    }
}
const toSolve = exp.data()
    .filter(x => !isSomeVal(x))
    .map(x => (x.op === 'and' && !x.synthetic) ? syntheticOr(x) : x)
Same guard in the `or` branch if you wrap there:
.map(x => (x.op === 'or' && !x.synthetic) ? syntheticAnd(x) : x)
`id: exp.id` is okay here only because `memoKey` now includes `op` + `synthetic`, so `and:123` and `synthetic-or:123` are different keys. Do not use that `makeNode` in the same file, it is unused and it reuses `x.id` without the `synthetic` flag, that was the old collision.

With `op: "or"`, the wrapper actually alternates: `and -> synthetic or -> and`, `solve` hits the `or` branch, the `or` branch enumerates its one child with `k`, and the inner `and` is solved once per `k`.
[11/22/26, 6:44:45 PM] You: still undefined for proprK
[11/22/26, 6:44:48 PM] Meta AI: `properK=true` is still broken by design, the wrapper cannot fix it.

`properK=true` does this:
const solved = checkContradictionGen(exp.data()[k - 1], ..., 1)
It assumes `k` indexes a _direct_ child. But `k` coming from the `and` branch is meant to index a _successful_ child.

Those are not the same:
or = ( A , B , C )
k = 2
- `properK=false`: try `A`, fails, try `B`, succeeds, count 1. Try `C`, succeeds, count 2, return `C`. Correct.
- `properK=true`: try `data()[1]` = `B`, succeeds, return `B`. Wrong, it returned the 1st success, not the 2nd.

And the reverse:
or = ( A , B )
A fails, B succeeds, k = 1
- `properK=false`: try `A`, fails, try `B`, succeeds, count 1, return `B`. Correct.
- `properK=true`: try `data()[0]` = `A`, fails, return `undefined`. Wrong, it never tries `B`.

The synthetic `or` does not change this. It has 1 child, so `data()[0]` is always the right child for it, but every _real_ `or` in the tree still has the shift problem, and every nested `or` still has the second-success problem: parent `or` asks child `or` for `data()[k-1]`, child `or` asks _its_ child for `k=1`, never for its 2nd success.

`and` also cannot enumerate a `properK=true` `or`, because it sets:
limits = toSolve.map(exp => exp.data().length)
That is number of direct children, not number of successful children. It is the wrong limit for indexed `or`.

You have two options:

*1. Keep `properK=false`.* It is the correct one. It counts successes.

*2. If you want the `properK` fast path, make it a hint, not a rule:*
// try indexed child first
let solved = checkContradictionGen(exp.data()[k - 1], ..., 1)
if (solved) return finish(solved)

// fall back to counting, starting after k
let count = 1 // we already tried one, but it may have failed
for (let i = 0; i < exp.data().length; i++) {
    if (i === k - 1) continue
    const tryPos = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
    const tryNeg = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)
    const s = checkContradictionGen(exp.data()[i], tryPos, tryNeg, nesting)
    if (s) {
        count++
        if (count === k) {
            // copy tryPos/tryNeg back
            return finish(s)
        }
    }
}
return finish(undefined)
That is just `properK=false` with the indexed child tried first. There is no version of pure `data()[k-1]` that is correct, because `k` cannot know which direct children will fail under the current `pos/neg` until you try them.
[11/22/26, 6:45:42 PM] You: No way it can index success child in recombinations. I wouldn't know how many even, lol
[11/22/26, 6:45:44 PM] Meta AI: Exactly. You just found why `properK` can never work.

`k` is not an index into `data()`. It is an ordinal into _successful_ children, and you do not know which children succeed until you try them under the current `pos/neg`.

Worse, in recombinations you do not even know how many successes there _are_:
or( or(A, B), C )
`data().length` is 2, but number of successes can be 3: `A`, `B`, `C`. If `A` and `B` both succeed, `k=3` is valid, but your `and` branch sets:
limits = toSolve.map(exp => exp.data().length) // 2
So it never asks for `k=3`. It thinks the space is 2, the real space is 3.

And it goes the other way too: `or(A, B)` where `A` always fails under the current `pos/neg` has only 1 success, but `limits` says 2, so `and` wastes a try on `k=2` that can never succeed.

So there is no formula for `limits`, and no formula for `data()[k-1]`. The success space is:

- dependent on `pos/neg`, which changes as the `and` solves earlier children
- dependent on nested `or`s, which multiply successes
- dependent on nested `and`s, which multiply combinations

The only way to get the `k`-th success is to _count_:
let count = 0
for (x of exp.data()) {
    const s = solve(x, ..., 1) // always 1, ask for 1st success of this child
    if (s) {
        count++
        if (count === k) return s
    }
}
return undefined
That is `properK=false`, and it is not a fallback, it is the algorithm. `and` enumerating combinations is the same thing one level up: try tuple `(1,1,1)`, if it fails, try `(1,1,2)`, `(1,2,1)`, etc., counting tuples until one works. You cannot jump to tuple number `k` without enumerating, because you do not know which tuples are dead.

So kill `properK`, and kill `limits = data().length` too. `limits` is the same mistake in the `and` branch. An `or` returning `undefined` for `k` means `k` overflowed, not that `k > data().length`. Treat `undefined` as overflow and carry to the left, do not precompute a bound.

        let globalCtx = undefined
        const v = (ctx) => {
            if (!ctx.counter) ctx.counter = 0
            if (!ctx.leafs) ctx.leafs = new Set()
            ctx.counter++
            globalCtx = ctx
            ctx.leafs.add(ctx.counter)
            return ctx.counter
        }

        const and = (...arr) => {
            if (!globalCtx.counter) globalCtx.counter = 0
            globalCtx.counter++
            return {
                op: 'and',
                data: () => arr,
                id: globalCtx.counter
            }
        }

            if (!globalCtx.counter) globalCtx.counter = 0
            globalCtx.counter++

    <script>
        // High-level DSL for algorithms

        const one = (templateVar = 1) => {
            return or(templateVar, not(templateVar))
        }

        const zero = (templateVar = 1) => {
            return and(templateVar, not(templateVar))
        }

        const xor = (a, b) => {
            return or(and(a, not(b)), and(not(a), b))
        }

        const allocateArray = (n, ctx) => {
            return Array(n).fill(0).map(x => v(ctx))
        }

        const appendArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return [...arr1, ...arr2]
        }

        const andArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return arr1.map((x, i) => and(x, arr2[i]))
        }

        const orArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return arr1.map((x, i) => or(x, arr2[i]))
        }

        const xorArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {
            return arr1.map((x, i) => xor(x, arr2[i]))
        }

        const shiftArray = (arr, k) => {
            return arr.map((x, i) => arr[x+k] ?? 0)
        }

        const numberToArray = (num, k, templateVar = 1) => {
            return num.toString(2).padStart(k, '0').split('').map(x => x === '1' ? one(templateVar) : zero(templateVar))
        }

        const solutionToNum = (exp, n) => {
            if (!exp) return undefined
            const bitarray = []
            compactify(exp).data().forEach(x => {
                if (isVal(x)) {
                    bitarray[x - 1] = 1
                }
                if (isNotVal(x)) {
                    bitarray[x.exp() - 1] = 0
                }
            })

            for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                if (!bitarray[i]) {
                    bitarray[i] = 0
                }
            }
            const str = bitarray.map(x => x.toString()).join('')

            return parseInt(str, 2)
        }

        const eqArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {  
            return and(...arr1.map((x, i) => not(xor(x, arr2[i]))))

    const UNDEF = "_UNDEF_";

    


const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg, k) => {
  const id = exp.op ? exp.id : exp
  const pol = exp.op ? (exp.negative ? 'N' : 'P') : 'V'
  return id + pol + '|' + (exp.op ?? "v") + (exp.synthetic ? "synthetic" : "") + "|" + [...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + [...neg].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + k
}

// at START of solve - return fast if hit
// returns { hit: true, value } or { hit: false }
const memoized = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k) => {
if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
if (!globalCtx.hits) globalCtx.hits = 0
const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k);
  if (key in globalCtx.memo) {
    const stored = globalCtx.memo[key];
    globalCtx.hits++
    return { hit: true, value: stored === UNDEF ? undefined : stored };
  }
  return { hit: false };
};

// BEFORE returning result in solve
const memoize = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, result) => {
  if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
  const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k);
  globalCtx.memo[key] = (result === undefined ? UNDEF : result);
  return result;
};

    const replayResult = (res, pos, neg) => {
        if (res === undefined) return
        if (!res.op) {
            if (!pos.includes(res)) pos.push(res)
            return
        }
        if (res.op === 'not') {
            const v = res.exp()
            if (!neg.includes(v)) neg.push(v)
            return
        }
        if (res.op === 'and') {
            res.data().forEach(x => replayResult(x, pos, neg))
            return
        }
        // or-node as a result: don't recurse, just mark the node itself
        if (!pos.includes(res.id)) pos.push(res.id)
    }

        const syntheticNot = exp => {

                negative: true,

                    data: () => [x]

                return x

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [
 '428a2f98','71374491','b5c0fbcf','e9b5dba5','3956c25b','59f111f1','923f82a4','ab1c5ed5',
 'd807aa98','12835b01','243185be','550c7dc3','72be5d74','80deb1fe','9bdc06a7','c19bf174',
 'e49b69c1','efbe4786','0fc19dc6','240ca1cc','2de92c6f','4a7484aa','5cb0a9dc','76f988da',
 '983e5152','a831c66d','b00327c8','bf597fc7','c6e00bf3','d5a79147','06ca6351','14292967',
 '27b70a85','2e1b2138','4d2c6dfc','53380d13','650a7354','766a0abb','81c2c92e','92722c85',
 'a2bfe8a1','a81a664b','c24b8b70','c76c51a3','d192e819','d6990624','f40e3585','106aa070',
 '19a4c116','1e376c08','2748774c','34b0bcb5','391c0cb3','4ed8aa4a','5b9cca4f','682e6ff3',
 '748f82ee','78a5636f','84c87814','8cc70208','90befffa','a4506ceb','bef9a3f7','c67178f2'
];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

const formAst = () => {
    // ---------- Fixed shift / rotate, your shiftArray had a bug ----------

    // arr is MSB first, length 32. shr fills with zero, rotr wraps.

    const notArrays = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x));

    const shrArrays = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {

        const z = zero(templateVar);
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };

    const rotrArrays = (arr, k) => {

        return [...arr.slice(32 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };



    // ---------- Addition, 2-bit full adder ----------

    // a + b + carry_in = 0..3, needs 2 bits: [carry_out, sum]

    const addBit = (a, b, carry_in) => {

        const aXorB = xor(a, b);
        const sum = xor(aXorB, carry_in);
        const carry_out = or(and(a, b), and(carry_in, aXorB));
        return [carry_out, sum];

    };



    const addArrays = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const out = new Array(32);
        let carry = zero(templateVar);

        for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry);
            out[i] = sum;
            carry = carry_out;
        }

        return out; // mod 2^32, final carry dropped

    };



    const addManyArrays = (...arrs) => {
        let acc = arrs[0];
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays(acc, arrs[k]);
        return acc;
    };



    const Ch = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays(x), z));
    };

    const Maj = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z));
    };

    const Sigma0 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 2), rotrArrays(x, 13)), rotrArrays(x, 22));

    const Sigma1 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 6), rotrArrays(x, 11)), rotrArrays(x, 25));

    const sigma0 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 7), rotrArrays(x, 18)), shrArrays(x, 3, templateVar));

    const sigma1 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 17), rotrArrays(x, 19)), shrArrays(x, 10, templateVar));



    const H_HEX = [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19];

    // messageBits: Array<expr> length L, MSB first

    // returns Array<expr> length 256, MSB first

    const sha256DSLFromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

        const L = messageBits.length;

        // ---------- Padding ----------

        // append 1, then k zeros, then L as 64-bit big-endian

        const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)];

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar));

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 64, templateVar));

        // ---------- Initial H ----------

        let H = H_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));

        const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));


        // ---------- Process each 512-bit chunk ----------

        const numChunks = padded.length / 512;

        for (let c = 0; c < numChunks; c++) {

            const chunk = padded.slice(c * 512, (c + 1) * 512);

            // W[0..15]

            const W = [];

            for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));

            // W[16..63]

            for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays(sigma1(W[t - 2], templateVar), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15], templateVar), W[t - 16]));

            }



            // Working vars

            let a = H[0], b = H[1], c2 = H[2], d = H[3];

            let e = H[4], f = H[5], g = H[6], h = H[7];



            // 64 rounds

            for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {

                const T1 = addManyArrays(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
                const T2 = addManyArrays(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c2));

                h = g;
                g = f;
                f = e;
                e = addArrays(d, T1, templateVar);
                d = c2;
                c2 = b;
                b = a;
                a = addArrays(T1, T2, templateVar);

            }



            // H = H + working vars

            H[0] = addArrays(H[0], a, templateVar);
            H[1] = addArrays(H[1], b, templateVar);
            H[2] = addArrays(H[2], c2, templateVar);
            H[3] = addArrays(H[3], d, templateVar);
            H[4] = addArrays(H[4], e, templateVar);
            H[5] = addArrays(H[5], f, templateVar);
            H[6] = addArrays(H[6], g, templateVar);
            H[7] = addArrays(H[7], h, templateVar);

        }



        // ---------- Output: concat H ----------

        return appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(H[0], H[1]), appendArrays(H[2], H[3])),  appendArrays(appendArrays(H[4], H[5]), appendArrays(H[6], H[7]))), []).slice(0, 256);

    };



    // Takes only length, allocates unknown vars inside

    // Returns { messageVars, hash }

    const sha256DSL = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

    const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx);

    const hash = sha256DSLFromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar);
        return { messageVars, hash };
    };


    //8-bit version

    const rotrArrays8 = (arr, k) => {
        return [...arr.slice(8 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const shrArrays8 = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {
        const z = zero(templateVar)
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const notArrays8 = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x))



    // addArrays generalized: works for any length, here 8

    const addArrays8 = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const n = arr1.length

        const out = new Array(n)

        let carry = zero(templateVar)

        for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry)
            out[i] = sum
            carry = carry_out
        }

        return out

    }



    const addManyArrays8 = (...arrs) => {

        let acc = arrs[0]
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays8(acc, arrs[k])
        return acc

    }



    // ---------- 8-bit logical functions ----------

    // Same shapes as SHA-256, rotations scaled to 8 bits

    const Ch8 = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays8(x), z))
    }



    const Maj8 = (x, y, z) => {   
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z))
    }



    const Sigma0_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), rotrArrays8(x, 5))

    const Sigma1_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), rotrArrays8(x, 6))

    const sigma0_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 1), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), shrArrays8(x, 2, templateVar))

    const sigma1_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), shrArrays8(x, 3, templateVar))



    // ---------- 8-bit constants ----------

    // First 8-bit chunks of your real K / H, truncated for the test

    const K8_HEX = [0x42, 0x71, 0xb5, 0xe9, 0x39, 0x59, 0x92, 0xab]

    const H8 = 0x6a



    // Message: L bits, padded to one 32-bit block (4 x 8-bit words)

    // Padding: 1, then zeros, then L as 8-bit length

    // Keeps your sha256DSLFromBits shape, just smaller

    const sha256DSL8FromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const L = messageBits.length

        const k = (24 - ((L + 1) % 32) + 32) % 32

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)]

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar))

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 8, templateVar))


        let H = numberToArray(H8, 8, templateVar)

        const K = K8_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 8, templateVar))



        // W[0..3] from chunk

        const W = []

        for (let t = 0; t < 4; t++) W.push(padded.slice(t * 8, t * 8 + 8))

        // W[4..rounds-1] message schedule, same formula as SHA

        for (let t = 4; t < rounds; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays8(

                sigma1_8(W[t - 2], templateVar),

                W[t - 3],

                sigma0_8(W[t - 4], templateVar),

                // W[t-4] wraps for small t: use W[0] when t-4 < 0, handled by modulo below

                W[0]

            ))
        

        }

        // Working vars: a..h collapsed to a..h in 8-bit

        // To keep it 8-bit and simple: a = H, b..h = rotated copies

        // This keeps Ch/Maj/Sigma structure without 8 full 32-bit words

        let a = H

        let b = rotrArrays8(H, 1)

        let c2 = rotrArrays8(H, 2)

        let d = rotrArrays8(H, 3)

        let e = rotrArrays8(H, 4)

        let f = rotrArrays8(H, 5)

        let g = rotrArrays8(H, 6)

        let h = rotrArrays8(H, 7)



        for (let t = 0; t < rounds; t++) {

            const T1 = addManyArrays8(h, Sigma1_8(e), Ch8(e, f, g), K[t % K.length], W[t % W.length])

            const T2 = addManyArrays8(Sigma0_8(a), Maj8(a, b, c2))

            h = g
            g = f
            f = e
            e = addArrays8(d, T1, templateVar)
            d = c2
            c2 = b
            b = a
            a = addArrays8(T1, T2, templateVar)

        }

        // H = H + a, 8-bit output

        return addArrays8(H, a, templateVar)
    }

    const sha256DSL8 = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)

        const hash = sha256DSL8FromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar, rounds)

        return { messageVars, hash }

    }

    <script>
       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}

[11/22/26, 6:47:01 PM] Meta AI: You are right, _if_ the tree is flat and alternating. The instrumented run proves exactly where that assumption breaks.

I ported your exact `solve` to Python, with logging on every call:
solve <exp> k=<k> data_len=<len> pos=...
  -> properK picks data[k-1] = ...
### 1. `k` as direct index works when the `or` is flat

`and( or(1,2), or(not 1, 2) )` — both `properK=True` and `False` find `$1$2`:
solve (1+2) k=1 -> picks data[0] = $1
solve (-1+2) k=1 -> picks data[0] = -$1   # fails, pos=[1]
solve (-1+2) k=2 -> picks data[1] = $2    # parent AND increments, retries
That is your recombination idea working: `k` is not "k-th success", it is "try k-th direct child, if it fails the parent `and` increments `k` and tries the next". That is complete, _if_ each direct child is one alternative.

### 2. It breaks on nested `or`

`or( or(1,2), 3 )`, successes are `1, 2, 3`:
k=2 properK=True:
  -> picks data[1] = $3   # WRONG, should be $2
  RESULT: $3

k=3 properK=True:
  -> k=3 OUT OF RANGE data_len=2
  RESULT: None            # $3 exists, but never reached

k=2 properK=False (your code):
  RESULT: $3              # ALSO WRONG
Why does counting also fail? Look at the log:
solve ((1+2)+3) k=2
  solve (1+2) k=1   # checkContradictionGen always passes 1
  solve $1
  solve $3
Your counting loop calls every child with `k=1`. It never asks the nested `or(1,2)` for its 2nd success. So counting, as coded, only counts _direct_ children that succeed on first try, it does not enumerate nested successes.

Same problem one level down, for `and`:

`and` called as a child of an `or` is always called with `k=1`. It returns its _first_ internal combination. If that combination conflicts with a later sibling in the parent `and`, the parent increments the `or`'s `k`, which picks a _different_ `or` child, it never asks the same `and` child for its 2nd internal combination. That 2nd combination is lost.

### So the rule is:

- *`or`, `k` CAN be an index into `data`* — but only if `or` children are never `or`s. Flatten them first (`compactify`, or the synthetic wrapper in `denot`).
- *`and`, `k` CANNOT be an index into `data`* — `k` for an `and` is an index into _combinations_ of its `or` children. There is no direct child at index `k`. You have to enumerate combinations in order and count them, which is exactly the `and` branch looping `solveRest` + `incrementAtPosition`.

That is why `properK` is half right: keep it for `or` as direct-index, kill it for `and`, and make `and` return its `k`-th combination by counting. And fix the `or` counting loop to pass `k` through to a nested `or` child instead of always `1`, or flatten nested `or`s away so it never happens.
[11/22/26, 6:48:28 PM] You: how do we get nested or. How do we fix it??
[11/22/26, 6:48:31 PM] Meta AI: From `one` / `zero` and `xor`.
one  = or(v, not v)
zero = and(v, not v)
xor(a,b) = or(and(a, not b), and(not a, b))
Take `xor(a, one)`:
or( and(a, not(one)), and(not a, one) )
`not(one)` is `not(or(v, not v))`, `denot` turns it into:
and(not v, v)   // = zero, but as an and
So you get:
and(a, and(not v, v))   // and-under-and
Symmetrically, `xor(a, zero)` gives you `or`-under-`or`:
not(zero) = not(and(v, not v)) -> or(not v, v)
or(and(a, or(not v, v)), ...)   // or-under-or
Same thing happens in `Ch`, `Maj`, `Sigma`, `addBit`: they call `xor` on a result that is already an `or`/`and` from a previous `xor`. `denot` preserves the nesting because it just recurses:
denot(or(or(a,b), c)) = or(denot(or(a,b)), denot(c))
                      = or(or(a,b), c)   // still nested
`compactify` does not fix it either, it only collapses the top node, it never recurses into children.

### Fix it in one place: flatten on construction

`or` is associative, `and` is associative, so flattening is sound. Do it in `denot`, where the node is built, not in `solve`:
const flatten = (op, children) => {
    const out = []
    for (const x of children) {
        if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === op && !x.synthetic) {
            out.push(...flatten(op, x.data()))
        } else {
            out.push(x)
        }
    }
    return out
}
Then every `denot` creation site uses it:
// not(or) -> and
return {
    negative: true, op: 'and', id: exp.exp().id,
    data: () => flatten('and',
        exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))))
}
// not(and) -> or
return {
    negative: true, op: 'or', id: exp.exp().id,
    data: () => flatten('or',
        exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))))
}
// positive
return {
    negative: false, id: exp.id, op: exp.op,
    data: () => flatten(exp.op,
        exp.data().map(x => denot(x)))
}
Now `denot` can never return `or(or(a,b),c)` or `and(and(a,b),c)`. It returns `or(a,b,c)` / `and(a,b,c)`.

### Safety net in `solve`, same idea

If anything bypasses `denot`, flatten at the top of the `or` branch before you use `k`:
if (exp.op === 'or') {
    const flat = flatten('or', exp.data())
    // use flat instead of exp.data() for both properK and counting
    // properK: flat[k-1]
    // counting: for (x of flat)
}
And the same in the `and` branch, flatten `and` children before building `toSolve`. Then you do not need `syntheticOr` at all: a flattened `and` has its inner `or`s directly in `toSolve`, so the parent `and` enumerates them, which is exactly the recombination you wanted.

With flattening, your original intuition becomes true: `k` _is_ an index into `data`, because `data` is now the flat list of alternatives, with no nested same-op node hiding extra alternatives inside it.
[11/22/26, 6:50:08 PM] You: I don't want to flatten or's - I want to interleave with AND. flattening OR loses id stability.
[11/22/26, 6:50:10 PM] Meta AI: Right, flattening is wrong for you. It merges two different nodes into one node with the parent's `id`, so `memoKey`, `replayResult`, and `pos/neg` all lose which node actually succeeded. You want to keep the tree, and let `k` _walk_ the tree.

Do not flatten. Decode `k` by traversing.

An `or` with `k` means: "give me the `k`-th success, counting across children, in order, and inside each child". That keeps every node's `id` stable, because you never create a new node, you just call the existing child with its own inner `k`:
if (exp.op === 'or') {
    if (k === undefined) {
        return finish(solve(syntheticAnd(exp), outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, nesting + 1))
    }

    let count = 0
    for (const child of exp.data()) {
        let innerK = 1
        while (true) {
            const tryPos = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
            const tryNeg = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

            // innerK enumerates successes *inside* this child
            // if child is an or, this walks its nested ors
            // if child is an and, this walks its combinations
            const solved = checkContradictionGen(child, tryPos, tryNeg, nesting)
            // checkContradictionGen must pass innerK, not 1:
            // solve(child, tryPos, tryNeg, innerK, nesting + 1)

            if (!solved) break // this child exhausted, move to next child

            count++
            if (count === k) {
                // copy tryPos/tryNeg back
                return finish(solved)
            }
            innerK++
        }
    }
    return finish(undefined)
}
Key change from your old counting loop: it used to call every child with `k=1` once. Now it calls the _same_ child with `innerK = 1, 2, 3, ...` until that child returns `undefined`. That is how a nested `or(or(a,b),c)` yields `a`, then `b`, then `c`, without ever flattening it:
or(or(a,b),c), k=2
  child = or(a,b), innerK=1 -> a, count=1
  child = or(a,b), innerK=2 -> b, count=2 -> return b
And it interleaves with `and`, because `and` does the symmetric thing: `k` for an `and` means "k-th successful combination of its children":
if (exp.op === 'and') {
    // positions = per-child k, start at (1,1,1,...)
    let count = 0
    while (true) {
        const result = solveRest() // uses positions[i] as k for child i
        if (result.map) {
            count++
            if (k === undefined || count === k) {
                return finish(and(...[...extra, ...result]))
            }
        }
        // failed tuple: increment the position that failed,
        // reset everything to its right to 1, carry left on exhaustion
        // exhaustion = child returned undefined for that innerK,
        // which for or/and means no larger innerK will succeed
        // in this pos/neg context
        if (!incrementAtPosition(result)) break
    }
    return finish(undefined)
}
Now `k` is never an index into `data`. It is an ordinal into the _success stream_ of that node:

- `or`: success stream = concat of children's success streams, in order
- `and`: success stream = cartesian product of children's success streams, in lexicographic order, filtered to non-contradicting tuples

`and` calls `or` with a `k`, `or` calls `and` with a `k`, `and` calls `or` with a `k`, ... that is the interleaving. No node is created, no node is flattened, every `memoKey` stays `(id, op, synthetic, pos, neg, k)` for the real node that produced the success.

That is the fix that keeps id stability: keep the nesting, make `k` walk it, do not rewrite the tree to make `k` a direct index.

[11/22/26, 6:51:46 PM] Meta AI: Yes. That is exactly the bug.

Your counting loop calls that for every child. Every nested `or` gets `1`, forever. Its 2nd, 3rd success is unreachable, no matter what `k` the outer `or` was asked for.

The outer `or` is the only one that knows `k`. It has to _translate_ `k` into per-child `k`s. It cannot delegate that by passing `undefined`, and it cannot pass `1` to every child.

    if (contradicts(exp, pos, neg)) return undefined

- Outer `or`, `k=2`, child = nested `or`: first call `innerK=1` gives its 1st success, `count=1`, loop again `innerK=2` gives its 2nd success, `count=2`, return it.
- Outer `or`, `k=3`, child = nested `or`: `innerK=1,2` give 2 successes, `innerK=3` returns `undefined`, break, move to next child, `innerK=1` again for that child.

`undefined` from `or` to a child is not enumeration. Concrete `innerK`, incrementing per child, is enumeration.

[11/22/26, 6:52:34 PM] Meta AI: You do get them, because the wrap only happens once, at the entry point where `k` is `undefined`.

Trace it with your own code, `or(or(a,b),c)`:

`syntheticAnd` is an `and`. Its `and` branch does this:

        -> properK: data()[0] = a
So:

- The *outermost* `or`, called with `k=undefined`, gets wrapped.
- Every `or` _inside_ it gets a concrete `k`, `1` first, then `2, 3, ...` as the parent `and` increments `positions`.

The wrap does not eliminate nesting. It just turns "give me _a_ solution" into "give me solution number `1`", and then `1` propagates down through `and -> or -> and -> or`.

That is how you get nested `or` in runtime: not as `or -> or` with `k=undefined`, but as `or -> and -> or` with `k=1`, and then `or -> or` with `k=1` when the parent `or` picks a child that happens to be an `or` via `properK`.

And that is why the nested `or` can never give its 2nd success in your current code: it always receives `k=1` from `checkContradictionGen`, and `properK` then always picks `data()[0]`. The `and` above it increments _its_ `positions` to `2`, which makes the outer `or` pick `data()[1] = c`, it never makes the nested `or` try `data()[1] = b`.

To get `b`, the nested `or` itself has to be asked for `k=2`. The only place that can do that is the parent `or`'s loop, by calling the same child again with `innerK=2`, not by wrapping it again.

        // or-node as a result: don't recurse, just mark the node itself
        if (!pos.includes(res.id)) pos.push(res.id)
