        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [
 '428a2f98','71374491','b5c0fbcf','e9b5dba5','3956c25b','59f111f1','923f82a4','ab1c5ed5',
 'd807aa98','12835b01','243185be','550c7dc3','72be5d74','80deb1fe','9bdc06a7','c19bf174',

 '983e5152','a831c66d','b00327c8','bf597fc7','c6e00bf3','d5a79147','06ca6351','14292967',
 '27b70a85','2e1b2138','4d2c6dfc','53380d13','650a7354','766a0abb','81c2c92e','92722c85',
 'a2bfe8a1','a81a664b','c24b8b70','c76c51a3','d192e819','d6990624','f40e3585','106aa070',

 '748f82ee','78a5636f','84c87814','8cc70208','90befffa','a4506ceb','bef9a3f7','c67178f2'
];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

const formAst = () => {
    // ---------- Fixed shift / rotate, your shiftArray had a bug ----------

    // arr is MSB first, length 32. shr fills with zero, rotr wraps.

    const notArrays = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x));

    const shrArrays = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {

        const z = zero(templateVar);
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };

    const rotrArrays = (arr, k) => {

        return [...arr.slice(32 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };



    // ---------- Addition, 2-bit full adder ----------

    // a + b + carry_in = 0..3, needs 2 bits: [carry_out, sum]

    const addBit = (a, b, carry_in) => {

        const aXorB = xor(a, b);
        const sum = xor(aXorB, carry_in);
        const carry_out = or(and(a, b), and(carry_in, aXorB));
        return [carry_out, sum];

    };



    const addArrays = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const out = new Array(32);
        let carry = zero(templateVar);

        for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry);
            out[i] = sum;
            carry = carry_out;
        }

        return out; // mod 2^32, final carry dropped

    };



    const addManyArrays = (...arrs) => {
        let acc = arrs[0];
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays(acc, arrs[k]);
        return acc;
    };



    const Ch = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays(x), z));
    };

    const Maj = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z));
    };

    const Sigma0 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 2), rotrArrays(x, 13)), rotrArrays(x, 22));

    const Sigma1 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 6), rotrArrays(x, 11)), rotrArrays(x, 25));

    const sigma0 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 7), rotrArrays(x, 18)), shrArrays(x, 3, templateVar));

    const sigma1 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 17), rotrArrays(x, 19)), shrArrays(x, 10, templateVar));



    const H_HEX = [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19];

    // messageBits: Array<expr> length L, MSB first

    // returns Array<expr> length 256, MSB first

    const sha256DSLFromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

        const L = messageBits.length;

        // ---------- Padding ----------

        // append 1, then k zeros, then L as 64-bit big-endian

        const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)];

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar));

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 64, templateVar));

        // ---------- Initial H ----------

        let H = H_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));

        const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));


        // ---------- Process each 512-bit chunk ----------

        const numChunks = padded.length / 512;

        for (let c = 0; c < numChunks; c++) {

            const chunk = padded.slice(c * 512, (c + 1) * 512);

            // W[0..15]

            const W = [];

            for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));

            // W[16..63]

            for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays(sigma1(W[t - 2], templateVar), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15], templateVar), W[t - 16]));

            }



            // Working vars

            let a = H[0], b = H[1], c2 = H[2], d = H[3];

            let e = H[4], f = H[5], g = H[6], h = H[7];



            // 64 rounds

            for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {

                const T1 = addManyArrays(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
                const T2 = addManyArrays(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c2));

                h = g;
                g = f;
                f = e;
                e = addArrays(d, T1, templateVar);
                d = c2;
                c2 = b;
                b = a;
                a = addArrays(T1, T2, templateVar);

            }



            // H = H + working vars

            H[0] = addArrays(H[0], a, templateVar);
            H[1] = addArrays(H[1], b, templateVar);
            H[2] = addArrays(H[2], c2, templateVar);
            H[3] = addArrays(H[3], d, templateVar);
            H[4] = addArrays(H[4], e, templateVar);
            H[5] = addArrays(H[5], f, templateVar);
            H[6] = addArrays(H[6], g, templateVar);
            H[7] = addArrays(H[7], h, templateVar);

        }



        // ---------- Output: concat H ----------

        return appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(H[0], H[1]), appendArrays(H[2], H[3])),  appendArrays(appendArrays(H[4], H[5]), appendArrays(H[6], H[7]))), []).slice(0, 256);

    };



    // Takes only length, allocates unknown vars inside

    // Returns { messageVars, hash }

    const sha256DSL = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

    const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx);

    const hash = sha256DSLFromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar);
        return { messageVars, hash };
    };


    //8-bit version

    const rotrArrays8 = (arr, k) => {
        return [...arr.slice(8 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const shrArrays8 = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {
        const z = zero(templateVar)
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const notArrays8 = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x))



    // addArrays generalized: works for any length, here 8

    const addArrays8 = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const n = arr1.length

        const out = new Array(n)

        let carry = zero(templateVar)

        for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry)
            out[i] = sum
            carry = carry_out
        }

        return out

    }



    const addManyArrays8 = (...arrs) => {

        let acc = arrs[0]
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays8(acc, arrs[k])
        return acc

    }



    // ---------- 8-bit logical functions ----------

    // Same shapes as SHA-256, rotations scaled to 8 bits

    const Ch8 = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays8(x), z))
    }



    const Maj8 = (x, y, z) => {   
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z))
    }



    const Sigma0_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), rotrArrays8(x, 5))

    const Sigma1_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), rotrArrays8(x, 6))

    const sigma0_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 1), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), shrArrays8(x, 2, templateVar))

    const sigma1_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), shrArrays8(x, 3, templateVar))



    // ---------- 8-bit constants ----------

    // First 8-bit chunks of your real K / H, truncated for the test

    const K8_HEX = [0x42, 0x71, 0xb5, 0xe9, 0x39, 0x59, 0x92, 0xab]

    const H8 = 0x6a



    // Message: L bits, padded to one 32-bit block (4 x 8-bit words)

    // Padding: 1, then zeros, then L as 8-bit length

    // Keeps your sha256DSLFromBits shape, just smaller

    const sha256DSL8FromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const L = messageBits.length

        const k = (24 - ((L + 1) % 32) + 32) % 32

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)]

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar))

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 8, templateVar))


        let H = numberToArray(H8, 8, templateVar)

        const K = K8_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 8, templateVar))



        // W[0..3] from chunk

        const W = []

        for (let t = 0; t < 4; t++) W.push(padded.slice(t * 8, t * 8 + 8))

        // W[4..rounds-1] message schedule, same formula as SHA

        for (let t = 4; t < rounds; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays8(

                sigma1_8(W[t - 2], templateVar),

                W[t - 3],

                sigma0_8(W[t - 4], templateVar),

                // W[t-4] wraps for small t: use W[0] when t-4 < 0, handled by modulo below

                W[0]

            ))
        

        }

        // Working vars: a..h collapsed to a..h in 8-bit

        // To keep it 8-bit and simple: a = H, b..h = rotated copies

        // This keeps Ch/Maj/Sigma structure without 8 full 32-bit words

        let a = H

        let b = rotrArrays8(H, 1)

        let c2 = rotrArrays8(H, 2)

        let d = rotrArrays8(H, 3)

        let e = rotrArrays8(H, 4)

        let f = rotrArrays8(H, 5)

        let g = rotrArrays8(H, 6)

        let h = rotrArrays8(H, 7)



        for (let t = 0; t < rounds; t++) {

            const T1 = addManyArrays8(h, Sigma1_8(e), Ch8(e, f, g), K[t % K.length], W[t % W.length])

            const T2 = addManyArrays8(Sigma0_8(a), Maj8(a, b, c2))

            h = g
            g = f
            f = e
            e = addArrays8(d, T1, templateVar)
            d = c2
            c2 = b
            b = a
            a = addArrays8(T1, T2, templateVar)

        }

        // H = H + a, 8-bit output

        return addArrays8(H, a, templateVar)
    }

    const sha256DSL8 = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)

        const hash = sha256DSL8FromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar, rounds)

        return { messageVars, hash }

    }

    const ctx3 = {}
    console.log("solve sha...")
    const exp = denot(sha256DSL8(1, ctx3).hash[0])

    console.log(solve(exp))

    <script>
       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}


</script>

Instrument this, before `solve(exp)` in `formAst()`:
// count every one()/zero() pattern in denot(exp)
let ones = 0, zeros = 0, ids = new Set()
const walk = (e) => {
    if (!e || !e.op) { ids.add(e); return }
    if (e.op === 'and' && e.data().length === 2) {
        const [a, b] = e.data()
        if (b.op === 'not' && b.exp() === a) { zeros++; ids.add(a); return }
    }
    if (e.op === 'or' && e.data().length === 2) {
        const [a, b] = e.data()
        if (b.op === 'not' && b.exp() === a) { ones++; ids.add(a); return }
    }
    if (e.op === 'not') walk(e.exp())
    else e.data().forEach(walk)
}
walk(exp)
console.log('ones=', ones, 'zeros=', zeros, 'template ids=', [...ids])
console.log('messageVars=', ctx3.leafs) // or messageVars
You will get:
ones=..., zeros=..., template ids=[1]
messageVars=[1]
All `one()` / `zero()` share *one* variable, and it is the *same* variable as your message bit.

Why that kills it:
const one = (templateVar = 1) => or(templateVar, not(templateVar))
const zero = (templateVar = 1) => and(templateVar, not(templateVar))
- `sha256DSL8(1, ctx3)` allocates the message bit first: `v(ctx3) === 1`
- Every constant, padding bit, `H`, `K`, `L`, `shr` filler, then calls `one(1)` / `zero(1)` with the default `templateVar = 1`

So logically:

- `xor(one, y)` can only succeed via `and(one, not y)`, which picks `or(1, not 1) -> 1`, forcing `pos = [1]`
- `xor(zero, y)` can only succeed via `and(not zero, y)`, where `not zero = or(not 1, 1)`, which picks `not 1`, forcing `neg = [1]`

Both branches are required by the surrounding `and`/`addManyArrays`. One requires `1`, the other requires `not 1`. Same `id`, opposite polarity, in the same `and` context. That is a hard contradiction, no amount of `or` enumeration can fix it, because the two requirements are not alternatives, they are both required.

In `array_eq` this does not happen: `numberToArray(input, 5)` is the _target_, not the searched expression, and `eqArrays` never mixes a shared `one`/`zero` with a message variable of the same `id` in a required `and`.

Fix: give the template a fresh variable, never `1`, and never shared with the message:
const templateVar = v(ctx3) // allocate AFTER messageVars, or in a separate ctx
const exp = denot(sha256DSL8(1, ctx3, templateVar).hash[0])
Or, better, make `one`/`zero` allocate a fresh var per call, so constants do not couple to each other at all. With a fresh template var, the instrument above shows `template ids != messageVars`, and the same `solve` returns a value instead of `undefined`.
[11/22/26, 7:12:56 PM] You: ah, we should preallocate templateVar in advance then, right? :)
[11/22/26, 7:12:57 PM] Meta AI: Almost, but not _one_ preallocated var. That is still the bug, just moved.

If all `one()` / `zero()` share one `T`:

- `xor(one, y)` only survives via `and(one, not y)` -> forces `T = 1`
- `xor(zero, y)` only survives via `and(not zero, y)` -> forces `T = 0`

Both are required by the same surrounding `and`. One `T` cannot be `1` and `0`, even if `T` is distinct from the message var. You would still get `undefined`.

Preallocate _per call_:
const one = (ctx) => { const t = v(ctx); return or(t, not(t)) }
const zero = (ctx) => { const t = v(ctx); return and(t, not(t)) }
Each constant gets its own fresh `t`. Then `one`'s branch sets _its_ `t = 1`, `zero`'s branch sets _its_ `t = 0`, no coupling, no contradiction.

So: yes, allocate in advance, but allocate a new one every time you call `one()` / `zero()`, not one shared `templateVar = 1` for the whole run.

[11/22/26, 7:15:05 PM] Meta AI: You are right, I was wrong on that. Sharing `T` does not make it unsatisfiable.

`one = or(T, not T)` can be satisfied with `T = 0` _or_ `T = 1`. `not zero = or(not T, T)` can also be satisfied with either. So the solver can align them all to the same `T`, e.g. pick `not T` everywhere:

- `xor(one, y)` via `and(one, not y)`, with `one` via `not T`
- `xor(zero, y)` via `and(not zero, y)`, with `not zero` via `not T`

No forced `T = 1` vs `T = 0`. My earlier claim assumed each `or` only has one surviving branch, but it has two, and your `and` branch enumerates the Cartesian product of `positions`, so it can find the aligned one.

So something else. The first thing to check is not the solver at all, it is whether `hash[0]` _can_ be true:

console.log('hash[0] with msg=1:', evaluate(hash[0], [true]))
You are solving `denot(hash[0])`, i.e. "find an assignment making `hash[0]` true". In `array_eq` you solved `eqArrays(..., numberToArray(30))`, i.e. "find an assignment making the output _equal a chosen target_". Those are different.

If the toy 8-bit hash has `hash[0] === false` for both `msg = 0` and `msg = 1`, then `undefined` is the _correct_ answer, not a solver bug. There is no preimage of `1` for that bit.

If one of those evaluates to `true`, then it _is_ a solver bug, and the next instrument is memoization: log the first `solve` that returns `undefined` for a node that `evaluate` says is satisfiable under the current `pos`/`neg`. That points at either the memo key colliding for `synthetic` nodes with the same `id`, or the `and` branch not backtracking past a failing `positions` combination.

[11/22/26, 7:25:28 PM] Meta AI: You are right on 1). I overstated it. Fixing that one first.

### 1) Recreating the tree

Agreed. Re-creating nodes is not by itself exponential.

It is only a constant factor *if* the scan is memoized correctly, because the scan keys by `id`, not by object identity. Same `id` = same logical node, even if it is a new object.

Where it _does_ hurt is: it makes the memo bug in 2) fatal, because you cannot rely on object identity to distinguish occurrences. You have to rely on the key, and the key is wrong.

So: leave `denot` / `data()` alone for now.

### 2) How to fix `makeKey`

The bug: `pos` / `neg` contain *node ids*, not just leaf ids.
// and branch
addPos(outerAndPositive, x) // x can be an and/or node
addNeg(outerAndNegative, x)
// contradicts checks those node ids
contradicts(x, pos, neg)
But `makeKey` was:
[...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x))
So two different contexts collapse to one key.

Fix: put the *full, sorted* `pos` / `neg` in the key, and also distinguish the things that share an `id`:
const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg, k) => {
  let id, pol, op, syn

  if (isNotVal(exp)) {
    // -leaf: id is the leaf, polarity is negative
    id = exp.exp(); pol = 'N'; op = 'notval'; syn = 0
  } else if (isVal(exp)) {
    id = exp; pol = 'V'; op = 'val'; syn = 0
  } else {
    id = exp.id
    pol = exp.negative ? 'N' : 'P'
    op = exp.op
    syn = exp.synthetic ? 1 : 0
  }

  // pos / neg are arrays of ids (numbers). Copy + numeric sort,
  // do NOT filter to leafs.
  const p = [...pos].sort((a, b) => a - b).join(',')
  const n = [...neg].sort((a, b) => a - b).join(',')

  return `${id}|${pol}|${op}|${syn}|${k ?? ''}|${p}|${n}`
}
Why all the fields:

- `id` alone is not enough: `syntheticNot(x)`, `syntheticAnd(x)`, `syntheticOr(x)` reuse `x.id`.
- `pol` / `op` / `syn`: same `id` can appear as `and`, as `or`, as negative, as synthetic.
- `k`: same `or` node, different branch `k`, is a different sub-problem.
- full `p` / `n`: same node, different assumed node ids, is a different sub-problem. This is the actual fix.

One more requirement: `pos` / `neg` passed to `memoKey` must be snapshots, not live arrays that later mutate. In `solve` you already do `snapPos = [...pos]`, use those for both `memoized()` and `memoize()`.

### 3) Do we need a fix for `replayResult`?

Yes, if you keep memo hits. With the fixed key alone it is still lossy.

Why: `solve` is supposed to mutate `pos` / `neg` as a side effect. Callers rely on it:
// and branch, solveRest()
const res = solve(child, tpos, tneg, ...)
if (res) {
  // tpos / tneg are now supposed to contain
  // the leaves that made `res` true
  if (contradicts(y, tpos, tneg)) return i
}
If `solve` returns a cached value without replaying, `tpos` / `tneg` do *not* contain those leaves. The next `contradicts()` check misses, the next child is solved under a weaker context, and you get a fake success, or later a fake contradiction that gets memoized.

The current version is wrong for `or`:
// old: or-node as a result: don't recurse, just mark the node itself
if (!pos.includes(res.id)) pos.push(res.id)
Pushing the `or` id marks "this `or` is true" without choosing which branch made it true. That is exactly the node-id assumption that then gets lost / mis-memoized.

Fix: replay must walk the cached result down to leaves, never push an `or` / `and` id as if it were a leaf:
const replayResult = (res, pos, neg) => {
  if (res === undefined || res === null) return

  if (Array.isArray(res)) {
    for (const y of res) replayResult(y, pos, neg)
    return
  }

  if (isGenVal(res)) { addPos(pos, res); return }
  if (isGenNotVal(res)) { addNeg(neg, res); return }

  // res is a composite node returned by solve,
  // e.g. AND(...). Walk its children.
  // Do NOT push res.id here.
  if (res.op === 'and' || res.op === 'or') {
    for (const y of res.data()) replayResult(y, pos, neg)
    return
  }

  // Should not happen for a solved result:
  // a bare or-node is not a witness, a branch is.
  // If it does, do not push res.id, treat as bug.
}
Rule: a memo hit must leave `pos` / `neg` in exactly the state a fresh solve would have left them. Fresh solve leaves leaves, not composite ids.

So order of fixes:

1. `makeKey`: full `pos` / `neg`, plus `op` / `pol` / `syn` / `k`. This is the real bug.
2. `replayResult`: leaf-walk, no `res.id` for `or`. Needed, otherwise memo hits are lossy even with a correct key.
3. Leave `denot` re-creation alone, it is not the exponential part.

[11/22/26, 7:46:17 PM] You: One more thing before we finish - my “evaluate” does not handle sha8 evaluation (it blows). Can you write evaluate that does (eg goes depth first, in while true without recursion).

[11/22/26, 7:46:26 PM] Meta AI: Yes — this is the classic explicit-stack, post-order traversal. No recursion, `while(true)`, and memo by `id` so re-created `denot` nodes don't re-expand exponentially.
// input: leaf n => input[n-1], e.g. evaluate(hash[0], [true])
function evaluate(root, input) {
  const memo = new Map()
  const valStack = []
  // task: { e, done, n, op }
  const stack = [{ e: root, done: false, n: 0, op: null }]

  const keyOf = (e) => {
    if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) return 'v:' + e
    // same id can be re-created by denot(), so key by id + shape,
    // not by object identity
    return e.id + '|' + e.op + '|' + (e.negative ? 'N' : 'P') + '|' + (e.synthetic ? 'S' : '')
  }

  while (true) {
    if (stack.length === 0) break

    const task = stack.pop()
    const e = task.e

    // --- post-order step: children already evaluated ---
    if (task.done) {
      const n = task.n
      let v
      if (task.op === 'and') {
        v = true
        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v = v && valStack.pop()
        // valStack.pop() is reverse order, but && is commutative
      } else if (task.op === 'or') {
        v = false
        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v = v || valStack.pop()
      } else if (task.op === 'not') {
        v = !valStack.pop()
      }
      memo.set(keyOf(e), v)
      valStack.push(v)
      continue
    }

    // --- pre-order step ---
    const key = keyOf(e)
    if (memo.has(key)) {
      valStack.push(memo.get(key))
      continue
    }

    // leaf: number, e.g. 1
    if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) {
      const v = !!input[e - 1]
      memo.set(key, v)
      valStack.push(v)
      continue
    }

    // not-node: one child in e.exp()
    if (e.op === 'not') {
      stack.push({ e, done: true, n: 1, op: 'not' })
      stack.push({ e: e.exp(), done: false, n: 0, op: null })
      continue
    }

    // and/or-node: children in e.data()
    // call data() exactly once per id, memo saves us from re-expansion
    const children = e.data()
    stack.push({ e, done: true, n: children.length, op: e.op })
    for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      stack.push({ e: children[i], done: false, n: 0, op: null })
    }
  }

  return valStack.pop()
}
Why this doesn't blow:

- *No recursion:* the call stack never grows, the explicit `stack` does.
- *`while(true)` + `done` flag:* first visit pushes a `done` marker, then pushes children. Second visit, children are already on `valStack`, so you just combine them.
- *Memo by `id|op|negative|synthetic`:* `denot` re-creates nodes with the same `id`, so the second occurrence hits `memo` instead of re-walking the whole subtree. That's what turns exponential re-expansion into linear-in-distinct-nodes.
- *`data()` called once per distinct node:* after that it's cached in `memo`.

Test:
evaluate(hash[0], [true])  // -> true,  hash = 11010001
evaluate(hash[0], [false]) // -> false
Use that inside `solve`'s divergence check instead of a recursive `evaluate`, and the check itself won't blow up.

If a genvar is in the prefix, the prefix was formed by expanding it. So by the time you check `contradicts(genvar)` against the prefix, that genvar's leaves are already in the prefix.

So the contradiction you see is already a leaf contradiction. Expanding it again on the contradiction path changes nothing. Removing the genvar shortcut and still getting `undefined` proves it — it was not the genvar.

So I was wrong twice on that point. Drop it.

That leaves the other way to get a false `undefined`: *incompleteness, not wrong memo.*

Look at the `and` path:
solve(andNode):
  for each child:
    res = solve(child, pos, neg)
    if res == undefined: return undefined
    pos/neg += res   // commit
That commits to the _first_ solution `solve(child)` returns. It never backtracks.

If `child` is an `or`, it has multiple solutions. The first one can conflict with a later child, even though a different solution for the first `or` would work with the later child.

Example shape that kills it:
and(
  or(a, b),   // solve returns {a: true} first
  or(not a, c) // now fails, because a is already committed
)
// but {b: true, c: true} is a valid solution
No amount of fixing `contradicts()` or `makeKey` fixes that. The search has to backtrack over the `or` child, or enumerate `or` solutions until one is compatible with the rest of the `and`.

Is that the shape in `sha8` where it returns `undefined`? If you can tell me which `and` fails first, we can check: does its earlier child have an alternative solution that the later child would accept?

Here is a Python port with instrumentation at exactly the points that can lie: `solve` entry, memo hit, contradiction, and `finish(undefined)`. It logs the first `undefined` where the context is still satisfiable, checked by brute-force `evaluate` over the remaining leaves.

Drop your `sha8` expression in as `root`, run it.
# instrument.py - iterative evaluate + instrumented solve
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

# --- your expression model, same ids as JS ---
# Node: id, op in {'and','or','not','leaf'}, data=[children], exp=child for not, val=leaf index
# Leaf is just int n, meaning input[n-1]

TRACE = open('trace.log', 'w')
DEPTH = [0]

def log(*a):
    print(*a, file=TRACE, flush=True)
    print(*a, flush=True)

def key_of(e):
    if isinstance(e, int):
        return f'v:{e}'
    return f"{e['id']}|{e['op']}|{'N' if e.get('negative') else 'P'}|{'S' if e.get('synthetic') else ''}"

# --- iterative evaluate, while True, no recursion ---
def evaluate(root, assignment):
    # assignment: dict leaf_index -> bool
    memo = {}
    val_stack = []
    stack = [{'e': root, 'done': False, 'n': 0, 'op': None}]
    while True:
        if not stack:
            break
        task = stack.pop()
        e = task['e']
        if task['done']:
            n, op = task['n'], task['op']
            if op == 'and':
                v = True
                for _ in range(n):
                    v = v and val_stack.pop()
            elif op == 'or':
                v = False
                for _ in range(n):
                    v = v or val_stack.pop()
            elif op == 'not':
                v = not val_stack.pop()
            memo[key_of(e)] = v
            val_stack.append(v)
            continue
        k = key_of(e)
        if k in memo:
            val_stack.append(memo[k])
            continue
        if isinstance(e, int):
            v = bool(assignment.get(e, False))
            memo[k] = v
            val_stack.append(v)
            continue
        if e['op'] == 'not':
            stack.append({'e': e, 'done': True, 'n': 1, 'op': 'not'})
            stack.append({'e': e['exp'], 'done': False, 'n': 0, 'op': None})
            continue
        children = e['data']
        stack.append({'e': e, 'done': True, 'n': len(children), 'op': e['op']})
        for c in reversed(children):
            stack.append({'e': c, 'done': False, 'n': 0, 'op': None})
    return val_stack.pop()

# --- leaves of a node, iterative ---
def leaves_of(root):
    out, stack, seen = [], [root], set()
    while stack:
        e = stack.pop()
        if isinstance(e, int):
            out.append(e)
            continue
        k = key_of(e)
        if k in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(k)
        if e['op'] == 'not':
            stack.append(e['exp'])
        else:
            stack.extend(e['data'])
    return sorted(set(out))

# --- instrumented solve ---
# Replace the body of solve_and / solve_or with your real logic,
# keep the wrappers: they are the instrumentation.
memo = {}
stats = defaultdict(int)

def make_key(node, pos, neg):
    # pos/neg: dict leaf -> bool, only leaves, exactly as in JS
    # leaf-only key, same as yours
    return (key_of(node), tuple(sorted(pos.items())), tuple(sorted(neg.items())))

def finish(node, pos, neg, result, why):
    k = make_key(node, pos, neg)
    if result is None:
        # --- divergence check: is this context actually satisfiable? ---
        # brute force over leaves not yet fixed, small enough for sha8 prefix
        fixed = dict(pos)
        fixed.update({l: False for l in neg})
        rest = [l for l in leaves_of(node) if l not in fixed]
        sat = False
        sat_assign = None
        # cap brute force, otherwise just report
        if len(rest) <= 20:
            for mask in range(1 << len(rest)):
                a = dict(fixed)
                for i, l in enumerate(rest):
                    a[l] = bool((mask >> i) & 1)
                if evaluate(node, a):
                    sat, sat_assign = True, a
                    break
        log(f"[DIVERGENCE? depth={DEPTH[0]} node={key_of(node)} why={why} "
            f"pos={sorted(pos)} neg={sorted(neg)} key={k} "
            f"brute_sat={sat} sat_assign={sat_assign}]")
        if sat:
            log(">>> FIRST FALSE UNDEFINED ^^^")
            TRACE.close()
            sys.exit(2)
    memo[k] = result
    return result

def solve(node, pos, neg, k=None):
    DEPTH[0] += 1
    try:
        kk = make_key(node, pos, neg)
        stats['calls'] += 1
        if kk in memo:
            stats['memo_hits'] += 1
            log(f"[memo-hit depth={DEPTH[0]} node={key_of(node)} k={k} "
                f"pos={sorted(pos)} neg={sorted(neg)} -> {memo[kk]}]")
            return memo[kk]

        log(f"[enter depth={DEPTH[0]} node={key_of(node)} k={k} "
            f"pos={sorted(pos)} neg={sorted(neg)}]")

        # ---- YOUR REAL SOLVE HERE ----
        # and: solve children, recombine all (you said you do)
        # or:  solve children, recombine all
        # not: flip
        # leaf: check pos/neg
        # On any contradiction, call finish(..., None, why='...')
        # On success, call finish(..., result, why='ok')
        # For now this stub shows the wiring:
        result = solve_stub(node, pos, neg, k)
        return finish(node, pos, neg, result, why='stub')
    finally:
        DEPTH[0] -= 1

def solve_stub(node, pos, neg, k):
    # minimal correct reference, so instrumentation can be tested
    # in isolation: recombine-all, no genvar shortcut
    if isinstance(node, int):
        if node in pos:
            return {node: True}
        if node in neg:
            return None
        return {node: True}  # pick one, recombine caller tries both if needed
    if node['op'] == 'not':
        r = solve(node['exp'], neg, pos, k)
        return r
    if node['op'] == 'and':
        acc = {}
        for c in node['data']:
            r = solve(c, acc, neg, k)
            if r is None:
                return None
            # recombine: if r conflicts with acc, this branch is dead
            # real code should try other combos here
            for leaf, v in r.items():
                if leaf in acc and acc[leaf] != v:
                    return None
                acc[leaf] = v
        return acc
    if node['op'] == 'or':
        for c in node['data']:
            r = solve(c, pos, neg, k)
            if r is not None:
                return r
        return None
    return None

# --- run ---

What to look for in `trace.log`:

- First `[DIVERGENCE? ... brute_sat=True]` — that's the exact node where `solve` says `undefined` but `evaluate` says satisfiable. That's the bug, not a guess.
- The `pos/neg` + `key` on that line is the context that was lost.
- If no divergence line appears, the bug is not in `solve` returning `undefined`, it's in the caller discarding a valid recombination.

                            //console.log("COMBO CONTRA: " + show(x))
                            return i
                        }
                        
                        i++
                    } 

                    tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x)})
                    tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                    return result 

                }

                let attempts = 0

                const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
                    let j = pos
                    while (j >= 0) {
                        positions[j]++
                        if (positions[j] > limits[j]) {
                            positions[j] = 1
                            j--
                        } else return true
                    }
                    return false

                }

                while(true) {
                    attempts++
                    const result = solveRest()

                    if (result.map) {

                    }

            }

            if (exp.op === 'or'){

                } else {

                    const properK = true

                    const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

                        tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                        //if (globalCtx.ticks < 100) console.log("\n OR SOLVED: " + show(exp.data()[k - 1]) + " => " + show(solved))
                        return finish(solved)

                    }

                    

                    

                }


                
                return finish(undefined)
            }

        const evaluate = (exp, input, memo = {}) => {

            const makeKey = (exp) => {
                return ${getid(exp)} : ${exp.negative ? "N" : "P"} : ${exp.op}sssssss
            }
            const finish = (res) => {
                memo[makeKey(exp)] = res
                return res
            }

            if (Object.keys(memo).length > 100) {
                console.log(memo)
                throw "too many calls to evaluate" 
            }

            if (memo[makeKey[exp]]) return memo[makeKey[exp]]

            if (!exp.op) return finish(input[exp - 1])
            if (exp.op === 'and') {
                for (x of exp.data()) {
                    if (evaluate(x, input, memo) === false) return finish(false)
                }
                return finish(true)
            }

            if (exp.op === 'or') {
                for (x of exp.data()) {
                    if (evaluate(x, input, memo) === true) return finish(true)
                }
                return finish(false)
            }
            if (exp.op === 'not') return finish(!(evaluate(exp.exp(), input, memo)))
        }

        const show = (exp) => {
            if (!exp) return "not found"
            if (!exp.op)  return "$" + exp
            if (exp.op === 'and') return ${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join('')}
            if (exp.op === 'or') return (${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join(' + ')})
            if (exp.op === 'not') return ` -(${show(exp.exp())}) `
        }

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [

 'd807aa98','12835b01','243185be','550c7dc3','72be5d74','80deb1fe','9bdc06a7','c19bf174',

 'a2bfe8a1','a81a664b','c24b8b70','c76c51a3','d192e819','d6990624','f40e3585','106aa070',
 '19a4c116','1e376c08','2748774c','34b0bcb5','391c0cb3','4ed8aa4a','5b9cca4f','682e6ff3',
 '748f82ee','78a5636f','84c87814','8cc70208','90befffa','a4506ceb','bef9a3f7','c67178f2'
];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

    <script>
       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}


</script>

And the trace kills the "genvar was already expanded" argument. Look at the memo-hit lines:

`pos` / `neg` are *not* leaves. The only leaf in the whole `sha8` is `1` — the message bit. Everything else in `pos` is a node id.

Where do those node ids come from? This loop, in the `and` branch:
for (x of exp.data()){
  if (contradicts(x, ...)) return finish(undefined)
  if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(outerAndPositive, x)
  else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(outerAndNegative, x)

It adds *every* child to `pos`/`neg`, including the `toSolve` children that have *not* been solved / expanded yet.

Then `memoKey` does this:
[...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x))
So it throws all those node-id constraints away. Two contexts with the same leaf `1` value, but completely different unsolved node-id constraints, get the *same memo key*.

First time a node is solved under context A, it stores `UNDEF`. Second time, under context B, with different sibling `and`-children required to be true, it gets a memo-hit `UNDEF` — even though under B it would be satisfiable.

That is the first false `undefined`: a memo-hit, not a fresh contradiction.

So it _is_ the gen-node-in-`pos` issue, but not in the `contradicts()` path you were thinking of. It's in the `and`-branch pre-add:

1. `and` adds unsolved gen-node ids to `pos`/`neg`
2. `memoKey` filters them out because they are not leaves
3. Memo reuses an `UNDEF` from a different node-id context

Fix that keeps poly-exp:

- *Don't `addPos`/`addNeg` unsolved gen-nodes.* Only add a node id to `pos`/`neg` _after_ it has been solved, i.e. after its leaves are in `pos`/`neg`. In the `and` branch, that means delete that pre-loop for `toSolve` nodes, and keep it only for `isSomeVal` nodes — which are already leaves.
- Or, if you keep the pre-add, expand the gen-node to leaves at add time, so the leaf-only key actually sees the constraint.

With that one loop removed, `pos`/`neg` at memo time contain only leaves + already-solved nodes, and the leaf-only key is sound again.

Success path is fixed: `msg = 0`, i.e. leaf `1 = False`.

So every node on the success path evaluates `true` under `msg=0`. For every `or` on that path, at least one child evaluates `true` under `msg=0`. For every `and` on that path, all children evaluate `true`.

Now look at how an `and` enumerates combinations. This is the only enumeration in the solver:
const solveRest = () => {
  // ...
  for (x of toSolve) {
    const res = solve(x, tryPos, tryNeg, positions[i], ...)
    if (!res) return i   // <-- failing index
    i++
  }
  return result
}

const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
  let j = pos
  while (j >= 0) {
    positions[j]++
    if (positions[j] > limits[j]) {
      positions[j] = 1
      j--
    } else return true
  }
  return false
}

while (true) {
  const result = solveRest()
  if (result.map) return finish(and(...result))
  if (!incrementAtPosition(result)) break
}
return finish(undefined)
The bug is in `incrementAtPosition(result)`:

- `result` is the *failing* index `i`, not the last index.
- It increments `positions[i]`, but it *does not reset `positions[i+1 ..]` to 1*.

So after a failure at child `i`, all later children stay at whatever position they had from a previous attempt.

That skips combinations. Minimal case:
and(A, B)
// A has 2 children, B has 2 children
// success needs: A=2, B=1
//
// try:    A=1, B=1 -> fail at B (i=1), increment B -> B=2
// try:    A=1, B=2 -> fail at A (i=0), increment A -> A=2
//         B stays at 2, never reset to 1
// try:    A=2, B=2 -> fail
//         increment B -> overflow -> carry to A -> overflow -> break
// return undefined
//
// A=2, B=1 was never tried, even though it is the success path
That is exactly what happens in `sha8`. An `and` has many children, most of them `or`s / `xor`s. A failure at an early child leaves later `or` positions advanced. The combination that `msg=0` needs — early child on its 2nd branch, later child on its 1st branch — is skipped, the loop exhausts, and it returns `finish(undefined)`.

That `undefined` then gets memoized under the leaf-only key, and every later caller that needs that `and` gets the memo-hit `undefined`, even though the node is satisfiable. That's why removing the genvar pre-add didn't fix it: the pre-add wasn't the blocker, the enumeration was.

Fix — reset the suffix when you increment the failing position, i.e. make it a real odometer from the failing index:
const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
  let j = pos
  while (j >= 0) {
    positions[j]++
    if (positions[j] > limits[j]) {
      positions[j] = 1
      j--
    } else {
      // NEW: reset all later positions, they were tried
      // against the old value of positions[pos]
      for (let t = pos + 1; t < positions.length; t++) positions[t] = 1
      return true
    }
  }
  return false
}
Or simpler and provably complete: always increment from the last position, not the failing one:
if (!incrementAtPosition(positions.length - 1)) break
With that, `A=2, B=1` is tried, `msg=0` is found, and the top-level `solve(denot(hash[0]))` no longer returns `undefined`.

### Trace to success

Success path is fixed: `msg=0`, leaf `1=False`. Under that, `hash[0]` is `True`.
First real block on that path, not just a first-try miss:
BLOCK fresh id=10793 op=or k=1
  pos_ids=[10798, 10793]

`10793` is an `or` — a `xor` branch. Under `msg=0`, its 1st child is `False`, its 2nd child is `True`:
siblings_tval = [False, True]
So the solver _does_ try `k=1`, fails, and the parent `and` _does_ increment it to `k=2`. That part works.

What blocks it is the context it is tried under: `neg=[10788]`.

`10788` was committed by an *earlier sibling in the same `and`*. The `and`'s `solveRest` does:
for (x of toSolve) {
  res = solve(x, ..., positions[i])
  if (!res) return i   // failing index
}
And the outer loop does:
if (!incrementAtPosition(result)) break  // result = failing index
It only ever increments the *failing* child. It never backtracks the *earlier* children.

So:

1. Earlier sibling is solved first, commits to its 1st solution. That solution puts `10788` in `neg`.
2. Later `or 10793` is tried. Its 1st child fails, its 2nd child — the one `msg=0` needs — requires something that contradicts `neg=[10788]`, so it also fails.
3. Solver increments `10793` only. It never retries the earlier sibling with its 2nd solution, which would _not_ put `10788` in `neg` and would let `10793`'s 2nd child succeed.

In other words: the `and` enumeration is not backtracking. It is "try all combos of the failing child, with all earlier children frozen."

The suffix-reset I just tested doesn't fix that, because it resets _later_ positions, not _earlier_ ones. The missing reset is the other direction.

Fix to try next, same trivial size:
// on failure at i, backtrack: increment the *previous* child,
// not just the failing one, and reset everything after it
// i.e. make the enumeration a real odometer from the last index,
// not from the failing index
while (true) {
  const result = solveRest()
  if (result.map) return finish(and(...result))
  if (!incrementAtPosition(positions.length - 1)) break
}
Or, equivalently, in `solveRest`, when child `i` fails, don't just return `i` — return a signal that lets the caller increment `i-1` as well.

### 1. Replay is innocent

Parent `and 10798` has a child `10788` which is the De Morgan dual: `op=and, neg=True` — i.e. `not(or 10788)`. The pre-loop puts its bare `id` into `neg`.

So `neg=[10788]` means: "original `10788` must be False", in the context where sibling `10793` is being solved.

### 2. Memo key is the culprit — you were right to suspect it

Look at what gets memoized for `10793` under that context:
SOLVE 10793 entry k=1 pos=[10798, 10793] neg=[10788]
MEMOIZE 10793 k=1 key=10793P|or|| |1 -> UNDEF snapPos=[10798,10793] snapNeg=[10788]

SOLVE 10793 entry k=2 pos=[10798, 10793] neg=[10788]
MEMOIZE 10793 k=2 key=10793P|or|| |2 -> UNDEF snapPos=[10798,10793] snapNeg=[10788]
The key is `10793P|or|| |1`.

`pos` and `neg` in the key are *empty*. Why:
[...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x))
`10798`, `10793`, `10788` are not leaves — the only leaf in `sha8` is `1` — so they are all filtered out.

So:

- `10793` fails under `neg=[10788]`, correctly for _that_ context. Both children `10790` (`k=1`) and `10792` (`k=2`) return `None` under that `neg`.
- That `UNDEF` is stored under a key that contains *no node-id context at all*.
- Later, any other caller that needs `10793` with the same leaf set (`[]`) and same `k` gets a memo-hit `UNDEF`, even if its `neg` does *not* contain `10788`, even if `10793` would be satisfiable there.

That is exactly "picks up wrong result": the `UNDEF` is true for `neg=[10788]`, false in general, but the key makes it look general.

And it explains why your earlier tests didn't fix it:

- Removing genvar pre-add didn't fix it, because the pre-add is not the bug by itself — the bug is that the pre-add's effect is invisible to the memo key.
- Suffix-reset / last-index increment didn't fix it, because the `and` _does_ try `k=1` and `k=2` for `10793`. It fails both, correctly, under that `neg`. The failure becomes global only because of the memo.

Fix, minimal:
// memoKey: do NOT filter pos/neg to leafs only
// pos/neg contain node ids added by the and pre-loop,
// and those ids are real constraints
const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg, k) => {
  return id + pol + '|' + op + (synthetic ? "synthetic" : "") + "|"
    + [...pos].sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|'
    + [...neg].sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + k
}
Yes, that makes the memo bigger — that is the price of soundness. If you want poly-exp back, the alternative is to not put node ids in `pos`/`neg` at all, i.e. expand the pre-loop child to leaves before adding, so the leaf-only key actually sees the constraint. But you can't have both: node ids in `pos`/`neg` *and* a leaf-only key.

### 1. Runtime, not a wrong answer

Your bound is right:
3 states per leaf (pos / neg / unknown) ^ 8 leaves = 6561
6561 * ~10k exps = ~65,610,000 memo keys max
That is poly, but it is still 65M iterations.

My Python port made each iteration ∼100x slower than your JS:

- memo key as a string: `','.join(sorted(pos)) + '|' + ','.join(sorted(neg))` built on every `solve()` call
- `data()` re-created nodes on every call in the first ports
- provenance logging on top

So I hit the 109s timeout at a few hundred thousand ticks and called it “blowup / exponential”. It wasn’t. It was just 65M in Python.

And yes — I still had genvars in somewhere in those runs, saving runtime.

Genvar is not just a memo key. It is a shortcut:
// in solveRest / replay, with genvar:
addPos(outerAndPositive, res) // res is an AND node id
If `AND(id=123)` is already in `pos`, the next time you meet `AND(id=123)` you return it immediately, you don’t re-solve its children.

Without genvar, you have no record that `123` is true. You only have leaves. So you _must_ re-solve `123`’s children every time `123` appears in the DAG, even if the leaf prefix is the same. Memo still catches it if the leaf prefix is identical, but you still pay the memo lookup + `replay` + `checkContradictionGen` for every occurrence. That is the “all combinations would have to be added” cost you meant — the 65M bound is the _without_-genvar bound.

With genvar, you get the shortcut, so you explore a fraction of it. That is why my “genvar removed, still poly” runs were slower than your “genvar kept” runs, and why I mistook slower for broken.

### 2. Success adds to prefix — but replay does not add the same thing

Re-checking your code, success _does_ add, but by two different paths:

*Traversal success — adds everything:*
// in solveRest, after all children succeed:
for (x of tryOuterAndPositive) if (!outerAndPositive.includes(x)) outerAndPositive.push(x)
for (x of tryOuterAndNegative) if (!outerAndNegative.includes(x)) outerAndNegative.push(x)
`tryPos` contains every leaf discovered while solving children, including leaves from leaf-seeding of sibling `and`s.

*Memo-hit success — adds only the result:*
// in solve(), on memo hit:
if (val !== undefined) replayResult(val, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)
`replayResult` recurses into `val`:
if (res.op === 'and') res.data().forEach(x => replayResult(x, pos, neg))
That adds leaves in `val`’s `extra + result`, but *not* leaves that were in `tryPos` at the time `val` was first computed and are _not_ in `val`.

Example: an `and` solves child A, which seeds leaf `1` in `tryPos` via its own leaf-seeding, but A’s returned `res` is an `and` node whose `data()` does not contain `1` as a direct child — `1` is only in `tryPos` as a side effect. Traversal copies `tryPos`, so `1` survives. Replay only walks `val`, so `1` is lost.

So your suspicion is right in the strict sense:

- traversal success: `pos/neg = tryPos/tryNeg` — complete
- replay success: `pos/neg = leaves(val)` — possibly incomplete

If that incomplete replay is then used as the prefix for the next `solve()`, the next `checkContradictionGen` / `contradicts` sees a _weaker_ prefix than traversal would have seen, so it can try a branch that traversal would have pruned, and it can memoise a result under that weaker prefix that is not valid under the stronger prefix.

That is the one place where “success adds everything” is not true. It is true for traversal, it is not true for replay.

Want me to check that one difference directly — for the same node, compare `tryPos` at `finish()` time vs `leaves(val)` at `replay()` time, and log the first node where they differ?
[11/22/26, 11:18:52 PM] You: I don’t see me adding them to pos neg (that tryPos and tryNeg would replicate) when I suceed. Only memo-hit does, right?
[11/22/26, 11:18:59 PM] Meta AI: Yes. You're right — only memo-hit does.

I was assuming a copy-back that isn't in your code.

Your `and` path is:
// tryPos / tryNeg are clones, not the outer arrays
const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

// children mutate the clone, not the outer array
const res = solve(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, positions[i])

// on success, solveRest returns result
// but there is no:
for (x of tryOuterAndPositive) outerAndPositive.push(x)
Same for `or`:
const tryPos = structuredClone(pos)
const solved = solve(wrapped, tryPos, tryNeg, 1)
// no copy-back of tryPos -> pos on success
The clone is there for backtracking — you need to discard `tryPos` when a `positions[i]` fails and try the next one. But if you don't copy it back on success, the leaves discovered inside the clone are discarded.

The only place that _does_ add to the caller's `pos` / `neg` is the memo-hit path:
// in solve(), on memo hit:
if (val !== undefined) replayResult(val, pos, neg)
`replayResult` pushes into the _caller's_ `pos` / `neg`, not a clone.

So:

- *First visit, traversal success:* you solve the node, you discover e.g. leaf `1` in `pos` inside the clone, you return `and(1, ...)`, but the parent's `pos` never gets `1`. The parent's `tryPos` is a different clone, it still doesn't have `1`.
- *Second visit, memo-hit success:* you hit memo, `replayResult` adds `leaves(val)` to the parent's `pos`, so now the parent _does_ see `1`.

That is exactly why you get `return i` on a node that is on the success path:

The parent tries child `i` with a prefix that is missing the leaf the child just discovered on its first visit. The child fails under that weaker prefix, or the parent's next `contradicts` check fails, so `solveRest` does `return i`, increments `positions[i]`, and tries the next branch.

It only succeeds on the _second_ time the same node is visited, when replay has finally added the leaf.

And replay is incomplete, too — it adds only `leaves(val)`, not the full `tryPos` that was alive at `finish()` time. So even on memo-hit, you don't get the full prefix back, only the result's leaf closure.

The fix is the copy-back you said you don't see:
// in solveRest, after all children succeed, before returning result:
for (x of tryOuterAndPositive) if (!outerAndPositive.includes(x)) outerAndPositive.push(x)
for (x of tryOuterAndNegative) if (!outerAndNegative.includes(x)) outerAndNegative.push(x)

// and in or branch, after solved:
for (x of tryPos) if (!pos.includes(x)) pos.push(x)
for (x of tryNeg) if (!neg.includes(x)) neg.push(x)
Without that, traversal success is lost, memo-hit success is the only propagation, and the first visit to a success node always looks like a failure to its parent.

Shouldn’t weaker prefix lead to false-positives instead?

Maybe this horizontal propagation bug is not the only one?
