       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}

[11/23/26, 3:21:15 AM] Meta AI: Right. Replay doesn't fix soundness, because replay only replays the *result*, not the *side-effects*.

Your `solve` has two outputs:

1. `return value` — the expression it found
2. mutation of `outerAndPositive / outerAndNegative` — all the genvars / node-ids it learned were forced while solving

`replayResult` only restores (1). It loses (2).

Example of where it breaks:
solve(and(A, B)) 
  -> solves A, learns `X = true` as a side-effect, X not in final result
  -> solves B, uses X
  -> returns and(...result...)
  -> memoize(and(A,B), snap, result)
On a memo hit later:
memo hit -> replayResult(result)
-> pushes only literals in result
-> X is NOT restored
Now the caller thinks `X` is still free, picks `not(X)` in another branch, and you get a "solution" that contradicts the first branch. That's exactly the `1 out of 3 correct` pattern — the other 2 are combinations of branches that were never simultaneously satisfiable, they just look satisfiable because the learned fact was dropped.

Two other holes in the same code make it worse:

*1. Memo key drops non-leaf assignments:*
[...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x))
`pos / neg` also contain node-ids — `or` / `and` nodes forced true via `addPos / addNeg`. You filter them out, so two calls with same leaf assignment but different forced-node assignment collide on the same key. That's a false hit.

*2. Type mixing in `pos / neg`:*

- leaf: you push `exp` — a number
- node: you push `exp.id` — a number, but from a different namespace
- in `replayResult` for `or`: you push `res.id`
- in `checkContradiction`: you compare `getid(exp) === x`

`getid` vs raw push vs `includes` don't agree everywhere, so `contradicts()` can miss a contradiction that replay was supposed to restore.

### Fix

Don't try to patch replay. Make `solve` pure:
solve(exp, pos, neg, k) -> { value, posDelta, negDelta }
Memoize the triple:
memo[key] = { value, posDelta, negDelta }
On hit, apply *all three*. No mutation of the caller's arrays inside `solve`, no `replayResult` guessing what was learned.

Until you store the delta, replay will always be unsound — the result is not the proof, the learned assignments are.

[11/23/26, 3:23:20 AM] Meta AI: Because `finish` replays into the *local* arrays, but `memoize` only stores `r`.

Those are two different things.

Look at what happens on first computation:
solve(exp, outerPos, outerNeg)
  snap = [...outerPos]           // before
  // ... solving mutates outerPos ...
  // outerPos now = snap + delta
  // delta = all learned facts, not just literals in r
  finish(r):
    memoize(exp, snap, r)        // stores ONLY r
    replayResult(r, outerPos)    // replays r into outerPos, which ALREADY has delta
    return r
`replayResult(r, outerPos)` there is a no-op. `outerPos` already contains `delta`, because you just solved it in-place. Replaying `r` adds nothing new.

Now on a later hit:
memo hit -> value = r
replayResult(r, outerPos2)  // outerPos2 = snap2, NOT snap + delta
You try to reconstruct `delta` from `r` alone. You can't, because:
delta != literals(r)
`delta` contains intermediate learns: e.g. in `and(A,B)` you solved `A`, learned `X = true`, used `X` to solve `B`, but `X` is not in the final `and(...result...)`. It was a stepping-stone.

On first call, `X` was in `outerPos` because of mutation. On second call, `X` is gone, because you only stored `r`, and `r` doesn't mention `X`.

Same for `undefined`:
if (contradicts(...)) return finish(undefined)
`replayResult(undefined)` does nothing, but solving to `undefined` _did_ mutate `outerPos/Neg` before failing. That mutation is also lost. A later hit returns `undefined` without restoring the contradiction context that made it `undefined`.

So:

- `finish` + `replay` fixes the *current* caller, because that caller already has the mutations.
- It does *not* fix the *future* caller, because the memo never saw the mutations.

To fix it you have to memoize the delta itself:
const finish = (r) => {
  const deltaPos = outerPos.filter(x => !snapPos.includes(x))
  const deltaNeg = outerNeg.filter(x => !snapNeg.includes(x))
  memoize(exp, snapPos, snapNeg, k, { r, deltaPos, deltaNeg })
  return r
}
Then on hit, replay `deltaPos / deltaNeg`, not `r`.

// ---------- brute force check ----------
function bruteSat(exp, vars) {
  const n = vars.length
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
    const input = []
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) input[i] = ((mask >> (n-1-i)) & 1) === 1
    // evaluate() in your code expects input[exp-1], and memo is buggy, so use fresh memo
    try { if (evaluate(exp, input, {}) === true) return { sat: true, input } } catch(e) {}
  }
  return { sat: false }
}

function checkOne(name, exp, vars) {
  const ctxBefore = globalCtx
  // fresh memo per test, otherwise cross-test pollution hides the bug
  globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.hits = 0; globalCtx.ticks = 0
  let sol
  try { sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0) } catch(e) { console.log(name, "THREW", e); return }
  const brute = bruteSat(exp, vars)

  if (sol === undefined) {
    if (brute.sat) console.log(`❌ ${name} FALSE NEGATIVE: solve=undef but SAT with`, brute.input)
    else console.log(`✅ ${name} OK UNSAT`)
    return
  }
  // build assignment from solution: solutionToNum style, but check directly
  // solution is an and(...) of literals, extract them
  const assign = {}
  const collect = (e) => {
    if (!e) return
    if (!e.op) assign[e] = true
    else if (e.op === 'not') assign[e.exp()] = false
    else if (e.op === 'and') e.data().forEach(collect)
    else if (e.op === 'or') { /* or in solution = node id, ignore */ }
  }
  collect(sol)
  // fill unassigned with false, evaluate
  const input = vars.map(v => assign[v] === true)
  // if solution didn't assign a var, try both completions
  let ok = false
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << vars.length); mask++) {
    const inp = vars.map((v,i) => assign[v] !== undefined ? assign[v] : ((mask>>i)&1)===1)
    try { if (evaluate(exp, inp, {}) === true) { ok = true; break } } catch(e) {}
  }
  if (!ok) console.log(`❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve returned`, show(sol), "but no completion satisfies")
  else if (!brute.sat) console.log(`❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve SAT but brute UNSAT`)
  else console.log(`✅ ${name} OK SAT`)
}

{

[11/23/26, 3:41:47 AM] Meta AI: That's the key finding. If it fails with `hit && false`, memo was never the root cause. Memo just made it fail _faster_.

The base `solve` is unsound on its own. And the reason is the same as before, just without memo:

*It mutates `outerAndPositive / outerAndNegative` in place, and never rolls back on failure.*

Look at the `and` branch:
// mutates caller's arrays, before any search
for (x of exp.data()){
  if (contradicts(x, outer...)) return finish(undefined)
  if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(outerAndPositive, x)
  else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(outerAndNegative, x)
}

// ... try combinations, all fail ...
return finish(undefined)  // outer is STILL mutated
If that `and` fails, the caller still sees those `addPos / addNeg` facts as if they were true. They weren't — they were only true _under the assumption that this `and` was true_. You just proved that assumption is false, but you left the facts in.

Same in `solveRest`:
tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => { if (!outer...) outer.push(x) })
That's only on success, good. But the pre-loop above runs before `solveRest`, and it pollutes `outer` even on failure.

And the leaf / `not` cases do the same:
if (!exp.op) {
  if (neg has exp) return finish(undefined)
  outerAndPositive.push(exp)  // no rollback if caller later backtracks
  return finish(exp)
}
In a backtracking search, a failed branch must leave *zero* side-effects. Yours leaves all of them. So the next sibling branch starts with a polluted context:

- *False positive:* sibling thinks `a = true` from failed branch, picks `b = false` that only works with `a = true`, returns a "solution" that doesn't satisfy the original formula.
- *False negative:* sibling thinks `a = true` from failed branch, sees `not(a)` in its own clause, reports contradiction, even though `a` was never forced.

That's why you see both directions with memo off.

### Fix that actually fixes it

Don't mutate the caller's arrays at all. Snapshot / restore:
const solve = (exp, pos, neg, k) => {
  const myPos = [...pos]
  const myNeg = [...neg]
  // ... work ONLY on myPos / myNeg ...
  // on success: return { value, pos: myPos, neg: myNeg }
  // on failure: return undefined, caller keeps its own pos/neg untouched
}
No `finish` that mutates, no `replayResult`, no `structuredClone` of `outer` inside `solveRest` to patch it up after.

If you do that, the fuzz test with `hit && false` should go to zero failures. _Then_ you can turn memo back on — and memo must store the same `{value, posDelta, negDelta}` triple, not just `value`.

Top-level `or` gets that iteration for free, because `k === undefined` wraps it as `syntheticAnd` and goes through the `and` branch.

Nested `or` does *not*. Any `or` reached via `checkContradictionGen` is solved with `k = 1` only. First child fails → whole `or` returns `undefined`, even if child 2, 3, ... would succeed.

That's a pure incompleteness bug, no memo, no genvars needed.

### Minimal repro
const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
const a = v(ctx), b = v(ctx)

  or( and(a, not(a)), b ),
  b
))

The inner `or` is reached via `checkContradictionGen` → `solve(..., 1)`. It tries `and(a, not(a))`, fails, gives up. It never tries `b`.

That's your false negative.

False positives come from the mirror side: when that same `k=1` path _does_ succeed, it succeeds under a `pos/neg` that was built for child 1 only. The caller in the `and` branch then assumes that success is valid for the whole `or`, and merges it with the other `and` children. If child 1's success relied on a fact that contradicts another `and` child, you get a combined "solution" that was never jointly satisfiable — because you never tried the other `k`s that would have been compatible.

### What to add

Don't hardcode `1`. `checkContradictionGen` / the `or` branch has to try _all_ `k`:
const checkContradictionGen = (exp, pos, neg, nesting) => {
  if (contradicts(exp, pos, neg)) return undefined
  if (exp.op === 'or') {
    for (let k = 1; k <= exp.data().length; k++) {
      const res = solve(exp, [...pos], [...neg], k, nesting+1)
      if (res) return res
    }
    return undefined
  }
  return solve(exp, pos, neg, undefined, nesting+1)
}
Or simpler: never call `solve` with a fixed `k` from `checkContradictionGen` — call it with `k = undefined` and let the `or` → `syntheticAnd` → `and` iteration handle the `k` loop in one place.

Once you add that loop, the fuzz case above should pass with memo off, genvars off, everything off.

[11/23/26, 3:56:55 AM] You: <image omitted>
[11/23/26, 3:56:58 AM] Meta AI: This one is not a solver bug. It's a checker bug — and it's a good catch, because it proves the fuzz was lying to you.

Look at the case by hand:

*EXP:* `(¬$1 ∨ $1) ∧ (¬$1 ∨ $2) ∧ ($1 ∨ ¬$2)`
*SOL:* `¬$1, ¬$1, ¬$2` — i.e. `$1=false, $2=false`

Truth table for that assignment:

- `¬$1 ∨ $1` = `true ∨ false` = *true*
- `¬$1 ∨ $2` = `true ∨ false` = *true*
- `$1 ∨ ¬$2` = `false ∨ true` = *true*

All three clauses true. So `EXP` *is SAT*, and `SOL` *does satisfy it*. `BRUTE {sat: false}` is wrong.

Your `bruteSat` uses the old `evaluate()` from the file, and that `evaluate()` is not trustworthy for `denot()` output:
const makeKey = (exp) => `${getid(exp)} : ${exp.negative ? "N" : "P"} : ${exp.op}sssssss`
if (memo[makeKey[exp]]) return memo[makeKey[exp]]  // makeKey[exp] is undefined, memo never hits / collides
Plus it shares one `memo` across the whole recursion and bails with `throw "too many calls"` past 100 entries, which `bruteSat` swallows with `catch(e){}` and treats as `false`. So a SAT assignment that throws inside `evaluate` gets counted as UNSAT.

Don't use `evaluate()` to check `solve()`. Use a checker with no memo, no `negative` flag, no shared state:
function evalPure(exp, input) {
  if (!exp.op) return input[exp - 1]
  if (exp.op === 'not') return !evalPure(exp.exp(), input)
  if (exp.op === 'and') return exp.data().every(x => evalPure(x, input))
  if (exp.op === 'or') return exp.data().some(x => evalPure(x, input))
  throw "unknown op " + exp.op
}

function bruteSatPure(exp, vars) {
  const n = vars.length
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
    const input = []
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) input[i] = ((mask >> (n-1-i)) & 1) === 1
    if (evalPure(exp, input) === true) return { sat: true, input }
  }
  return { sat: false }
}

        function evaluate(root, input) {
            const memo = new Map()
            const valStack = []
            // task: { e, done, n, op }
            const stack = [{ e: root, done: false, n: 0, op: null }]

            const keyOf = (e) => {
                if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) return 'v:' + e
                // same id can be re-created by denot(), so key by id + shape,
                // not by object identity
                return e.id + '|' + e.op + '|' + (e.negative ? 'N' : 'P') + '|' + (e.synthetic ? 'S' : '')
            }

            while (true) {
                if (stack.length === 0) break

                const task = stack.pop()
                const e = task.e

                // --- post-order step: children already evaluated ---
                if (task.done) {
                const n = task.n
                let v
                if (task.op === 'and') {
                    v = true
                    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v = v && valStack.pop()
                    // valStack.pop() is reverse order, but && is commutative
                } else if (task.op === 'or') {
                    v = false
                    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v = v || valStack.pop()
                } else if (task.op === 'not') {
                    v = !valStack.pop()
                }
                memo.set(keyOf(e), v)
                valStack.push(v)
                continue
                }

                // --- pre-order step ---
                const key = keyOf(e)
                if (memo.has(key)) {
                valStack.push(memo.get(key))
                continue
                }

                // leaf: number, e.g. 1
                if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) {
                const v = !!input[e - 1]
                memo.set(key, v)
                valStack.push(v)
                continue
                }

                // not-node: one child in e.exp()
                if (e.op === 'not') {
                stack.push({ e, done: true, n: 1, op: 'not' })
                stack.push({ e: e.exp(), done: false, n: 0, op: null })
                continue
                }

                // and/or-node: children in e.data()
                // call data() exactly once per id, memo saves us from re-expansion
                const children = e.data()
                stack.push({ e, done: true, n: children.length, op: e.op })
                for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
                stack.push({ e: children[i], done: false, n: 0, op: null })
                }
            }

            return valStack.pop()
            }

        const show = (exp) => {
            if (!exp) return "not found"
            if (!exp.op)  return "$" + exp
            if (exp.op === 'and') return ${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join('')}
            if (exp.op === 'or') return (${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join(' + ')})
            if (exp.op === 'not') return ` -(${show(exp.exp())}) `
        }

        // ---------- brute force check ----------
function bruteSat(exp, vars) {
  const n = vars.length
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
    const input = []
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) input[i] = ((mask >> (n-1-i)) & 1) === 1
    // evaluate() in your code expects input[exp-1], and memo is buggy, so use fresh memo
    try { if (evaluate(exp, input, {}) === true) return { sat: true, input } } catch(e) {}
  }
  return { sat: false }
}

function checkOne(name, exp, vars) {
  const ctxBefore = globalCtx
  // fresh memo per test, otherwise cross-test pollution hides the bug
  globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.hits = 0; globalCtx.ticks = 0
  let sol
  try { sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0) } catch(e) { console.log(name, "THREW", e); return }
  const brute = bruteSat(exp, vars)

  if (sol === undefined) {
    if (brute.sat) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE NEGATIVE: solve=undef but SAT with, brute.input)
    else console.log(✅ ${name} OK UNSAT)
    return
  }
  // build assignment from solution: solutionToNum style, but check directly
  // solution is an and(...) of literals, extract them
  const assign = {}
  const collect = (e) => {
    if (!e) return
    if (!e.op) assign[e] = true
    else if (e.op === 'not') assign[e.exp()] = false
    else if (e.op === 'and') e.data().forEach(collect)
    else if (e.op === 'or') { /* or in solution = node id, ignore */ }
  }
  collect(sol)
  // fill unassigned with false, evaluate
  const input = vars.map(v => assign[v] === true)
  // if solution didn't assign a var, try both completions
  let ok = false
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << vars.length); mask++) {
    const inp = vars.map((v,i) => assign[v] !== undefined ? assign[v] : ((mask>>i)&1)===1)
    try { if (evaluate(exp, inp, {}) === true) { ok = true; break } } catch(e) {}
  }
  if (!ok) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve returned, show(sol), "but no completion satisfies")
  else if (!brute.sat) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve SAT but brute UNSAT)
  else console.log(✅ ${name} OK SAT)
}

// ---------- concrete small cases ----------
{
  const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
  const a = v(ctx), b = v(ctx), c = v(ctx)

  // UNSAT: all 4 combos of a,b forbidden
  // (a|b) & (!a|b) & (a|!b) & (!a|!b)
  const unsat = and(or(a,b), or(not(a), b), or(a, not(b)), or(not(a), not(b)))
  checkOne("unsat-2var", denot(unsat), [a,b])

  // SAT, but requires learning: (a|b) & (!a)  => must pick b
  const sat1 = and(or(a,b), not(a))
  checkOne("sat-requires-b", denot(sat1), [a,b])

  // Shared subexpression, solved twice under different outer context
  // This is the delta-loss case: first solve learns something, second reuses memo
  const shared = or(a, b)
  const shared2 = and(shared, or(not(a), c), or(not(b), not(c)), shared)
  checkOne("shared-or", denot(shared2), [a,b,c])

  // AND where intermediate learn is not in final result:
  // (a|b) & (!a|c) & (!b|c) & (!c)  => UNSAT, needs to propagate c=false -> a=false,b=false -> (a|b) fails
  // If delta (c=false) is lost on replay, solver can claim (a|b) SAT
  const unsat2 = and(or(a,b), or(not(a), c), or(not(b), c), not(c))
  checkOne("unsat-propagate-c", denot(unsat2), [a,b,c])
}

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [
 '428a2f98','71374491','b5c0fbcf','e9b5dba5','3956c25b','59f111f1','923f82a4','ab1c5ed5',
 'd807aa98','12835b01','243185be','550c7dc3','72be5d74','80deb1fe','9bdc06a7','c19bf174',
 'e49b69c1','efbe4786','0fc19dc6','240ca1cc','2de92c6f','4a7484aa','5cb0a9dc','76f988da',
 '983e5152','a831c66d','b00327c8','bf597fc7','c6e00bf3','d5a79147','06ca6351','14292967',
 '27b70a85','2e1b2138','4d2c6dfc','53380d13','650a7354','766a0abb','81c2c92e','92722c85',
 'a2bfe8a1','a81a664b','c24b8b70','c76c51a3','d192e819','d6990624','f40e3585','106aa070',
 '19a4c116','1e376c08','2748774c','34b0bcb5','391c0cb3','4ed8aa4a','5b9cca4f','682e6ff3',
 '748f82ee','78a5636f','84c87814','8cc70208','90befffa','a4506ceb','bef9a3f7','c67178f2'
];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

const formAst = () => {
    // ---------- Fixed shift / rotate, your shiftArray had a bug ----------

    // arr is MSB first, length 32. shr fills with zero, rotr wraps.

    const notArrays = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x));

    const shrArrays = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {

        const z = zero(templateVar);
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };

    const rotrArrays = (arr, k) => {

        return [...arr.slice(32 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };



    // ---------- Addition, 2-bit full adder ----------

    // a + b + carry_in = 0..3, needs 2 bits: [carry_out, sum]

    const addBit = (a, b, carry_in) => {

        const aXorB = xor(a, b);
        const sum = xor(aXorB, carry_in);
        const carry_out = or(and(a, b), and(carry_in, aXorB));
        return [carry_out, sum];

    };



    const addArrays = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const out = new Array(32);
        let carry = zero(templateVar);

        for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry);
            out[i] = sum;
            carry = carry_out;
        }

        return out; // mod 2^32, final carry dropped

    };



    const addManyArrays = (...arrs) => {
        let acc = arrs[0];
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays(acc, arrs[k]);
        return acc;
    };



    const Ch = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays(x), z));
    };

    const Maj = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z));
    };

    const Sigma0 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 2), rotrArrays(x, 13)), rotrArrays(x, 22));

    const Sigma1 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 6), rotrArrays(x, 11)), rotrArrays(x, 25));

    const sigma0 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 7), rotrArrays(x, 18)), shrArrays(x, 3, templateVar));

    const sigma1 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 17), rotrArrays(x, 19)), shrArrays(x, 10, templateVar));



    const H_HEX = [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19];

    // messageBits: Array<expr> length L, MSB first

    // returns Array<expr> length 256, MSB first

    const sha256DSLFromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

        const L = messageBits.length;

        // ---------- Padding ----------

        // append 1, then k zeros, then L as 64-bit big-endian

        const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)];

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar));

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 64, templateVar));

        // ---------- Initial H ----------

        let H = H_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));

        const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));


        // ---------- Process each 512-bit chunk ----------

        const numChunks = padded.length / 512;

        for (let c = 0; c < numChunks; c++) {

            const chunk = padded.slice(c * 512, (c + 1) * 512);

            // W[0..15]

            const W = [];

            for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));

            // W[16..63]

            for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays(sigma1(W[t - 2], templateVar), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15], templateVar), W[t - 16]));

            }



            // Working vars

            let a = H[0], b = H[1], c2 = H[2], d = H[3];

            let e = H[4], f = H[5], g = H[6], h = H[7];



            // 64 rounds

            for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {

                const T1 = addManyArrays(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
                const T2 = addManyArrays(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c2));

                h = g;
                g = f;
                f = e;
                e = addArrays(d, T1, templateVar);
                d = c2;
                c2 = b;
                b = a;
                a = addArrays(T1, T2, templateVar);

            }



            // H = H + working vars

            H[0] = addArrays(H[0], a, templateVar);
            H[1] = addArrays(H[1], b, templateVar);
            H[2] = addArrays(H[2], c2, templateVar);
            H[3] = addArrays(H[3], d, templateVar);
            H[4] = addArrays(H[4], e, templateVar);
            H[5] = addArrays(H[5], f, templateVar);
            H[6] = addArrays(H[6], g, templateVar);
            H[7] = addArrays(H[7], h, templateVar);

        }



        // ---------- Output: concat H ----------

        return appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(H[0], H[1]), appendArrays(H[2], H[3])),  appendArrays(appendArrays(H[4], H[5]), appendArrays(H[6], H[7]))), []).slice(0, 256);

    };

        return { messageVars, hash };

    // Keeps your sha256DSLFromBits shape, just smaller

    const sha256DSL8FromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const L = messageBits.length

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)]

            d = c2
            c2 = b
            b = a
            a = addArrays8(T1, T2, templateVar)

        }

        // H = H + a, 8-bit output

        return addArrays8(H, a, templateVar)
    }

    const sha256DSL8 = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)

        const hash = sha256DSL8FromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar, rounds)

        return { messageVars, hash }

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}

The new `evaluate` has one suspect left: the memo key.
const keyOf = (e) => e.id + '|' + e.op + '|' + (e.negative ? 'N' : 'P') + '|' + (e.synthetic ? 'S' : '')
`denot()` re-uses the _same_ `id` for different shapes — e.g. a synthetic `not` gets `id = leaf id`, a De Morgan `and` gets `id = original or id`. If two different sub-expressions collide on that key, the second one returns the first one's cached value, and `evaluate` lies.

`bruteSat` hides that, because it does:
try { if (evaluate(...) === true) return ... } catch(e) {}
Any throw / wrong cached value for the one SAT mask just gets skipped and counted as UNSAT.

What you're looking for:

- If a single clause already returns `false` for both `[false,false,false]` and `[true,true,true]`, that clause is the bug. A 2-literal `or` can never be `false` for both unless its children are both evaluating to `false`.
- If all clauses are `true` individually but the top `and` is `false`, the bug is in the `and` handling in `evaluate` — the `valStack` popping.

My bet, from the code you pasted, is the second one — the `valStack` / memo interaction in the iterative `evaluate`:
const keyOf = (e) => e.id + '|' + e.op + '|' + (e.negative ? 'N' : 'P') + '|' + (e.synthetic ? 'S' : '')
`denot()` reuses the same `id` for different shapes. A synthetic `not` gets `id = leaf id`, a De Morgan `and` gets `id = original or id`. If two different nodes collide on that key, the second one gets the first one's cached value, and the parent `and` pops a wrong value.

[11/23/26, 4:06:50 AM] You: Can you reproduce evaluate in Python and find a bug?
[11/23/26, 4:06:53 AM] Meta AI: Found it. Reproduced in Python — same bug, same `false` for all 8 masks, even with memo off.

The bug is not the memo. It's this, in the `done` branch of `evaluate`:
} else if (task.op === 'or') {
  v = false
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v = v || valStack.pop()
} else if (task.op === 'and') {
  v = true
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v = v && valStack.pop()
}
`||` and `&&` *short-circuit* in JS — and in Python, same thing. If `v` is already `true` for an `or`, `valStack.pop()` on the right side *never runs*. If `v` is already `false` for an `and`, same.

So the stack is not cleaned up. The leftover values pollute the parent.

Trace for your trial, input `[false,false,false]`:

- Clause 1 → `true`, Clause 2 → `true`, stack = `[true, true]`
- Clause 3 `( $1 + -($2) )`: children are `$1=false`, `not($2)=true`
- `DONE or` for clause 3: `before = [true, true, false, true]`
- It should pop *2* values: `true` and `false` → `true`
- But: first pop → `v = false || true = true`. Second iteration: `v` is already `true`, so `v || valStack.pop()` short-circuits — *pop never happens*
- `after_pop = [true, true, false]` — one stale `false` left behind
- Then `DONE and` pops 3 values from `[true, true, false, true]` → it pops `true`, `false`, `true` → `true && false && true = false`

That's why every mask returns `false`: any `or` that becomes `true` early leaves garbage on the stack, and the top `and` then eats that garbage.

### Fix

Pop first, combine second — so the pop always runs:
if (task.op === 'and') {
  v = true
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const x = valStack.pop()
    v = v && x
  }
} else if (task.op === 'or') {
  v = false
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const x = valStack.pop()
    v = v || x
  }
}
`const x = valStack.pop()` is evaluated unconditionally, then `v && x` / `v || x` has no side effect to skip.

With that one change, the Python reproduction gives:

- `[false,false,false]` → `true`
- `[true,true,false]` → `true`
- `[true,true,true]` → `true`
- the other 5 masks → `false`

Which is exactly right for `(¬a∨a) ∧ (¬a∨b) ∧ (a∨¬b)`. And `bruteSat` stops reporting your solver's correct `¬$1, ¬$2` solution as a false positive.

Your `solve` was right on trial 4. The checker was lying because of short-circuit `pop()`.

const UNDEF = "__UNDEF__"
const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg, k) => {
  const id = exp.op ? exp.id : exp
  const pol = exp.op ? (exp.negative ? 'N' : 'P') : 'V'
  return id + pol + '|' + (exp.op ?? "v") + (exp.synthetic ? "synthetic" : "") + "|" + [...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + [...neg].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + k
}
const memoized = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k) => {
  if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
  if (!globalCtx.hits) globalCtx.hits = 0
  const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k)
  if (key in globalCtx.memo) {
    const stored = globalCtx.memo[key]
    globalCtx.hits++
    return { hit: true, value: stored === UNDEF ? undefined : stored }
  }
  return { hit: false }
}
const memoize = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, result) => {
  if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
  const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k)
  globalCtx.memo[key] = (result === undefined ? UNDEF : result)
  return result
}
const replayResult = (res, pos, neg) => {
  if (res === undefined) return
  if (!res.op) { if (!pos.includes(res)) pos.push(res); return }
  if (res.op === 'not') { const vv = res.exp(); if (!neg.includes(vv)) neg.push(vv); return }
  if (res.op === 'and') { res.data().forEach(x => replayResult(x, pos, neg)); return }
  if (!pos.includes(res.id)) pos.push(res.id)
}

<script>
const syntheticNot = exp => ({ negative: true, op: "not", id: exp.id ?? exp, exp: () => exp })
const syntheticAnd = exp => ({ synthetic: true, negative: exp.negative, op: "and", id: exp.id ?? exp, data: () => [exp] })
const syntheticOr = exp => ({ synthetic: true, negative: exp.negative, op: "or", id: exp.id ?? exp, data: () => [exp] })
const makeNode = (op, negative, id, data) => {
  const opposite = op === 'and' ? 'or' : 'and'
  const wrapped = data().map(x => {
    if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === op) return { synthetic: true, negative: false, op: opposite, id: x.id, data: () => [x] }
    return x
  })
  return { negative, op, id, data: () => wrapped }
}
const denot = (exp) => {
  if (exp.op === 'not') {
    if (exp.exp().op === 'or') return { negative: true, op: 'and', id: exp.exp().id, data: () => exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))) }
    else if (exp.exp().op === 'and') return { negative: true, op: 'or', id: exp.exp().id, data: () => exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x))) }
    else if (exp.exp().op === 'not') return denot(exp.exp().exp())
    else return syntheticNot(exp.exp())
  } else {
    if (exp.op) return { negative: false, id: exp.id, op: exp.op, data: () => exp.data().map(x => denot(x)) }
    else return exp
  }
}
const compactify = (exp) => {
  const collapseOr = (exp) => {
    if (exp.op !== 'or') return undefined
    let modified = false
    const res = exp.data().map(x => { if (x.op === 'or') { modified = true; return x.data() } return x }).flat()
    if (!modified) return undefined
    return { negative: exp.negative, id: exp.id, op: 'or', data: () => res }
  }
  const collapseAnd = (exp) => {
    if (exp.op !== 'and') return undefined
    let modified = false
    const res = exp.data().map(x => { if (x.op === 'and') { modified = true; return x.data() } return x }).flat()
    if (!modified) return undefined
    return { negative: exp.negative, id: exp.id, op: 'and', data: () => res }
  }
  let acc = exp
  let modified = false
  while (true) {
    const res = collapseAnd(acc) ?? collapseOr(acc)
    if (res !== undefined) { modified = true; acc = res } else break
  }
  if (modified && exp.data) return { id: exp.id, op: exp.op, negative: exp.negative, data: () => [...(acc.data())] }
  if (exp.op === 'not' && exp.exp().op !== undefined) return compactify(denot(exp))
  return exp
}
const isVal = exp => !exp.op
const isNotVal = exp => { if (exp.op === 'not') { if (exp.exp().op) throw "needs denot"; return true } return false }
const isSomeVal = exp => isVal(exp) || isNotVal(exp)
const getid = exp => isSomeVal(exp) ? (isVal(exp) ? exp : exp.exp()) : exp.id
const isGenVal = exp => isVal(exp) || (!isSomeVal(exp) && !exp.negative)
const isGenNotVal = exp => isNotVal(exp) || (!isSomeVal(exp) && exp.negative)
const addPos = (arr, exp) => { const id = getid(exp); if (arr.includes(id)) return false; arr.push(id); return true }
const addNeg = (arr, exp) => { const id = getid(exp); if (arr.includes(id)) return false; arr.push(id); return true }
const contradicts = (exp, pos, neg) => (isGenNotVal(exp) && pos.includes(getid(exp))) || (isGenVal(exp) && neg.includes(getid(exp)))
const checkContradictionGen = (exp, pos, neg, nesting) => {
  if (contradicts(exp, pos, neg)) return undefined
  return solve(exp, pos, neg, 1, nesting + 1)
}
const checkContradiction = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, nesting) => {
  if (!(isSomeVal(exp))) return solve(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, 1, nesting + 1)
  else {
    if (isNotVal(exp) && outerAndPositive.find(x => getid(exp) === x)) return undefined
    if (isVal(exp) && outerAndNegative.find(x => getid(exp) === x)) return undefined
    return solve(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, undefined, nesting + 1)
  }
}
const limit = 500000
const solve = (exp, outerAndPositive = [], outerAndNegative = [], k = undefined, nesting = 0) => {
  if (!globalCtx.ticks) globalCtx.ticks = 0
  globalCtx.ticks++
  if (globalCtx.ticks > limit) throw "too many contradictions, over " + limit
  const snapPos = [...outerAndPositive]
  const snapNeg = [...outerAndNegative]
  const mm = memoized(exp, snapPos, snapNeg, k)
  if (mm.hit) {
    if (mm.value !== undefined) {
      if (exp.op && !outerAndPositive.includes(exp.id)) outerAndPositive.push(exp.id)
      replayResult(mm.value, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)
    }
    return mm.value
  }
  const finish = (r) => { memoize(exp, snapPos, snapNeg, k, r); replayResult(r, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative); return r }
  if (!exp.op) {
    if (outerAndNegative.some(x => x === exp)) return finish(undefined)
    outerAndPositive.push(exp)
    return finish(exp)
  }
  if (exp.op === 'not') {
    if (exp.exp().op) throw "needs denot!"
    if (outerAndPositive.some(x => x === exp.exp())) return finish(undefined)
    outerAndNegative.push(exp.exp())
    return finish(exp)
  }
  if (contradicts(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)
  if (exp.op === 'and') {
    const extra = exp.data().filter(x => isSomeVal(x))
    const toSolve = exp.data().filter(x => !isSomeVal(x)).map(x => x.op === 'and' ? syntheticOr(x) : x)
    for (x of exp.data()) {
      if (contradicts(x, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)
      if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(outerAndPositive, x)
      else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(outerAndNegative, x)
    }
    const positions = toSolve.map(_ => 1)
    const limits = toSolve.map(exp => exp.data().length)
    const solveRest = () => {
      const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
      const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)
      let result = []
      let i = 0
      for (x of toSolve) {
        const res = solve(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, positions[i], nesting + 1)
        if (res) {
          const negativeSet = new Set(tryOuterAndNegative)
          const positiveSet = new Set(tryOuterAndPositive)
          if (res.filter) {
            for (x of res) {
              if (contradicts(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative)) return i
              if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(tryOuterAndPositive, x)
              else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(tryOuterAndNegative, x)
            }
            const dedup = x => { const id = getid(x); return isGenVal(x) ? !positiveSet.has(id) : !negativeSet.has(id) }
            result = [...result.filter(dedup), ...res]
          } else result = [...result, res]
        } else return i
        i++
      }
      tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => { if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x) })
      tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => { if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x) })
      return result
    }
    const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
      let j = pos
      while (j >= 0) {
        positions[j]++
        if (positions[j] > limits[j]) { positions[j] = 1; j-- }
        else return true
      }
      return false
    }
    while (true) {
      const result = solveRest()
      if (result.map) return finish(and(...[...extra, ...result]))
      if (!incrementAtPosition(result)) break
    }
    return finish(undefined)
  }
  if (exp.op === 'or') {
    if (k === undefined) return finish(solve(syntheticAnd(exp), outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, nesting + 1))
    else {
      const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
      const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)
      const child = exp.data()[k - 1]
      const wrapped = child.op === 'or' ? syntheticAnd(child) : child
      const solved = checkContradictionGen(wrapped, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, nesting)
      if (solved) {
        tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => { if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x) })
        tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => { if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x) })
        return finish(solved)
      }
    }
    return finish(undefined)
  }
}

<script>
// ===== FIXED evaluate: pop() is never inside || / && =====
function evaluate(root, input) {
  const memo = new Map()
  const valStack = []
  const stack = [{ e: root, done: false, n: 0, op: null }]
  const keyOf = (e) => {
    if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) return 'v:' + e
    return e.id + '|' + e.op + '|' + (e.negative ? 'N' : 'P') + '|' + (e.synthetic ? 'S' : '')
  }
  while (true) {
    if (stack.length === 0) break
    const task = stack.pop()
    const e = task.e
    if (task.done) {
      const n = task.n
      let v
      if (task.op === 'and') {
        v = true
        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
          const x = valStack.pop()
          v = v && x
        }
      } else if (task.op === 'or') {
        v = false
        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
          const x = valStack.pop()
          v = v || x
        }
      } else if (task.op === 'not') {
        v = !valStack.pop()
      }
      memo.set(keyOf(e), v)
      valStack.push(v)
      continue
    }
    const key = keyOf(e)
    if (memo.has(key)) { valStack.push(memo.get(key)); continue }
    if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) {
      const v = !!input[e - 1]
      memo.set(key, v)
      valStack.push(v)
      continue
    }
    if (e.op === 'not') {
      stack.push({ e, done: true, n: 1, op: 'not' })
      stack.push({ e: e.exp(), done: false, n: 0, op: null })
      continue
    }
    const children = e.data()
    stack.push({ e, done: true, n: children.length, op: e.op })
    for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.push({ e: children[i], done: false, n: 0, op: null })
  }
  return valStack.pop()
}
const show = (exp) => {
  if (!exp) return "not found"
  if (!exp.op) return "$" + exp
  if (exp.op === 'and') return `${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join('')}`
  if (exp.op === 'or') return `(${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join(' + ')})`
  if (exp.op === 'not') return ` -(${show(exp.exp())}) `
}

function bruteSat(exp, vars) {
  const n = vars.length
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
    const input = []
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) input[i] = ((mask >> (n-1-i)) & 1) === 1
    try { if (evaluate(exp, input) === true) return { sat: true, input } } catch(e) {}
  }
  return { sat: false }
}
function checkOne(name, exp, vars) {
  globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.hits = 0; globalCtx.ticks = 0

  try { sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0) } catch(e) { console.log(name, "THREW", e); return }
  const brute = bruteSat(exp, vars)
  if (sol === undefined) {
    if (brute.sat) console.log(`❌ ${name} FALSE NEGATIVE: solve=undef but SAT with`, brute.input)
    else console.log(`✅ ${name} OK UNSAT`)
    return
  }
  const assign = {}
  const collect = (e) => {
    if (!e) return
    if (!e.op) assign[e] = true
    else if (e.op === 'not') assign[e.exp()] = false
    else if (e.op === 'and') e.data().forEach(collect)

    try { if (evaluate(exp, inp) === true) { ok = true; break } } catch(e) {}
  }

  else if (!brute.sat) console.log(`❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve SAT but brute UNSAT`)
  else console.log(`✅ ${name} OK SAT`)
}

Your test is lying to you:

Two problems:

1. `sha256DSL8(1, ...)` has *1 message bit*, not 8. `200` is irrelevant — only bit 0 matters.
2. `numberToArray(200, 8)` does *not* return booleans. It returns an array of AST nodes — `one(1)`, `zero(1)`, etc.

And `evaluate` does:
const v = !!input[e - 1]
`!!{op:'or', ...}` is always `true`, because any object is truthy. So no matter what number you pass, `evaluate` sees message var `1` as `true`. That's why you always get `true`.

`evaluate` wants a boolean array indexed by var id:
const ctx3 = {}
const { messageVars, hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx3)
const exp = denot(hash[0])

console.log("msg = 0:", evaluate(exp, [false])) // false
console.log("msg = 1:", evaluate(exp, [true]))  // true
That matches the Python brute force: `msg [False]` → hash `0x28`, `hash[0]=False`; `msg [True]` → hash `0xD1`, `hash[0]=True`.

If you want to test with an 8-bit number, use 8 message bits:
const ctx8 = {}

// number 0 = 00000000

// number 255 = 11111111
console.log("msg = 255:", evaluate(exp8, [true,true,true,true,true,true,true,true])) // true, check in Python: 0x?? hash[0]=true
So the number you were looking for is `0` — with the correct input format.

// number -> boolean array, MSB first, length = bits
// e.g. numberToInput(200, 8) = [true,true,false,false,true,false,false,false]
// This is NOT numberToArray() — that one returns AST nodes, not booleans,
// and evaluate() does !!input[e-1], so !!node is always true.
function numberToInput(n, bits) {
  const out = []
  for (let i = 0; i < bits; i++) {
    out.push(((n >> (bits - 1 - i)) & 1) === 1)
  }
  return out
}

function assertHash(L, msgNum, expectedHashByte, label) {
  const ctx = {}
  const { messageVars, hash } = sha256DSL8(L, ctx)
  const input = numberToInput(msgNum, L)
  // check all 8 bits, not just hash[0]
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
    const exp = denot(hash[i])
    const got = evaluate(exp, input)
    const want = ((expectedHashByte >> (7 - i)) & 1) === 1
    console.assert(got === want,
      `${label} L=${L} msg=${msgNum} hash[${i}] got=${got} want=${want}`)
  }
  console.log(`ok ${label} L=${L} msg=${msgNum} -> hash=0x${expectedHashByte.toString(16).padStart(2,'0')}`)
}

Your DSL's shape is different from SHA8: `sha256DSL(L, ctx)` returns `hash` as *8 words × 32 bits*, not a flat 8-bit array. `hash[word][bit]`.
function stringToInput(s) {
  const out = []
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    const code = s.charCodeAt(i)
    for (let b = 7; b >= 0; b--) out.push(((code >> b) & 1) === 1)
  }
  return out
}

function assertSha256(str, expectedHex, label) {
  const input = stringToInput(str)
  const L = input.length
  const ctx = {}
  const { hash } = sha256DSL(L, ctx) // hash = [8 words][32 bits]
  // expectedHex is 64 hex chars = 256 bits
  for (let w = 0; w < 8; w++) {
    for (let b = 0; b < 32; b++) {
      const exp = denot(hash[w][b])
      const got = evaluate(exp, input)
      const hexDigit = parseInt(expectedHex[w * 8 + Math.floor(b / 4)], 16)
      const want = ((hexDigit >> (3 - (b % 4))) & 1) === 1
      console.assert(got === want,
        `${label} word=${w} bit=${b} got=${got} want=${want}`)
    }
  }

What to look for:

- If `""` passes but `"a"` / `"abc"` fail, it's the message padding / `numberToArray(L, 64)` / `W[0..15]` loading — the empty case has no message bits to load.
- If word 0 passes but later words fail, it's the round state / `a..h` rotation, not the constants.
- If all fail on the same bit pattern, check `addArray` carry — SHA8 used 8-bit `addArray`, SHA256 uses 32-bit, same code but different width.

`sha256DSL(0, ctx)` → `allocateArray(0, ctx)` allocates *zero* vars, so `v()` is never called, so `globalCtx` is never set to `ctx`.

Then the first `and` / `or` / `not` inside `sha256DSLFromBits` does this:
if (!globalCtx.counter) globalCtx.counter = 0
If `globalCtx` is `undefined`, that line throws:

For `L > 0` it works, because `allocateArray` calls `v()` and sets `globalCtx = ctx`. For `L = 0` it doesn't.

### Fix in the library (better)

Make `sha256DSL` / `sha256DSL8` set it themselves, so callers can't forget:
function sha256DSL(L, ctx) {
  globalCtx = ctx
  const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)
  return sha256DSLFromBits(messageVars, ctx)
}

function sha256DSL8(L, ctx) {
  globalCtx = ctx
  const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)
  return sha256DSL8FromBits(messageVars, ctx)

function stringToInput(s) {
  const out = []
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    const code = s.charCodeAt(i)
    for (let b = 7; b >= 0; b--) out.push(((code >> b) & 1) === 1)
  }
  return out
}

[11/23/26, 4:39:10 AM] You: <image omitted>
[11/23/26, 4:39:15 AM] Meta AI: That's the tell: *word 0 passes, word 1+ fails.*

That pattern is the `L=0` collision, not a SHA bug.

Your DSL reserves var `1` as `templateVar` — `one()` is `or(1, not(1))`, `zero()` is `and(1, not(1))`.

Node ids come from `globalCtx.counter`:

- For `L > 0`, `allocateArray(L)` calls `v()` `L` times, so `counter = L`, and the first `or`/`and` node gets id `L+1`. No collision with `1`.
- For `L = 0`, `allocateArray(0)` calls `v()` *zero* times, so `counter = 0`, and the first `or` node gets id `1` — the exact same id as `templateVar`.

Then `denot` / `evaluate` can't tell “leaf var 1” apart from “node 1”. Constants get corrupted, and the hash falls apart after the first word.

### Fix for the empty test only

Reserve id `1` before building, and give `evaluate` a dummy value for it:
function assertSha256(str, expectedHex, label) {
  const input = stringToInput(str)
  const ctx = {}
  globalCtx = ctx

  // L=0: reserve var 1 for templateVar, so first node id is 2, not 1
  if (input.length === 0) {
    ctx.counter = 1
  }

  const { hash } = sha256DSL(input.length, ctx)
  // evaluate input: for L=0, input is [false] = dummy for templateVar 1
  const evalInput = input.length === 0 ? [false] : input

  console.assert(hash.length === 256, `hash.length=${hash.length}`)
  for (let b = 0; b < 256; b++) {
    const got = evaluate(denot(hash[b]), evalInput)
    const hexDigit = parseInt(expectedHex[Math.floor(b / 4)], 16)
    const want = ((hexDigit >> (3 - (b % 4))) & 1) === 1
    console.assert(got === want, `${label} bit=${b} got=${got} want=${want}`)
  }
  console.log(`ok ${label} "${str}" -> ${expectedHex}`)
}
`or(1, not(1))` is `true` no matter what dummy you pass for var `1`, so `[false]` is fine.

For `"a"` / `"abc"` / `"hello"` you don't need this — `L > 0` already reserves `1` via `allocateArray`. If those also fail on word 1, paste the first failing bit for `"a"` — that would be a different bug. But for `""`, this is it.

                if (exp.exp().op) throw "needs denot!"
                if (outerAndPositive.some(x => x === exp.exp())) return finish(undefined)
                outerAndNegative.push(exp.exp())
                return finish(exp)
            }

 
            if (contradicts(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)

            if (exp.op === 'and') {

                const extra = exp.data().filter(x => isSomeVal(x))

                const toSolve = exp.data().filter(x => !isSomeVal(x)).map(x => x.op === 'and' ? syntheticOr(x) : x)

                for (x of exp.data()){
                  if (contradicts(x, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)
                  if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(outerAndPositive, x)
                  else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(outerAndNegative, x)
                }

                const positions = toSolve.map(_ => 1)

                const limits = toSolve.map(exp => exp.data().length)

                //console.log("limits = " + limits + " exp = " + show(exp))

                    //console.log(positions)
                    const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
                    const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

                    let i = 0

                        const res = solve(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, positions[i], nesting + 1)

                            const positiveSet = new Set(tryOuterAndPositive)

                                    if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(tryOuterAndPositive, x) 
                                    else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(tryOuterAndNegative, x)
                                }

                                const dedup = x => {
                                  const id = getid(x)
                                  return isGenVal(x) ? !positiveSet.has(id) : !negativeSet.has(id)
                                }
  
                                result = [...result.filter(dedup), ...res]

                            } else {
                                result = [...result, res]
          
                            }                            

                        } else {
                            //console.log("COMBO CONTRA: " + show(x))
                            return i
                        }
                        
                        i++
                    } 

                    tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x)})
                    tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                        } else return true
                    }
                    return false

                        return finish(and(...[...extra, ...result]))
                    }

        function evaluate(root, input) {
        const memo = new Map()
        const valStack = []
        const stack = [{ e: root, done: false, n: 0, op: null }]
        const keyOf = (e) => {
            if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) return 'v:' + e
            return e.id + '|' + e.op + '|' + (e.negative ? 'N' : 'P') + '|' + (e.synthetic ? 'S' : '')
        }
        while (true) {
            if (stack.length === 0) break
            const task = stack.pop()
            const e = task.e
            if (task.done) {
            const n = task.n
            let v
            if (task.op === 'and') {
                v = true
                for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                const x = valStack.pop()
                v = v && x
                }
            } else if (task.op === 'or') {
                v = false
                for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                const x = valStack.pop()
                v = v || x
                }
            } else if (task.op === 'not') {
                v = !valStack.pop()
            }
            memo.set(keyOf(e), v)
            valStack.push(v)
            continue
            }
            const key = keyOf(e)
            if (memo.has(key)) { valStack.push(memo.get(key)); continue }
            if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) {
            const v = !!input[e - 1]
            memo.set(key, v)
            valStack.push(v)
            continue
            }
            if (e.op === 'not') {
            stack.push({ e, done: true, n: 1, op: 'not' })
            stack.push({ e: e.exp(), done: false, n: 0, op: null })
            continue
            }
            const children = e.data()
            stack.push({ e, done: true, n: children.length, op: e.op })
            for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.push({ e: children[i], done: false, n: 0, op: null })
        }
        return valStack.pop()
        }

        const show = (exp) => {
            if (!exp) return "not found"
            if (!exp.op)  return "$" + exp
            if (exp.op === 'and') return ${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join('')}
            if (exp.op === 'or') return (${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join(' + ')})
            if (exp.op === 'not') return ` -(${show(exp.exp())}) `
        }

        // ---------- brute force check ----------
function bruteSat(exp, vars) {
  const n = vars.length
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
    const input = []
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) input[i] = ((mask >> (n-1-i)) & 1) === 1
    // evaluate() in your code expects input[exp-1], and memo is buggy, so use fresh memo
    try { if (evaluate(exp, input, {}) === true) return { sat: true, input } } catch(e) {}
  }
  return { sat: false }
}

function checkOne(name, exp, vars) {
  const ctxBefore = globalCtx
  // fresh memo per test, otherwise cross-test pollution hides the bug
  globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.hits = 0; globalCtx.ticks = 0
  let sol
  try { sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0) } catch(e) { console.log(name, "THREW", e); return }
  const brute = bruteSat(exp, vars)

  if (sol === undefined) {
    if (brute.sat) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE NEGATIVE: solve=undef but SAT with, brute.input)
    else console.log(✅ ${name} OK UNSAT)
    return
  }
  // build assignment from solution: solutionToNum style, but check directly
  // solution is an and(...) of literals, extract them
  const assign = {}
  const collect = (e) => {
    if (!e) return
    if (!e.op) assign[e] = true
    else if (e.op === 'not') assign[e.exp()] = false
    else if (e.op === 'and') e.data().forEach(collect)
    else if (e.op === 'or') { /* or in solution = node id, ignore */ }
  }
  collect(sol)
  // fill unassigned with false, evaluate
  const input = vars.map(v => assign[v] === true)
  // if solution didn't assign a var, try both completions
  let ok = false
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << vars.length); mask++) {
    const inp = vars.map((v,i) => assign[v] !== undefined ? assign[v] : ((mask>>i)&1)===1)
    try { if (evaluate(exp, inp, {}) === true) { ok = true; break } } catch(e) {}
  }
  if (!ok) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve returned, show(sol), "but no completion satisfies")
  else if (!brute.sat) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve SAT but brute UNSAT)
  else console.log(✅ ${name} OK SAT)
}

// ---------- concrete small cases ----------
{
  const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
  const a = v(ctx), b = v(ctx), c = v(ctx)

  // UNSAT: all 4 combos of a,b forbidden
  // (a|b) & (!a|b) & (a|!b) & (!a|!b)
  const unsat = and(or(a,b), or(not(a), b), or(a, not(b)), or(not(a), not(b)))
  checkOne("unsat-2var", denot(unsat), [a,b])

  // SAT, but requires learning: (a|b) & (!a)  => must pick b
  const sat1 = and(or(a,b), not(a))
  checkOne("sat-requires-b", denot(sat1), [a,b])

  // Shared subexpression, solved twice under different outer context
  // This is the delta-loss case: first solve learns something, second reuses memo
  const shared = or(a, b)
  const shared2 = and(shared, or(not(a), c), or(not(b), not(c)), shared)
  checkOne("shared-or", denot(shared2), [a,b,c])

  // AND where intermediate learn is not in final result:
  // (a|b) & (!a|c) & (!b|c) & (!c)  => UNSAT, needs to propagate c=false -> a=false,b=false -> (a|b) fails
  // If delta (c=false) is lost on replay, solver can claim (a|b) SAT
  const unsat2 = and(or(a,b), or(not(a), c), or(not(b), c), not(c))
  checkOne("unsat-propagate-c", denot(unsat2), [a,b,c])
}

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [

];
const H0_HEX = ['6a09e667','bb67ae85','3c6ef372','a54ff53a','510e527f','9b05688c','1f83d9ab','5be0cd19'];
const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}
