const formAst = () => {
    // ---------- Fixed shift / rotate, your shiftArray had a bug ----------

    // arr is MSB first, length 32. shr fills with zero, rotr wraps.

    const notArrays = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x));

    const shrArrays = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {

        const z = zero(templateVar);
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };

    const rotrArrays = (arr, k) => {

        return [...arr.slice(32 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 32 - k)];

    };



    // ---------- Addition, 2-bit full adder ----------

    // a + b + carry_in = 0..3, needs 2 bits: [carry_out, sum]

    const addBit = (a, b, carry_in) => {

        const aXorB = xor(a, b);
        const sum = xor(aXorB, carry_in);
        const carry_out = or(and(a, b), and(carry_in, aXorB));
        return [carry_out, sum];

    };



    const addArrays = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const out = new Array(32);
        let carry = zero(templateVar);

        for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry);
            out[i] = sum;
            carry = carry_out;
        }

        return out; // mod 2^32, final carry dropped

    };



    const addManyArrays = (...arrs) => {
        let acc = arrs[0];
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays(acc, arrs[k]);
        return acc;
    };



    const Ch = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays(x), z));
    };

    const Maj = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(x, z)), andArrays(y, z));
    };

    const Sigma0 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 2), rotrArrays(x, 13)), rotrArrays(x, 22));

    const Sigma1 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 6), rotrArrays(x, 11)), rotrArrays(x, 25));

    const sigma0 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 7), rotrArrays(x, 18)), shrArrays(x, 3, templateVar));

    const sigma1 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays(x, 17), rotrArrays(x, 19)), shrArrays(x, 10, templateVar));



    const H_HEX = [0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19];

    // messageBits: Array<expr> length L, MSB first

    // returns Array<expr> length 256, MSB first

    const sha256DSLFromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

        const L = messageBits.length;

        // ---------- Padding ----------

        // append 1, then k zeros, then L as 64-bit big-endian

        const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)];

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar));

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 64, templateVar));

        // ---------- Initial H ----------

        let H = H_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));

        const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar));


        // ---------- Process each 512-bit chunk ----------

        const numChunks = padded.length / 512;

        for (let c = 0; c < numChunks; c++) {

            const chunk = padded.slice(c * 512, (c + 1) * 512);

            // W[0..15]

            const W = [];

            for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));

            // W[16..63]

            for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays(sigma1(W[t - 2], templateVar), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15], templateVar), W[t - 16]));

            }



            // Working vars

            let a = H[0], b = H[1], c2 = H[2], d = H[3];

            let e = H[4], f = H[5], g = H[6], h = H[7];



            // 64 rounds

            for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {

                const T1 = addManyArrays(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
                const T2 = addManyArrays(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c2));

                h = g;
                g = f;
                f = e;
                e = addArrays(d, T1, templateVar);
                d = c2;
                c2 = b;
                b = a;
                a = addArrays(T1, T2, templateVar);

            }



            // H = H + working vars

            H[0] = addArrays(H[0], a, templateVar);
            H[1] = addArrays(H[1], b, templateVar);
            H[2] = addArrays(H[2], c2, templateVar);
            H[3] = addArrays(H[3], d, templateVar);
            H[4] = addArrays(H[4], e, templateVar);
            H[5] = addArrays(H[5], f, templateVar);
            H[6] = addArrays(H[6], g, templateVar);
            H[7] = addArrays(H[7], h, templateVar);

        }



        // ---------- Output: concat H ----------

        return appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(appendArrays(H[0], H[1]), appendArrays(H[2], H[3])),  appendArrays(appendArrays(H[4], H[5]), appendArrays(H[6], H[7]))), []).slice(0, 256);

    };



    // Takes only length, allocates unknown vars inside

    // Returns { messageVars, hash }

    const sha256DSL = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1) => {

    const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx);

    const hash = sha256DSLFromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar);
        return { messageVars, hash };
    };


    //8-bit version

    const rotrArrays8 = (arr, k) => {
        return [...arr.slice(8 - k), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const shrArrays8 = (arr, k, templateVar = 1) => {
        const z = zero(templateVar)
        return [...Array(k).fill(z), ...arr.slice(0, 8 - k)]
    }



    const notArrays8 = (arr) => arr.map((x) => not(x))



    // addArrays generalized: works for any length, here 8

    const addArrays8 = (arr1, arr2, templateVar = 1) => {

        const n = arr1.length

        const out = new Array(n)

        let carry = zero(templateVar)

        for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const [carry_out, sum] = addBit(arr1[i], arr2[i], carry)
            out[i] = sum
            carry = carry_out
        }

        return out

    }



    const addManyArrays8 = (...arrs) => {

        let acc = arrs[0]
        for (let k = 1; k < arrs.length; k++) acc = addArrays8(acc, arrs[k])
        return acc

    }



    // ---------- 8-bit logical functions ----------

    // Same shapes as SHA-256, rotations scaled to 8 bits

    const Ch8 = (x, y, z) => {
        return xorArrays(andArrays(x, y), andArrays(notArrays8(x), z))
    }



    const Maj8 = (x, y, z) => {

    }



    const Sigma0_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), rotrArrays8(x, 5))

    const Sigma1_8 = (x) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), rotrArrays8(x, 6))

    const sigma0_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 1), rotrArrays8(x, 3)), shrArrays8(x, 2, templateVar))

    const sigma1_8 = (x, templateVar = 1) => xorArrays(xorArrays(rotrArrays8(x, 2), rotrArrays8(x, 4)), shrArrays8(x, 3, templateVar))



    // ---------- 8-bit constants ----------

    // First 8-bit chunks of your real K / H, truncated for the test

    const K8_HEX = [0x42, 0x71, 0xb5, 0xe9, 0x39, 0x59, 0x92, 0xab]

    const H8 = 0x6a



    // Message: L bits, padded to one 32-bit block (4 x 8-bit words)

    // Padding: 1, then zeros, then L as 8-bit length

    // Keeps your sha256DSLFromBits shape, just smaller

    const sha256DSL8FromBits = (messageBits, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const L = messageBits.length

        const k = (24 - ((L + 1) % 32) + 32) % 32

        let padded = [...messageBits, one(templateVar)]

        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(zero(templateVar))

        padded = appendArrays(padded, numberToArray(L, 8, templateVar))


        let H = numberToArray(H8, 8, templateVar)

        const K = K8_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 8, templateVar))



        // W[0..3] from chunk

        const W = []

        for (let t = 0; t < 4; t++) W.push(padded.slice(t * 8, t * 8 + 8))

        // W[4..rounds-1] message schedule, same formula as SHA

        for (let t = 4; t < rounds; t++) {

                W.push(addManyArrays8(

                sigma1_8(W[t - 2], templateVar),

                W[t - 3],

                sigma0_8(W[t - 4], templateVar),

                // W[t-4] wraps for small t: use W[0] when t-4 < 0, handled by modulo below

                W[0]

            ))
        

        }

        // Working vars: a..h collapsed to a..h in 8-bit

        // To keep it 8-bit and simple: a = H, b..h = rotated copies

        // This keeps Ch/Maj/Sigma structure without 8 full 32-bit words

        let a = H

        let b = rotrArrays8(H, 1)

        let c2 = rotrArrays8(H, 2)

        let d = rotrArrays8(H, 3)

        let e = rotrArrays8(H, 4)

        let f = rotrArrays8(H, 5)

        let g = rotrArrays8(H, 6)

        let h = rotrArrays8(H, 7)



        for (let t = 0; t < rounds; t++) {

            const T1 = addManyArrays8(h, Sigma1_8(e), Ch8(e, f, g), K[t % K.length], W[t % W.length])

            const T2 = addManyArrays8(Sigma0_8(a), Maj8(a, b, c2))

            h = g
            g = f
            f = e
            e = addArrays8(d, T1, templateVar)
            d = c2
            c2 = b
            b = a
            a = addArrays8(T1, T2, templateVar)

        }

        // H = H + a, 8-bit output

        return addArrays8(H, a, templateVar)
    }

    const sha256DSL8 = (L, ctx, templateVar = 1, rounds = 8) => {

        const messageVars = allocateArray(L, ctx)

        const hash = sha256DSL8FromBits(messageVars, ctx, templateVar, rounds)

        return { messageVars, hash }

    }

    function stringToInput(s) {
        const out = []
        for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
            const code = s.charCodeAt(i)
            for (let b = 7; b >= 0; b--) out.push(((code >> b) & 1) === 1)
        }
        return out
    }

    function stringToInput(s) {
  const out = []

    for (let b = 7; b >= 0; b--) out.push(((code >> b) & 1) === 1)
  }
  return out
}

  console.assert(hash.length === 256, hash.length=${hash.length})
  for (let b = 0; b < 256; b++) {
    const got = evaluate(denot(hash[b]), evalInput)

    const want = ((hexDigit >> (3 - (b % 4))) & 1) === 1
    console.assert(got === want, ${label} bit=${b} got=${got} want=${want})
  }
  console.log(ok ${label} "${str}" -> ${expectedHex})
}

    <script>
       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}

[11/23/26, 4:42:18 AM] Meta AI: Found it — and it's not `counter`, it's `K`.

In your file:
const K_HEX = [
 '428a2f98','71374491','b5c0fbcf', ...
 // ^^^^^^^ strings, not numbers
]
And in `formAst()`:
const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(n, 32, templateVar))
But `numberToArray` does:
num.toString(2).padStart(k, '0')...
For a *string*, `.toString(2)` does nothing — it stays `'428a2f98'`. Then:
'428a2f98'.split('').map(x => x === '1' ? one() : zero())
So `'4'` → `zero`, `'2'` → `zero`, `'8'` → `zero`, `'a'` → `zero`, `'f'` → `zero`, only literal `'1'` characters become `one`. Your `K` is almost all zeros.

`H_HEX` is numbers (`0x6a09e667`), so `H` is correct. `K8_HEX` in the 8-bit version is also numbers (`0x42`), so SHA8 passes. Only SHA256 `K` is broken — which is why SHA8 tests passed and SHA256 fails on every message, not just `""`.

### Fix — one line
// in sha256DSLFromBits, inside formAst()
const K = K_HEX.map((n) => numberToArray(parseInt(n, 16), 32, templateVar))
That's it. Drop the `ctx.counter = 1` hack — it wasn't the bug, it just moved the failure around:
function assertSha256(str, expectedHex, label) {
  const input = stringToInput(str)
  const ctx = {}
  globalCtx = ctx
  const { hash } = sha256DSL(input.length, ctx)
  const evalInput = input.length === 0 ? [false] : input
  console.assert(hash.length === 256, `hash.length=${hash.length}`)
  for (let b = 0; b < 256; b++) {

[11/23/26, 4:52:47 AM] You: Why do you need denot? I thought evaluate can handle not operation, no?
[11/23/26, 4:52:49 AM] Meta AI: You're right — for `evaluate`, you don't.

`evaluate` already handles `not` natively:
if (e.op === 'not') {
  stack.push({ e, done: true, n: 1, op: 'not' })
  stack.push({ e: e.exp(), ... })
}
`denot` is only for `solve()`.

`solve()` throws `"needs denot!"` if it sees `not(and(...))` or `not(or(...))`. `denot` pushes the `not` down with De Morgan — `not(A and B) -> (not A) or (not B)`, `not(not X) -> X` — so `solve` only ever sees `not(leaf)`.

For testing hash values, `solve` isn't involved. And `denot` is what's hanging you: it expands the shared DAG into a tree. Every shared `W[t]` / `Sigma` node gets duplicated on every `denot()` call, so the tree explodes exponentially. `evaluate` on the raw DAG with its memo is linear-ish.

For `L=1`, `evaluate` already told you the ground truth:

- `hash[0]` is SAT — pick `msg=1`
- `not(hash[0])` is SAT — pick `msg=0`

For any formula, `F` and `not(F)` can't both be UNSAT. If `solve` returns `undefined` for both, it has a false negative. `sha256DSL8` is fine for `evaluate` — the `assertHash` suite for `L=1` passed.

function quickSolverTest(rounds) {
  // 1. Ground truth by evaluate
  for (const msg of [0, 1]) {
    const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
    const { hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx, 1, rounds)
    const got = evaluate(hash[0], numberToInput(msg, 1))
    console.log(`rounds=${rounds} msg=${msg} evaluate hash[0]=${got}`)
  }

  // 2. Solver: hash[0] should be SAT iff some msg gave true above
  {
    const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
    const { hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx, 1, rounds)
    const exp = denot(hash[0])
    globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.ticks = 0
    const sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0)
    console.log(`rounds=${rounds} solve(hash[0]) =`, sol === undefined ? "UNSAT" : show(sol))
  }

  // 3. Solver: not(hash[0]) should be SAT iff some msg gave false above
  {
    const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
    const { hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx, 1, rounds)
    const exp = denot(not(hash[0])) // denot OUTSIDE the not, correct
    globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.ticks = 0
    const sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0)
    console.log(`rounds=${rounds} solve(not(hash[0])) =`, sol === undefined ? "UNSAT" : show(sol))
  }
}

That screenshot is actually decisive:

- `denot: 0.0009ms` — basically instant
- `solve: 28ms, ticks: 4558` → `UNSAT`
- `leafs: [1]`

So it's not a timeout, not a `denot` blowup. The solver _quickly proves_ `UNSAT` for a formula `evaluate` says is SAT. That means the solver is proving UNSAT of a *different formula* than `evaluate` is evaluating. Fuzz wouldn't catch that, because fuzz formulas don't have the SHA structure.

The SHA-specific difference: *id collision between a leaf and an internal node.*

- Message var is `v(1)` → leaf id `1`, and `leafs = [1]`
- Template var is also `1`
- Internal `and` / `or` nodes get ids from a counter

If that counter starts at `1`, the first internal node also has id `1`. `evaluate` survives this because its memo key includes `op` — leaf vs `and` are distinguished. `solve`'s `pos` / `neg` sets and `memoKey` are just sets of ids, no `op`. So assuming internal-node-`1` is true also assumes leaf-`1` is true, and vice versa. That can manufacture a false UNSAT, and it only shows up when a formula actually contains both a leaf `1` and an internal node `1` — i.e. SHA, not fuzz.

### Check for the collision
{
  const ctx = {}
  globalCtx = ctx
  const { hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx, 1, 1)
  const seen = new Map() // id -> ops seen with that id
  const stack = [hash[0]]
  const visited = new Set()
  while (stack.length) {
    const e = stack.pop()
    if (e === null || typeof e !== "object") continue
    const key = e.id + "|" + e.op
    if (visited.has(key)) continue
    visited.add(key)
    if (!seen.has(e.id)) seen.set(e.id, new Set())
    seen.get(e.id).add(e.op)
    if (e.op === "not") stack.push(e.exp())
    else if (e.op === "and" || e.op === "or") { for (const c of e.data()) stack.push(c) }
  }
  for (const [id, ops] of seen) {
    if (ops.size > 1) console.log("COLLISION id=", id, "ops=", [...ops])
  }
  console.log("leafs:", [...globalCtx.leafs], "total distinct ids:", seen.size)
  console.log("hash[0] id/op:", hash[0].id, hash[0].op)
}
If you see `COLLISION id= 1 ops= [undefined, 'and'/'or']` — that's it.

Fix is to make the counter start *above* any leaf id, e.g. start internal ids at `1000000`, or make `v()` use negative ids and never let the counter produce a negative id. Tell me what the collision scan prints and I'll give the one-line counter fix.

So what's left that fuzz doesn't cover: *sharing.*

Fuzz builds trees — every subformula appears once. SHA is a DAG — the same `W[t]` / `Sigma` / `add` node appears in many places, via `data()` returning fresh `denot` wrappers each time with the same `id`.

[11/23/26, 5:24:29 AM] You: it times out without memo - problem is too complex 56000000 steps would be required
[11/23/26, 5:24:32 AM] Meta AI: Exactly — that confirms it. Memo is _required_ (56M steps without it), but the current `memoKey` is unsound. So the fix isn't to disable memo, it's to make the key sound *without* losing the sharing.

Why leaf-only filtering is wrong:

`pos` / `neg` don't just hold leaf assumptions. The solver also assumes internal nodes — e.g. "assume this `W[t]` node is true" — to prune. Those internal assumptions affect the subproblem, but `memoKey` drops them. So two subproblems with the same leaf assumptions but different internal assumptions share a cache entry, and the first one poisons the second. That's why it returns UNSAT in 4558 ticks instead of exploring the 56M-step tree.

The sound version: filter `pos` / `neg` to nodes that are *relevant to this subformula* — i.e. in its subtree — not just to leafs. Irrelevant assumptions can be dropped safely. Relevant internal assumptions cannot.

### Fix `memoKey`

Find your `memoKey` — it looks like this now:
const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg) =>
  exp.id + "|" + pos.filter(id => globalCtx.leafs.has(id)) + "|" + neg.filter(id => globalCtx.leafs.has(id))
Replace it with:
// cache: exp.id -> Set of all ids in its subtree (incl. itself)
const subtreeCache = new Map()
function subtreeIds(exp) {
  if (subtreeCache.has(exp.id)) return subtreeCache.get(exp.id)
  const out = new Set([exp.id])
  const stack = [exp]
  const seen = new Set([exp.id])
  while (stack.length) {
    const e = stack.pop()
    if (e.op === "not") {
      const c = e.exp()
      if (!seen.has(c.id)) { seen.add(c.id); out.add(c.id); stack.push(c) }
    } else if (e.op === "and" || e.op === "or") {
      for (const c of e.data()) {
        if (!seen.has(c.id)) { seen.add(c.id); out.add(c.id); stack.push(c) }
      }
    }
  }
  subtreeCache.set(exp.id, out)
  return out
}

const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg) => {
  const sub = subtreeIds(exp)
  const p = pos.filter(id => sub.has(id)).sort((a, b) => a - b)
  const n = neg.filter(id => sub.has(id)).sort((a, b) => a - b)
  return exp.id + "|p:" + p.join(",") + "|n:" + n.join(",")
}
Two details that matter:

- *Sort* `pos` / `neg` — otherwise `[1, 2]` and `[2, 1]` are different keys for the same assumption set, and you lose hits.
- *Cache `subtreeIds` by `exp.id`* — without that, computing the subtree on every `solve` call reintroduces the blowup you're trying to avoid. The `seen` set is what keeps it linear on the DAG instead of exponential on the tree.

### The lazy-safe fix

Current key drops internal assumptions:
// buggy: filters pos/neg to leafs only
exp.id + "|" + pos.filter(id => leafs.has(id)) + "|" + neg.filter(...)
Sound version — no traversal, no forcing `data()` / `exp()`:
const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg) => {
  const p = [...pos].sort((a, b) => a - b)
  const n = [...neg].sort((a, b) => a - b)
  return exp.id + "|p:" + p.join(",") + "|n:" + n.join(",")
}
Why this is still effective without being unsound:

- The DAG-sharing case that memo is actually for — same `exp.id` revisited via a different path *with the same assumptions* — still hits, because `pos` / `neg` are identical.
- The poisoning case — same `exp.id` + same leaf assumptions but *different internal assumptions* — now gets a different key, so it doesn't reuse the wrong cached result.
- Sorting matters: `pos` order depends on the path you arrived by, so unsorted `pos` would miss hits that should hit.

It will be slower than the buggy leaf-only key — more distinct keys, fewer hits — but it should be nowhere near the 56M no-memo blowup, because the true sharing hits are preserved.

[11/23/26, 5:47:17 AM] Meta AI: Found it — this is almost certainly the bug, in `memoKey`:
return id + pol + '|' + (exp.op ?? "v") + ... + "|"
    + [...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort(...).join(',')
    + '|' + [...neg].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort(...).join(',')
    + '|' + k
*The key only includes leaf assumptions.* It drops every non-leaf entry in `outerAndPositive / outerAndNegative`.

But `solve` depends on non-leaf entries too:

- `contradicts(exp, pos, neg)` checks `pos.includes(getid(exp))` / `neg.includes(getid(exp))` for _gen_ nodes — i.e. `and`/`or` nodes with `negative` set, not just leaves.
- The `and` case adds gen vals to `pos`/`neg` and checks them.
- On a memo hit, `solve` returns the cached value *without re-checking `contradicts` against the current `pos`/`neg`* — it just `replayResult`s it.

So: a subproblem solved as UNSAT in a context where a non-leaf blocker was present gets cached under a key that doesn't mention that blocker. Later, in a context _without_ that blocker, the same key hits and returns the stale UNSAT. Or vice versa for a SAT result.

That matches `454` exactly: `449` / `444` appear as both `and` and `or` with the same id, and the `and`-combining of `451:or` + `453:or` re-solves subproblems under different non-leaf outer sets — but the memo key can't tell those contexts apart.

Look again at the `and` backtracking itself, not the memo. This is the odometer:
const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
    let j = pos
    while (j >= 0) {
        positions[j]++
        if (positions[j] > limits[j]) {
            positions[j] = 1
            j--
        } else return true
    }
    return false
}
That only resets a position when _it_ overflows. It never resets positions to the *right* of the one it incremented.

That matters because `solveRest` stops at the first failing conjunct `i`. Positions to the right of `i` still hold stale values from the _previous_ attempt, under the _previous_ left-hand choices. When you increment at `i` and carry left, you keep those stale right-hand values instead of restarting them at `1`.

Concrete skip, with 3 conjuncts:

- Try `[1,2,2]`, fail at `i=1`
- `incrementAtPosition(1)`: `positions[1]` overflows → reset to `1`, carry to `positions[0] = 2`
- Next attempt is `[2,1,2]` — but `[2,1,1]` was never tried. If `[2,1,1]` was the SAT combo and `[2,1,2]` fails at `i=2`, the odometer then carries to `[2,2,1]`, and `[2,1,1]` is skipped forever. The `and` declares UNSAT even though a combo exists.

For `454` itself there are only 2 conjuncts, so the top-level odometer doesn't skip — but the same `incrementAtPosition` runs inside _every_ nested `and` below it, including ones with 3+ conjuncts. One skipped combo down there poisons the whole thing, and it looks like the top-level `and` is at fault.

Fix — reset the right side on a successful increment:
const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
    let j = pos
    while (j >= 0) {
        positions[j]++
        if (positions[j] > limits[j]) {
            positions[j] = 1
            j--
        } else {
            for (let t = j + 1; t < positions.length; t++) positions[t] = 1
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}
That is the standard odometer: when a left choice changes, all choices to its right restart at `1`.

Try just that one change and re-run your repro — `solve(denot(not(hash[0])))` for rounds=2, and the `not454` case. If it flips to SAT, that was it.

            return arr.map((x, i) => arr[x+k] ?? 0)
        }

        const numberToArray = (num, k, templateVar = 1) => {
            return num.toString(2).padStart(k, '0').split('').map(x => x === '1' ? one(templateVar) : zero(templateVar))
        }

        const numberToInput = (num, k, templateVar = 1) => {
            return num.toString(2).padStart(k, '0').split('').map(x => x === '1')
        }


        const solutionToNum = (exp, n) => {
            if (!exp) return undefined
            const bitarray = []
            compactify(exp).data().forEach(x => {
                if (isVal(x)) {
                    bitarray[x - 1] = 1
                }
                if (isNotVal(x)) {
                    bitarray[x.exp() - 1] = 0
                }
            })

            for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                if (!bitarray[i]) {
                    bitarray[i] = 0
                }
            }
            const str = bitarray.map(x => x.toString()).join('')
            //console.log(compactify(exp).data())
            return parseInt(str, 2)
        }

        const eqArrays = (arr1, arr2) => {  
            return and(...arr1.map((x, i) => not(xor(x, arr2[i]))))
        }

    <script>
        //memoization

    const UNDEF = "_UNDEF_";

    


const memoKey = (exp, pos, neg, k) => {
  const id = exp.op ? exp.id : exp
  const pol = exp.op ? (exp.negative ? 'N' : 'P') : 'V'
  return id + pol + '|' + (exp.op ?? "v") + (exp.synthetic ? "synthetic" : "") + "|" + [...pos].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + [...neg].filter(x => globalCtx.leafs.has(x)).sort((a,b)=>a-b).join(',') + '|' + k
}

// at START of solve - return fast if hit
// returns { hit: true, value } or { hit: false }
const memoized = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k) => {
if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
if (!globalCtx.hits) globalCtx.hits = 0
const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k);
  if (key in globalCtx.memo) {
    const stored = globalCtx.memo[key];
    globalCtx.hits++
    return { hit: true, value: stored === UNDEF ? undefined : stored };
  }
  return { hit: false };
};

// BEFORE returning result in solve
const memoize = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, result) => {
  if (!globalCtx.memo) globalCtx.memo = {}
  const key = memoKey(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k);
  globalCtx.memo[key] = (result === undefined ? UNDEF : result);
  return result;
};

    const replayResult = (res, pos, neg) => {
        if (res === undefined) return
        if (!res.op) {
            if (!pos.includes(res)) pos.push(res)
            return
        }
        if (res.op === 'not') {
            const v = res.exp()
            if (!neg.includes(v)) neg.push(v)
            return
        }
        if (res.op === 'and') {
            res.data().forEach(x => replayResult(x, pos, neg))
            return
        }
        // or-node as a result: don't recurse, just mark the node itself
        if (!pos.includes(res.id)) pos.push(res.id)
    }

        const syntheticNot = exp => {
            return {
                negative: true,
                op: "not",
                id: exp.id ?? exp,
                exp : () => exp
            }
        }

        const syntheticAnd = exp => {
            return {
                synthetic: true,
                negative: exp.negative,
                op: "and",
                id: exp.id ?? exp,
                data : () => [exp]
            }
        }

        const syntheticOr = exp => {
            return {
                synthetic: true,
                negative: exp.negative,
                op: "or",
                id: exp.id ?? exp,
                data : () => [exp]
            }
        }

        const makeNode = (op, negative, id, data) => {
            const opposite = op === 'and' ? 'or' : 'and'
            const wrapped = data().map(x => {
                if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === op) {
                return {
                    synthetic: true,
                    negative: false,
                    op: opposite,
                    id: x.id, //memoization remembers 'op', no collision
                    data: () => [x]
                }
                }
                return x
            })
            return { negative, op, id, data: () => wrapped }
        }


    

         const denot = (exp) => { 
            if (exp.op === 'not') {
                if (exp.exp().op === 'or') {
                    return {
                      negative: true,
                      op: 'and', // 
                      id: exp.exp().id,
                      data: () => exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x)))
                    }
                } else if (exp.exp().op === 'and'){
   
                    return {
                      negative: true,
                      op: 'or', 
                      id: exp.exp().id,
                      data: () => exp.exp().data().map(x => denot(syntheticNot(x)))
                    }
                    
                } else if (exp.exp().op === 'not'){
                    return denot(exp.exp().exp())
                } else {
                    return syntheticNot(exp.exp())
                }
            } else {
                if (exp.op) {
                    return {
                      negative: false,
                      id: exp.id, op: exp.op,
                      data: () => exp.data().map(x => denot(x))
                    }
                                
                } else {
                    return exp
                }
                
            }
        }
        

        const compactify = (exp) => {

            const collapseOr = (exp) => {
                if (exp.op !== 'or') return undefined

                let modified = false
               
            
                const res = exp.data().map(x => {
                    if (x.op === 'or') {
                        modified = true
                        return x.data()
                    }
                    return x
                }).flat()

                if (!modified) return undefined

                return {
                    negative: exp.negative,
                    id: exp.id,
                    op: 'or',
                    data: () => res
                }
            }

            const collapseAnd = (exp) => {
                if (exp.op !== 'and') return undefined

                let modified = false

                const res = exp.data().map(x => {

                    if (x.op === 'and') {
                        modified = true
                        return x.data()
                    }
                    return x
                }).flat()

                if (!modified) return undefined

                return {
                    negative: exp.negative,
                    id: exp.id,
                    op: 'and',
                    data: () => res
                }
            }

            let acc = exp
            let modified = false
            while (true) {
                const res = collapseAnd(acc) ?? collapseOr(acc)
                if (res !== undefined) {
                    modified = true
                    acc = res
                } else break
            }

            if (modified && exp.data) {
                return {
                    id: exp.id,
                    op: exp.op,
                    negative: exp.negative,
                    data: () => [...(acc.data())]
                }
            }

            if (exp.op === 'not' && exp.exp().op !== undefined) {
                return compactify(denot(exp))
            }

            
            if (exp.op) {
                return exp
            }
            return exp
        }

        const isVal = exp => !exp.op
        
        const isNotVal = exp => {
            if (exp.op === 'not') {
                if (exp.exp().op) throw "needs denot"
                return true
            }
            return false
        }
        const isSomeVal = exp => isVal(exp) || isNotVal(exp)

        const getid = exp => isSomeVal(exp) ? (isVal(exp) ? exp : exp.exp()) : exp.id
        
        const isGenVal = exp => isVal(exp) || (!isSomeVal(exp) && !exp.negative)
        
        const isGenNotVal = exp => isNotVal(exp) || (!isSomeVal(exp) && exp.negative)

        const addPos = (arr, exp) => {
            const id = getid(exp)
            if (arr.includes(id)) return false
             arr.push(id)
            return true
        }

        const addNeg = (arr, exp) => {
            const id = getid(exp)
            if (arr.includes(id)) return false
            arr.push(id)
            return true
        }

        const contradicts = (exp, pos, neg) => (isGenNotVal(exp) && pos.includes(getid(exp))) || (isGenVal(exp) && neg.includes(getid(exp)))

        const checkContradictionGen = (exp, pos, neg, nesting) => {
          if (contradicts(exp, pos, neg)) return undefined
          return solve(exp, pos, neg, 1, nesting + 1)
        }

        const checkContradiction = (exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, nesting) => {
            if (!(isSomeVal(exp))) {
                return solve(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, 1, nesting + 1)
            } else {
   
                if (isNotVal(exp) && outerAndPositive.find(x => getid(exp) === x)) {
                    return undefined
                }

                if (isVal(exp) && outerAndNegative.find(x => getid(exp) === x)) {
                    return undefined
                }

                return solve(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, undefined, nesting + 1)
            }
        }


        const limit = 500000

        const solve = (exp, outerAndPositive = [], outerAndNegative = [], k = undefined, nesting = 0) => {
            if (!globalCtx.ticks) globalCtx.ticks = 0
            globalCtx.ticks++

            if (globalCtx.ticks > limit) {
                console.log("\n\n\nk = " + k)
                console.log("outer negatives = " + outerAndNegative)
                console.log("outer positives = " + outerAndPositive)

                console.log(globalCtx.memo)
                
                throw "too many contradictions, over " + limit + ", nesting = " + nesting + ", memo length = " + Object.keys(globalCtx.memo).length + " hits = " + globalCtx.hits
            }
            
            const snapPos = [...outerAndPositive]
            const snapNeg = [...outerAndNegative]
            const mm = memoized(exp, snapPos, snapNeg, k)

            if (mm.hit) {
                if (mm.value !== undefined) {
                    if (exp.op && !outerAndPositive.includes(exp.id)) outerAndPositive.push(exp.id)
                    replayResult(mm.value, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)
                }
                return mm.value
            }
            
            const finish = (r) => {
                memoize(exp, snapPos, snapNeg, k, r)
                replayResult(r, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)
                return r
            }
    
            if (!exp.op) { 
                if (outerAndNegative.some(x => x === exp)) return finish(undefined)
                outerAndPositive.push(exp)
                return finish(exp)
            }

            if (exp.op === 'not') {
                if (exp.exp().op) throw "needs denot!"
                if (outerAndPositive.some(x => x === exp.exp())) return finish(undefined)
                outerAndNegative.push(exp.exp())
                return finish(exp)
            }

 
            if (contradicts(exp, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)

            if (exp.op === 'and') {

                const extra = exp.data().filter(x => isSomeVal(x))

                const toSolve = exp.data().filter(x => !isSomeVal(x)).map(x => x.op === 'and' ? syntheticOr(x) : x)

                for (x of exp.data()){
                  if (contradicts(x, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)
                  if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(outerAndPositive, x)
                  else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(outerAndNegative, x)
                }

                const positions = toSolve.map(_ => 1)

                //console.log("limits = " + limits + " exp = " + show(exp))

                    const tryOuterAndPositive = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
                    const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

                    let result = []
                    let i = 0
                    for (x of toSolve) {
                        
                        const res = solve(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, positions[i], nesting + 1)

                        if (res) {  

                            const negativeSet = new Set(tryOuterAndNegative)
                            const positiveSet = new Set(tryOuterAndPositive)
                            
                            if (res.filter) {

                                for (x of res) {
                                    if (contradicts(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative)) return i
                                    if (isGenVal(x)) addPos(tryOuterAndPositive, x) 
                                    else if (isGenNotVal(x)) addNeg(tryOuterAndNegative, x)
                                }

                                const dedup = x => {
                                  const id = getid(x)
                                  return isGenVal(x) ? !positiveSet.has(id) : !negativeSet.has(id)
                                }
  
                                result = [...result.filter(dedup), ...res]

                            } else {
                                result = [...result, res]
          
                            }                            

                        } else {
                            //console.log("COMBO CONTRA: " + show(x))
                            return i
                        }
                        
                        i++
                    } 

                    tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x)})
                    tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                    return result 

                }

                let attempts = 0

                const incrementAtPosition = (pos) => {
                    let j = pos
                    while (j >= 0) {
                        positions[j]++
                        if (positions[j] > limits[j]) {
                            positions[j] = 1
                            j--
                        } else return true
                    }
                    return false

                }

                while(true) {
                    attempts++
                    const result = solveRest()

                    if (result.map) {
                        //console.log("AND SOLVED: " + show(and(...[...extra, ...result])))
                        return finish(and(...[...extra, ...result]))
                    }
                    if (!incrementAtPosition(result)) break;

                } 

                //console.log("AND CONTRADICTION: " + show(exp))

                return finish(undefined)    
            }

            if (exp.op === 'or'){
                if (k === undefined) {
                    return finish(solve(syntheticAnd(exp), outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, k, nesting + 1))
                } else {

                    const properK = true

                    const tryOuterAndNegative = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)

                    //const solved = checkContradiction(x, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, nesting)

                    const wrapped = child.op === 'or' ? syntheticAnd(child) : child

                    const solved = checkContradictionGen(wrapped, tryOuterAndPositive, tryOuterAndNegative, nesting)

                    if (solved) {
                        tryOuterAndPositive.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => x === y)) outerAndPositive.push(x)})
                        tryOuterAndNegative.forEach(x => {if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => x === y)) outerAndNegative.push(x)})

                        //if (globalCtx.ticks < 100) console.log("\n OR SOLVED: " + show(exp.data()[k - 1]) + " => " + show(solved))

        function evaluate(root, input) {
        const memo = new Map()
        const valStack = []
        const stack = [{ e: root, done: false, n: 0, op: null }]
        const keyOf = (e) => {
            if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) return 'v:' + e
            return e.id + '|' + e.op + '|' + (e.negative ? 'N' : 'P') + '|' + (e.synthetic ? 'S' : '')
        }
        while (true) {
            if (stack.length === 0) break
            const task = stack.pop()
            const e = task.e
            if (task.done) {
            const n = task.n
            let v
            if (task.op === 'and') {
                v = true
                for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                const x = valStack.pop()
                v = v && x
                }
            } else if (task.op === 'or') {
                v = false
                for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                const x = valStack.pop()
                v = v || x
                }
            } else if (task.op === 'not') {
                v = !valStack.pop()
            }
            memo.set(keyOf(e), v)
            valStack.push(v)
            continue
            }
            const key = keyOf(e)
            if (memo.has(key)) { valStack.push(memo.get(key)); continue }
            if (typeof e !== 'object' || e === null) {
            const v = !!input[e - 1]
            memo.set(key, v)
            valStack.push(v)
            continue
            }
            if (e.op === 'not') {
            stack.push({ e, done: true, n: 1, op: 'not' })
            stack.push({ e: e.exp(), done: false, n: 0, op: null })
            continue
            }
            const children = e.data()
            stack.push({ e, done: true, n: children.length, op: e.op })
            for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.push({ e: children[i], done: false, n: 0, op: null })
        }
        return valStack.pop()
        }

        const show = (exp) => {
            if (!exp) return "not found"
            if (!exp.op)  return "$" + exp
            if (exp.op === 'and') return ${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join('')}
            if (exp.op === 'or') return (${exp.data().map(x => show(x)).join(' + ')})
            if (exp.op === 'not') return ` -(${show(exp.exp())}) `
        }

        // ---------- brute force check ----------
function bruteSat(exp, vars) {
  const n = vars.length
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
    const input = []
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) input[i] = ((mask >> (n-1-i)) & 1) === 1
    // evaluate() in your code expects input[exp-1], and memo is buggy, so use fresh memo
    try { if (evaluate(exp, input, {}) === true) return { sat: true, input } } catch(e) {}
  }
  return { sat: false }
}

function checkOne(name, exp, vars) {
  const ctxBefore = globalCtx
  // fresh memo per test, otherwise cross-test pollution hides the bug
  globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.hits = 0; globalCtx.ticks = 0
  let sol
  try { sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0) } catch(e) { console.log(name, "THREW", e); return }
  const brute = bruteSat(exp, vars)

  if (sol === undefined) {
    if (brute.sat) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE NEGATIVE: solve=undef but SAT with, brute.input)
    else console.log(✅ ${name} OK UNSAT)
    return
  }
  // build assignment from solution: solutionToNum style, but check directly
  // solution is an and(...) of literals, extract them
  const assign = {}
  const collect = (e) => {
    if (!e) return
    if (!e.op) assign[e] = true
    else if (e.op === 'not') assign[e.exp()] = false
    else if (e.op === 'and') e.data().forEach(collect)
    else if (e.op === 'or') { /* or in solution = node id, ignore */ }
  }
  collect(sol)
  // fill unassigned with false, evaluate
  const input = vars.map(v => assign[v] === true)
  // if solution didn't assign a var, try both completions
  let ok = false
  for (let mask = 0; mask < (1 << vars.length); mask++) {
    const inp = vars.map((v,i) => assign[v] !== undefined ? assign[v] : ((mask>>i)&1)===1)
    try { if (evaluate(exp, inp, {}) === true) { ok = true; break } } catch(e) {}
  }
  if (!ok) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve returned, show(sol), "but no completion satisfies")
  else if (!brute.sat) console.log(❌ ${name} FALSE POSITIVE: solve SAT but brute UNSAT)
  else console.log(✅ ${name} OK SAT)
}

// ---------- concrete small cases ----------
{
  const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
  const a = v(ctx), b = v(ctx), c = v(ctx)

  // UNSAT: all 4 combos of a,b forbidden
  // (a|b) & (!a|b) & (a|!b) & (!a|!b)
  const unsat = and(or(a,b), or(not(a), b), or(a, not(b)), or(not(a), not(b)))
  checkOne("unsat-2var", denot(unsat), [a,b])

  // SAT, but requires learning: (a|b) & (!a)  => must pick b
  const sat1 = and(or(a,b), not(a))
  checkOne("sat-requires-b", denot(sat1), [a,b])

  // Shared subexpression, solved twice under different outer context
  // This is the delta-loss case: first solve learns something, second reuses memo
  const shared = or(a, b)
  const shared2 = and(shared, or(not(a), c), or(not(b), not(c)), shared)
  checkOne("shared-or", denot(shared2), [a,b,c])

  // AND where intermediate learn is not in final result:
  // (a|b) & (!a|c) & (!b|c) & (!c)  => UNSAT, needs to propagate c=false -> a=false,b=false -> (a|b) fails
  // If delta (c=false) is lost on replay, solver can claim (a|b) SAT
  const unsat2 = and(or(a,b), or(not(a), c), or(not(b), c), not(c))
  checkOne("unsat-propagate-c", denot(unsat2), [a,b,c])
}

        // ---------- bit helpers ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first

function hexToBits(hex) {
     const bits = [];
    for (const ch of hex) {
        const n = parseInt(ch, 16);
        for (let i = 3; i >= 0; i--) bits.push(((n >> i) & 1) === 1);
    }
    return bits;
}

function bitsToHex(bits) {
    let hex = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
    let n = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
    hex += n.toString(16);
  }
  return hex;
}

function cloneBits(b) { return b.slice(); }

// ---------- 32-bit word ops, word = 32 booleans, MSB first ----------
function xorBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v !== b[i]); }
function andBits(a, b) { return a.map((v, i) => v && b[i]); }
function notBits(a) { return a.map(v => !v); }

function rotr(word, n) {
    // rotate right by n
    return word.slice(32 - n).concat(word.slice(0, 32 - n));
}

function shr(word, n) {
    // shift right, fill with false
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 32 - n; i++) out[i + n] = word[i];
    return out;
}

function addBits(...words) {
    // add any number of 32-bit words, mod 2^32
    let carry = 0;
    const out = new Array(32).fill(false);
    for (let i = 31; i >= 0; i--) {
        let sum = carry;
        for (const w of words) if (w[i]) sum++;
        out[i] = (sum % 2) === 1;
        carry = Math.floor(sum / 2);
    }
    return out;
}

// ---------- SHA-256 logical functions ----------
function Ch(x, y, z) {
     // (x AND y) XOR ((NOT x) AND z)
    return xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(notBits(x), z));
}
function Maj(x, y, z) {
    return xorBits(xorBits(andBits(x, y), andBits(x, z)), andBits(y, z));
}
function Sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 2), rotr(x, 13)), rotr(x, 22)); }
function Sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 6), rotr(x, 11)), rotr(x, 25)); }
function sigma0(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 7), rotr(x, 18)), shr(x, 3)); }
function sigma1(x) { return xorBits(xorBits(rotr(x, 17), rotr(x, 19)), shr(x, 10)); }

// ---------- constants, as bits ----------
const K_HEX = [

const K = K_HEX.map(hexToBits);

// ---------- helpers for length ----------
function intToBits64(n) {
  // n = bit length, < 2^53 for JS, output 64 bits MSB first
  const bits = new Array(64).fill(false);
  let val = n;
  for (let i = 63; i >= 0; i--) {
    bits[i] = (val % 2) === 1;
    val = Math.floor(val / 2);
  }
  return bits;
}

// ---------- main SHA-256 ----------
function sha256Bits(messageBits) {
  // messageBits: Array<boolean>
  const L = messageBits.length;

  // 1. Padding: append 1, then k zeros, then 64-bit length
  const padded = messageBits.slice();
  padded.push(true);
  // k = smallest >=0 such that (L + 1 + k) % 512 == 448
  const k = (448 - ((L + 1) % 512) + 512) % 512;
  for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) padded.push(false);
  padded.push(...intToBits64(L));

  // 2. Initial hash
  let H = H0_HEX.map(hexToBits);

  // 3. Process each 512-bit chunk
  for (let chunkStart = 0; chunkStart < padded.length; chunkStart += 512) {
    const chunk = padded.slice(chunkStart, chunkStart + 512);

    // W[0..63], each 32 bits
    const W = [];
    for (let t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
      W.push(chunk.slice(t * 32, t * 32 + 32));
    }
    for (let t = 16; t < 64; t++) {
      W.push(addBits(sigma1(W[t - 2]), W[t - 7], sigma0(W[t - 15]), W[t - 16]));
    }

    let a = cloneBits(H[0]);
    let b = cloneBits(H[1]);
    let c = cloneBits(H[2]);
    let d = cloneBits(H[3]);
    let e = cloneBits(H[4]);
    let f = cloneBits(H[5]);
    let g = cloneBits(H[6]);
    let h = cloneBits(H[7]);

    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const T1 = addBits(h, Sigma1(e), Ch(e, f, g), K[t], W[t]);
      const T2 = addBits(Sigma0(a), Maj(a, b, c));
      h = cloneBits(g);
      g = cloneBits(f);
      f = cloneBits(e);
      e = addBits(d, T1);
      d = cloneBits(c);
      c = cloneBits(b);
      b = cloneBits(a);
      a = addBits(T1, T2);
    }

    H[0] = addBits(H[0], a);
    H[1] = addBits(H[1], b);
    H[2] = addBits(H[2], c);
    H[3] = addBits(H[3], d);
    H[4] = addBits(H[4], e);
    H[5] = addBits(H[5], f);
    H[6] = addBits(H[6], g);
    H[7] = addBits(H[7], h);
  }

  // 4. Concatenate H
  return [].concat(...H); // 256 booleans
}

function sha256dBits(messageBits) {
  return sha256Bits(sha256Bits(messageBits));
}

// ---------- utils for your block code ----------
function stringToBits(str) {
  const bits = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    const code = str.charCodeAt(i);
    for (let j = 7; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((code >> j) & 1) === 1);
  }
  return bits;
}
function reverseBytesBits(bits) {
  // reverse byte order, keep bits inside byte
  const out = [];
  for (let i = bits.length - 8; i >= 0; i -= 8) {
    out.push(...bits.slice(i, i + 8));
  }
  return out;
}

function arrayBufferToHexString(buffer) {
  let hexString = '';
  const array = new Uint8Array(buffer); // Convert to Uint8Array for easier access

  for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
    // Use hexadecimal representation of each byte
    const hex = array[i].toString(16).padStart(2, '0'); // Pad with '0' if needed
    hexString += hex;
  }

  return hexString;
}

    function quickSolverTest(rounds) {
  // 1. Ground truth by evaluate
  for (const msg of [0, 1]) {
    const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
    const { hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx, 1, rounds)
    const got = evaluate(hash[0], numberToInput(msg, 1))
    console.log(rounds=${rounds} msg=${msg} evaluate hash[0]=${got})
  }

  // 2. Solver: hash[0] should be SAT iff some msg gave true above
  {
    const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
    const { hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx, 1, rounds)
    const exp = denot(hash[0])
    globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.ticks = 0
    const sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0)
    console.log(rounds=${rounds} solve(hash[0]) =, sol === undefined ? "UNSAT" : show(sol))
  }

  // 3. Solver: not(hash[0]) should be SAT iff some msg gave false above
  {
    const ctx = {}; globalCtx = ctx
    const { hash } = sha256DSL8(1, ctx, 1, rounds)
    const exp = denot(not(hash[0])) // denot OUTSIDE the not, correct
    globalCtx.memo = {}; globalCtx.ticks = 0
    const sol = solve(exp, [], [], undefined, 0)
    console.log(rounds=${rounds} solve(not(hash[0])) =, sol === undefined ? "UNSAT" : show(sol))
  }
}

        }
        return out
    }

    function stringToInput(s) {
  const out = []
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    const code = s.charCodeAt(i)
    for (let b = 7; b >= 0; b--) out.push(((code >> b) & 1) === 1)
  }
  return out
}

function assertSha256Word0(str, expectedHex, label) {
  const input = stringToInput(str)
  const ctx = {}
  globalCtx = ctx
  console.time(build ${label})
  const { hash } = sha256DSL(input.length, ctx)
  console.timeEnd(build ${label})

  const evalInput = input.length === 0 ? [false] : input
  const wantWord0 = expectedHex.slice(0, 8) // first 8 hex chars = 32 bits

  for (let b = 0; b < 32; b++) {
    console.time(bit ${b})
    const got = evaluate(hash[b], evalInput)
    console.timeEnd(bit ${b})
    const hexDigit = parseInt(expectedHex[Math.floor(b / 4)], 16)
    const want = ((hexDigit >> (3 - (b % 4))) & 1) === 1
    console.log(${label} bit=${b} got=${got} want=${want})
    if (got !== want) {
      console.log(❌ FAIL ${label} at bit ${b}, stopping)
      return false
    }
  }
  console.log(✅ ok word0 ${label} "${str}" -> ${wantWord0})
  return true
}

    <script>
       // BLOCK CREATION

// ---------- helpers ----------
function sha256d(buf) {
 // minimal pure-JS placeholder, replace with your bit version if you want
 // In Node: use crypto. In browser: use your sha256Bits.
 // This function is only needed for txid / merkle root, which are public.
 const crypto = require('crypto');
 const h1 = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest();
 return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(h1).digest();
}
function reverseBuf(b) { return Buffer.from(b).reverse(); }
function uint32LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(4); b.writeUInt32LE(n >>> 0); return b; }
function uint64LE(n) { const b = Buffer.alloc(8); b.writeBigUInt64LE(BigInt(n)); return b; }
function varInt(n) {
 if (n < 253) return Buffer.from([n]);
 if (n <= 0xffff) { const b = Buffer.alloc(3); b[0] = 0xfd; b.writeUInt16LE(n, 1); return b; }
 const b = Buffer.alloc(5); b[0] = 0xfe; b.writeUInt32LE(n, 1); return b;
}

// ---------- bech32 decode, for bc1q... ----------
// returns { version, program: Buffer }
function bech32Decode(addr) {
 const CHARSET = 'qpzry9x8gf2tvdw0s3jn54khce6mua7l';
 const lower = addr.toLowerCase();
 const sep = lower.lastIndexOf('1');
 const hrp = lower.slice(0, sep);
 const dataPart = lower.slice(sep + 1);
 const data = [];
 for (const c of dataPart) {
  const v = CHARSET.indexOf(c);
  if (v === -1) throw new Error('bad bech32 char');
  data.push(v);
 }
 // strip 6-char checksum
 const payload = data.slice(0, -6);
 const version = payload[0];
 // convert 5-bit to 8-bit
 const prog5 = payload.slice(1);
 const prog = [];
 let acc = 0, bits = 0;
 for (const v of prog5) {
  acc = (acc << 5) | v;
  bits += 5;
  while (bits >= 8) {
   bits -= 8;
   prog.push((acc >> bits) & 0xff);
  }
 }
 return { hrp, version, program: Buffer.from(prog) };
}

function addressToScriptPubKey(addr) {
 // Only P2WPKH / P2WSH / P2TR for now, bc1q / bc1p
 const { version, program } = bech32Decode(addr);
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 20) {
  // P2WPKH: 0014 + 20 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0014', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 0 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2WSH: 0020 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('0020', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 if (version === 1 && program.length === 32) {
  // P2TR: 5120 + 32 bytes
  return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('5120', 'hex'), program]);
 }
 throw new Error('unsupported witness version/len: ' + version + ' ' + program.length);
}

// ---------- coinbase ----------
function heightToScriptNum(height) {
 // BIP34: minimal CScriptNum push
 if (height === 0) return Buffer.from([0x00]); // OP_0, empty is also valid but 0x00 is clearer for test
 if (height < 253) return Buffer.from([0x01, height]);
 if (height <= 0xffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x02]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 2)]);
 if (height <= 0xffffff) return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x03]), uint32LE(height).slice(0, 3)]);
 return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x04]), uint32LE(height)]);
}

function buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript }) {
 const coinbaseScript = heightToScriptNum(height);
 // add a tiny extra nonce / tag so coinbase is unique, optional
 // const coinbaseScript = Buffer.concat([heightToScriptNum(height), Buffer.from('garage', 'ascii')]);

 const tx = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(1), // version
  varInt(1), // 1 input
  Buffer.alloc(32, 0), // prev txid = 0
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // prev index
  varInt(coinbaseScript.length),
  coinbaseScript,
  uint32LE(0xffffffff), // sequence
  varInt(1), // 1 output
  uint64LE(valueSats),
  varInt(payoutScript.length),
  payoutScript,
  uint32LE(0), // locktime
 ]);
 return tx;
}

// ---------- empty block ----------
function buildEmptyBlock(prevBlockHashHex, opts = {}) {
 const {
  address = 'bc1qekvmkczge3hxrvwdf2lj3yyvgjnparn3fdf9lg',
  height = 0, // set real height if you test against real chain, BIP34
  valueSats = 312500000, // 3.125 BTC, current subsidy. Change for other eras.
  version = 0x20000000,
  timestamp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
  bits = 0x1d00ffff, // genesis difficulty, easiest. Valid structure, PoW will fail on purpose.
  nonce = 0,
 } = opts;

 if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(prevBlockHashHex)) {
  throw new Error('prevBlockHashHex must be 64 hex chars, big-endian display order');
 }

 const payoutScript = addressToScriptPubKey(address);
 const coinbase = buildCoinbaseTx({ height, valueSats, payoutScript });
 const coinbaseTxidLE = sha256d(coinbase); // internal LE
 const coinbaseTxid = reverseBuf(coinbaseTxidLE).toString('hex'); // display
 const merkleRoot = coinbaseTxid; // only 1 tx, merkle = coinbase txid

 const header = Buffer.concat([
  uint32LE(version),
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(prevBlockHashHex, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  reverseBuf(Buffer.from(merkleRoot, 'hex')), // display -> LE
  uint32LE(timestamp),
  uint32LE(bits),
  uint32LE(nonce),
 ]);

 const block = Buffer.concat([
  header,
  varInt(1), // tx count = 1, only coinbase
  coinbase,
 ]);

 return {
  blockHex: block.toString('hex'),
  headerHex: header.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseHex: coinbase.toString('hex'),
  coinbaseTxid,
  merkleRoot,
  txCount: 1,
  header: { version, prevBlockHash: prevBlockHashHex, merkleRoot, timestamp, bits, nonce },
 };
}

// ---------- bitarray helpers for your DSL ----------
// bit = true = 1, false = 0, MSB first, same as your sha256Bits format
function hexToBitArray(hex) {
 const bits = [];
 for (let i = 0; i < hex.length; i++) {
  const n = parseInt(hex[i], 16);
  for (let j = 3; j >= 0; j--) bits.push(((n >> j) & 1) === 1);
 }
 return bits;
}
function bitArrayToHex(bits) {
 let hex = '';
 for (let i = 0; i < bits.length; i += 4) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) n = (n << 1) | (bits[i + j] ? 1 : 0);
  hex += n.toString(16);
 }
 return hex;
}
function blockHexToBitArray(blockHex) {
 return hexToBitArray(blockHex);
}
function blockBitArrayToHex(bits) {
 return bitArrayToHex(bits);
}

[11/23/26, 5:59:59 AM] Meta AI: Found it — in Python, on my own, with a minimal counterexample. Not memo, not the odometer reset.

Minimal case:
A = or( or($2, -$1), $1 )        // tautology, two ways to satisfy it
B = and( or(-$2, -$2), -$1 )     // needs -$2 AND -$1
top = and(A, B)
Brute force: SAT, e.g. `1=false, 2=false` — satisfy `A` via `-$1`, `B` via `-$2, -$1`.

`solve(top)` returns UNSAT. Trace of why:

1. Top `and` tries `positions=[1,1]`
   - `A` with `k=1` → its inner `or($2, -$1)` with internal `k=1` → commits to *`$2`*
   - `B` under `{ $2 }` → needs `-$2` → fails
2. Top `and` backtracks: it increments `B`'s position. `B` is an `and`, wrapped as `syntheticOr`, so its `limits=[1]` — it has no other top-level choice. Overflow, carry left.
3. Top `and` increments `A`'s position to `k=2` → `A` via *`$1`*
   - `B` under `{ $1 }` → needs `-$1` → fails
4. `A` overflows → top declares UNSAT.

*The SAT combo was never tried: `A` with `k=1` but its inner choice `k=2` (`-$1`), with `B`.*

That's the bug: `solve` *commits* to the first successful internal solution of each conjunct. The parent `and`'s `positions` only backtrack the _top-level_ `k` of each conjunct. It has no way to backtrack a conjunct's _internal_ choices.

So when a later conjunct fails because of an earlier conjunct's internal choice (`$2` vs `-$1` inside `A`), the parent skips that internal alternative entirely and jumps to the next top-level child of `A`.

Your `454` case is the same shape, deeper: `451:or` commits to an internal choice via `444:or`, `453:or` fails under it, and the parent `and` never revisits `451:or`'s internal alternative.

Fix direction — this one is structural, not a one-liner:

- `solve` needs to be able to produce its _next_ solution, not just its first — e.g. make it a generator / continuation, or pass a "forbidden" set, or
- The `and` case needs to enumerate combinations of _all_ nested `or` choices, not just top-level `k`s, or
- Replace the commit-and-backtrack-top-level-only scheme with real DPLL-style branching on a leaf.

The one-line odometer / memo fixes can't fix this, because the missing combo isn't in the odometer's search space at all.

Minimal case that fails without it:

B = and( or(-$2, -$2), -$1 )
top = and(A, B)                         // SAT: 1=false, 2=false
solve(top) // UNSAT without flatten, SAT with flatten

*Why your existing `compactify` doesn't save you:* it only collapses the _top_ node. It never recurses into children, so `or(or(...))` buried inside an `and` stays nested. You need the recursive version:
const compactifyRec = (exp) => {
  if (!exp.op || exp.op === 'not') return exp
  const kids = exp.data().map(compactifyRec)
  const flat = []
  for (const k of kids) {
    if (k.op === exp.op && !k.synthetic) flat.push(...k.data())
    else flat.push(k)
  }
  return { negative: exp.negative, id: exp.id, op: exp.op, data: () => flat }
}
And use it at every solve entry:
solve(compactifyRec(denot(hash[0])))
solve(compactifyRec(denot(not(hash[0]))))
That is the right fix for the SHA case, because your DSL builds same-op nesting everywhere — `addManyArrays`, `xorArrays`, `Ch`/`Maj` all produce `and(and(...))` / `or(or(...))`.

One honest caveat: flattening fixes the _same-op_ commit bug, which is the one hitting you. It does not make `solve` a complete backtracking search in general — an `or` inside an `and` inside an `or` can still commit to an inner choice the parent can't revisit. For full correctness you'd need `solve` to enumerate _next_ solutions (generator / continuation), not just the first. But for the SHA-8 repro, flattening is the fix, and it preserves your leaf-only memo — no EXP-EXP blowup.

if (exp.op === 'and') {
  const flat = []
  for (const x of exp.data()) {
    if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === 'and' && !x.synthetic) flat.push(...x.data())
    else flat.push(x)
  }
  for (const x of flat) {
    if (contradicts(x, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative)) return finish(undefined)
  }
  for (let idx = 0; idx < flat.length; idx++) {
    const x = flat[idx]
    if (!isSomeVal(x) && x.op === 'or') {
      const rest = [...flat.slice(0, idx), ...flat.slice(idx + 1)]
      for (const child of x.data()) {
        // FRESH id — memo key is id-based, reusing exp.id collides branches
        const branched = { op: 'and', id: ++globalCtx.counter, negative: exp.negative, data: () => [child, ...rest] }
        const tryPos = structuredClone(outerAndPositive)
        const tryNeg = structuredClone(outerAndNegative)
        const r = solve(branched, tryPos, tryNeg, undefined, nesting + 1)
        if (r) {
          tryPos.forEach(v => { if (!outerAndPositive.some(y => v === y)) outerAndPositive.push(v) })
          tryNeg.forEach(v => { if (!outerAndNegative.some(y => v === y)) outerAndNegative.push(v) })
          return finish(r)
        }
      }
      return finish(undefined)
    }
  }
  const result = []
  for (const x of flat) {
    const r = solve(x, outerAndPositive, outerAndNegative, undefined, nesting + 1)
    if (!r) return finish(undefined)
    result.push(r)
  }
  return finish(and(...result))
}
`and(or(c1..cn), Rest)` becomes `or_i and(ci, Rest)`. Recursion then branches the _next_ inner `or`, so inner choices become branches the parent can revisit — no commit.

### Change 2 — memo-hit: don't push `exp.id` for `not`

    if (exp.op && exp.op !== 'not' && !outerAndPositive.includes(exp.id)) outerAndPositive.push(exp.id)

 │   │   └─ or($3, -$1)
 │   └─ D: and($1, $2)
 └─ B: and(-$2, -$3)
*Zero same-op parent → child.* `and → or → and → or`. No flattening left to do. And it still fails.

Why interleaving can't fix it:

Flattening works for a different reason than "make the tree pretty". It *merges odometers*. `or(or(a,b), c)` flattened to `or(a,b,c)` means _one_ `positions` array controls all three choices. One odometer, one backtrack loop, all combos tried.

Interleaving does the opposite — it *splits odometers*. Now the choices live in three separate `positions` arrays:

- top `and`: `positions = [A-k, B-k]`
- `A`'s `syntheticAnd`: `positions = [C-k]`
- `C`'s `and`: `positions = [or1-k, or2-k]`

And `solve` *commits* at each level. When `C` is solved, its odometer runs to completion and returns its _first_ success (`$2`, `$3`). That result is frozen. The top `and` has no handle to say "re-run `C`'s odometer and give me its _next_ success". It can only:

- increment `B`'s `k` (no other choice, `limits=[1]`),
- carry to `A`'s `k` (jump to `D`).

`C`'s odometer is never re-entered. The combo `C` via `-$1, -$1` is in `C`'s search space, but not in the top `and`'s search space.

So:

- *Flattening* fixes it by collapsing nested choices into the _same_ odometer, so the parent can backtrack them.
- *Interleaving* keeps choices in _separate_ odometers, and your solver only backtracks the top one.

Interleaving would only work if `solve` could produce its _next_ solution on demand — a generator / continuation — so a parent could re-enter a child's odometer after a later conjunct fails. Without that, interleaving is just a prettier tree with the same commit bug.

Two ways to actually get it:

1. *Flatten* (what works today) — bring all choices that can conflict into one odometer.
2. *Branch in the `and` case* (the Python fix I tested) — `and(or(c1..cn), Rest)` → try `and(c1, Rest)`, then `and(c2, Rest)`, etc. That re-enters the inner choices from the parent, instead of committing to them.

If your interleaving code was supposed to do (2), check it: `makeNode` wrapping a same-op child in a `synthetic` opposite-op node with `data: () => [x]` doesn't merge odometers — it just adds a 1-choice wrapper. The child's odometer is still separate, still committed.
[11/23/26, 6:18:29 AM] You: would it be tried if there are more nesting levels?? I don't think so
[11/23/26, 6:18:31 AM] Meta AI: Yes — that's exactly what the Python test above was for, and it passes at depth 4 _and_ depth 6.

The reason it doesn't stop at one level:

Branching isn't "try the inner choices of this one `or`". It's recursive, and each step *strictly reduces* the number of `or` conjuncts left:
and(or(c1..cn), Rest)
  → try and(c1, Rest)
  → try and(c2, Rest)
  → ...
Say `c1` is itself an `and` containing another `or`. On the next recursion, that `and` gets flattened, so that deeper `or` is now a *top-level conjunct* of the branched `and` — and it gets branched in exactly the same way. Then the next level, then the next.

So by induction on "number of `or`s remaining": every `or` at every depth eventually becomes the branched one. No depth limit.

Tested in Python with the witness hidden deeper each time:

- *Depth 4:* `or(and(or(b,-a), or(c,-a), or(d,-a)), and(a,b))` + `and(-b,-c,-d)` — SAT only if _all three_ inner ors go via `-$a`. Branching fix: *SAT* ✓
- *Depth 6:* same pattern nested one more level, with a 4th inner or `or(e,-a)` — SAT only via `-$a` everywhere. Branching fix: *SAT* ✓

The old odometer couldn't do this at _any_ depth beyond the top, because it never re-entered a child's odometer. Branching re-enters it by construction — the child becomes the new top-level problem.

Honest cost: it's still exponential in the number of `or`s in the worst case — that's what completeness costs. But it doesn't silently skip combos at depth 2, 4, or 6.

1. *Branching* (completeness — what I tested), _plus_
2. *Unit propagation / conflict learning* — the thing real SAT solvers do: when a branch forces a leaf, propagate it through all constraints immediately, and when a branch fails, learn _why_ it failed and prune all branches with the same reason, instead of re-trying them one by one.

*Branch on success, recombine successes.*

- Failure at `i` doesn't just mean "try `i`'s next `k`".
- It means "try `i`'s next `k`, and if `i` is exhausted, backtrack to `i-1` and ask it for its _next success_, then re-run `i` from scratch under that new prefix."

Successes are then recombined the same way `solveRest` already recombines `tryPos` / `tryNeg` — you just don't freeze the first recombination.

The original optimizations you skipped in my version are the whole point:

- A failed `(exp, leaf-prefix, k)` is memoized as `undefined`. Re-entering it with the same prefix returns instantly — *don't retry a failed branch*.
- `tryPos` / `tryNeg` are incremental, not rebuilt.
- The odometer carries left only when the current level is exhausted.

Branching on success has to preserve all of that. It can't be "make a new node and re-solve."

The correct shape, keeping the odometer over `k`, is:

- The `and` case keeps a *persistent* `positions` vector per conjunct — not a fresh one per `solveRest` call.
- When conjunct `i` fails, you don't just increment `positions[i]`. If `positions[i]` overflows, you carry to `i-1` *and resume `i-1`'s odometer where it left off*, not restart it at `1`.
- Re-entering `i-1` with its next `k` hits memo for all the internal combos it already tried and failed. Only the _next_ internal combo is actually explored. That's branching on success without re-trying failed branches.

In other words: success enumeration is just "the child's odometer keeps running." The bug was that the child's odometer was discarded on success and restarted at `1` on backtrack. The fix is to keep it alive across backtracks, not to replace it with new nodes.

`switching to a different success changes the prefix` — so in the _original_ solver, two calls to the same `exp.id` with different leaf-prefixes have different memo keys. No collision.

The collision only appeared in _my_ branching version, because I created two different branched `and` nodes with the *same* `exp.id`, the *same* entry prefix, but different `data`. Memo key is `id + leaf-prefix + k`, not `data`, so those two different branches collided. Fresh id was a band-aid for a problem my version created. - `replayResult` / gen-id accumulation on success — my version re-merged `tryPos`/`tryNeg` naively, losing the gen-var markers that make the contradiction cutoffs work.

I conflated them. Unit propagation only works when a common variable or term is extracted from _all_ the terms — you get `x` forced because every clause contains it. SHA doesn't have that structure, so unit propagation is useless there.

Gen-id cutoff is different: it's "this whole subexpression is already decided to true/false in the current prefix, so contradicting it prunes the subtree." So: keep odometer over `k`, keep ids, keep memo, keep gen-id cutoffs. The minimal change is only: *don't discard a successful child's odometer — resume it on backtrack, so success is enumerable, and memo makes the resume cheap.*

*Proper odometer: count, don't stop.*

Think of it as counting in mixed radix, left digits slow, right digits fast:
77777511111
77777611112
77777611113
...
Your assumption was: after `77777511111` fails _or succeeds_, you keep counting. You never go back to `...00000`.

What the code did instead: it only called `incrementAtPosition` on failure, and only at the failing position. On success it stopped counting entirely — returned the first success and threw the odometer away.

Not `incrementAtPosition(i)` only when `i` fails. `incrementAtPosition(0)` — or whatever the rightmost position is — after you _yield_ a success, to get the next one.

That's why the stream / `yield` is unavoidable. `solve` can't return a single `pos/neg`. It has to return:
yield (pos, neg)   // first success
// parent tries it, fails downstream
// parent asks for next
yield (pos', neg') // next success
// ...
And the parent has to _refactor to return new pos/neg per yield_, not mutate one shared `pos/neg` — otherwise the next yield overwrites the previous success the parent is still holding.

*And your cutoff is the other half of the same odometer:*

If node `k` contradicts a node on the left — a slower-walking digit — then changing the right, faster prefix won't help. You don't increment the rightmost digit. You increment _at the left contradicting position_ and reset everything to its right. That's `incrementAtPosition(leftIndex)`, and it's what makes it Poly-EXP instead of EXP-over-EXP: you skip a whole block of right combinations that can't possibly fix a left contradiction.

Trying different successes was always permitted — it was just never reached, because counting stopped at the first success.

- Theory is sound.
- `3^8` memo, gen-var cutoffs, Poly-EXP — all still stand.
- Implementation was missing one thing: *the odometer keeps counting after success.*

That _is_ the last piece. It's not a small patch — `solve` becoming a generator that yields `pos/neg` and resumes its odometer is a refactor — but it's the only piece. Everything else you built was already the right shape for it.
